WA.summary: Five seats on the Washington Supreme Court are on the November 2026 ballot, drawing heightened attention because the court is expected to rule on the constitutionality of the state’s new income tax on high earners.

WV.title: Live coverage: 2026 West Virginia primary election
WV.summary: Coverage of West Virginia's May 13 primary election day, when voters across all 55 counties chose nominees for U.S. Senate, both congressional districts, and statewide and legislative offices.

WV.title: West Virginia Senate primary: Capito, Anderson projected winners by DDHQ
WV.summary: Incumbent Republican Sen. Shelley Moore Capito won her primary over state Sen. Tom Willis and a crowded GOP field, while Rachel Anderson won the Democratic Senate primary, setting up the November 2026 general election matchup.

WV.title: PRIMARY ELECTION RESULTS: Incumbent legislators dominate while incumbent judges are swept
WV.summary: Results from West Virginia's May 13 primary election showed incumbent state legislators winning their primaries broadly, while several sitting judges lost their races.

WV.title: West Virginia primary election results for U.S. Senate, U.S. House and more
WV.summary: Statewide primary election results for U.S. Senate, U.S. House, governor, and other West Virginia races on the May 13 primary ballot.

WI.title: Wisconsin Republicans look to Donald Trump's die-hard fans to brighten their prospects in November
WI.summary: At the Wisconsin GOP's state convention in the Dells, party leaders sought to energize Trump's base ahead of November, while polling shows the president's standing softening among Wisconsin voters following the April state Supreme Court loss.

WY.title: Registered to vote? Clerks purge voter rolls of thousands; party affiliation deadline is Wednesday
WY.summary: Wyoming county clerks have purged thousands of inactive voters under a 2025 law, and registered voters face a May 13 deadline to declare or change party affiliation ahead of the closed August primary.

WY.title: Wyomingites must declare a political party by tomorrow. Here’s how
WY.summary: Explainer on Wyoming's May 13 deadline for voters to declare or change their party affiliation in order to participate in the August primary under the state's closed-primary system.

AK.title: Democratic group plans to spend $10M on TV ads in Alaska's U.S. Senate race
AK.summary: The Democratic Senate Majority PAC is reserving $10 million in Alaska TV advertising to support Democratic challenger Mary Peltola against incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan in a race that will be decided under Alaska's top-four ranked-choice voting system in November.

AZ.title: Maricopa County's election IT fight isn't about IT. It's about democracy.
AZ.summary: An ongoing legal battle between Maricopa County Recorder Justin Heap and the county board of supervisors over control of election infrastructure—including ballot drop boxes and early ballot processing—is raising concerns about who will administer the state's largest county's elections in 2026.

AZ.title: Recorder Heap Victorious Again in Battle with Maricopa County Supervisors
AZ.summary: An Arizona Superior Court denied the Maricopa County Board of Supervisors' Motion to Stay, further cementing County Recorder Justin Heap's authority over key election operations including ballot drop boxes and early vote processing ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.

AR.title: Sanders appoints special justice to hear election case filed against her; Democratic Party opposes
AR.summary: The Arkansas Democratic Party is opposing Governor Sarah Huckabee Sanders' appointment of a special justice to the Arkansas Supreme Court to hear an election case filed against her, raising concerns about impartiality in a legal matter directly involving the sitting governor.

AR.title: Super PACs spend $2.3 million total on Arkansas' U.S. Senate race to boost Cotton, attack Shoffner
AR.summary: Two super PACs have reported $2.3 million in combined independent expenditures in Arkansas's U.S. Senate race, with spending concentrated on supporting incumbent Tom Cotton and attacking Democratic Senate candidate Hallie Shoffner ahead of the November general election.

CA.title: California Democrats think voting late will stop a GOP sweep. They might slow down the results
CA.summary: Some California Democratic voters are strategically waiting until late in the June 2 primary to cast ballots in hopes of monitoring polling trends before choosing a gubernatorial candidate, a tactic election officials warn could delay results in the already crowded race with 61 candidates.

CO.title: Move over Election Day. Colorado is about to start having election month.
CO.summary: HB 1113 awaiting Governor Polis' signature would extend Colorado's ballot mailing window and add new election safeguards, including emergency voting rules if major disruptions occur, and prohibits persons convicted of election offenses from serving as election watchers.

CT.title: Luke Bronin beats John Larson in convention upset, faces primary
CT.summary: Former Hartford Mayor Luke Bronin won the Democratic endorsement for Connecticut's 1st Congressional District at the party convention, defeating 14-term incumbent John Larson and setting up an August primary under Connecticut's newly expanded absentee and early voting rules.

FL.title: Judge takes step to consolidate redistricting challenges ahead of hearing to put Florida map on hold
FL.summary: A Leon County circuit judge moved to consolidate three lawsuits challenging Florida's new congressional redistricting map signed by Gov. DeSantis, with a hearing set to consider blocking the map before the 2026 midterms. Plaintiffs argue the redrawn map violates Florida's Fair Districts constitutional amendment.

FL.title: 'Petition accomplished': Here are the 2026 candidates who qualified for the ballot by petition
FL.summary: Florida Politics tracks candidates who qualified for the 2026 general election ballot by petition, including several local races ahead of the August 18 primary, explaining how Florida's petition-qualifying process works and which candidates have met the signature threshold.

GA.title: 6 candidates qualify in special election to replace late Rep. David Scott in Congress
GA.summary: Six candidates, including Rep. Scott's daughter Marcye Scott, qualified for the July 28 special election to fill Georgia's 13th congressional district seat left vacant by Scott's death, with a runoff on August 25 if no candidate wins a majority.

HI.title: Hawaii sticks with its mail-in voting system despite Trump's order
HI.summary: Hawaii election officials say the state will continue its mandatory mail-in voting system for the 2026 elections despite President Trump's executive order targeting mail ballots, with the state elections officer saying a change would require new legislation. Hawaii has joined a 19-state coalition suing the Trump administration over the order.

ID.title: It's not clear if Idaho district judge candidate in Ada County is legally qualified for the role
ID.summary: An Ada County judicial candidate in Idaho's May 19 primary appears to fall months short of the state's 10-year bar admission requirement, raising questions about ballot eligibility days before the election and broader concerns about candidate vetting.

IL.title: How Illinois county clerks are combating election misinformation
IL.summary: Illinois county clerks and state election officials describe their proactive strategies for countering voting misinformation ahead of the 2026 midterms, including monitoring social media with state police and DHS. Officials across party lines say transparency and rapid response have helped address declining voter confidence in election security.

IN.title: GOP Sen. Deery's lead firms up to 3 votes over Trump-backed challenger
IN.summary: State Sen. Spencer Deery extended his lead to three votes over Trump-endorsed challenger Paula Copenhaver after Parke County verified a provisional ballot, though two more provisional ballots in Tippecanoe County remain. The ultra-close Indiana Senate District 23 result may still trigger a formal recount petition.

IN.title: Indiana's Senate District 23 race could come down to a single vote
IN.summary: With provisional ballots still being counted in Tippecanoe County, the Indiana Senate District 23 Republican primary margin could shrink to a single vote. Candidates have until May 19 noon to file a recount petition in a race that has drawn national attention.

IN.title: SOS Morales asked to step aside if recount occurs, criticized for D.C. trip
IN.summary: A Democratic state legislator called on Indiana Secretary of State Diego Morales to recuse himself from any potential recount of the Senate District 23 primary race, citing concerns about impartiality after he attended a White House event during the vote-counting period. Morales' office declined.

IN.title: Indiana Sec. of State's office outlines recount, contest petition process following primary election
IN.summary: Indiana's Secretary of State office clarified the recount and contest petition process after the May 5 primary, explaining there are no automatic recounts and candidates have until May 19 to file. The explainer is directly relevant to the ongoing Senate District 23 race decided by three votes.

IA.title: Iowa Democrats face a competitive primary as they attempt to flip Ernst's open Senate seat
IA.summary: Iowa Public Radio profiles the Democratic Senate primary between Josh Turek and Zach Wahls as early voting opens, with both candidates competing to flip the seat vacated by retiring Sen. Joni Ernst and a televised debate scheduled for May 14 evening.

IA.title: Democrats Will Debate in Iowa US Senate Primary Shaped by Outside Money and Big-Name Endorsements
IA.summary: Turek and Wahls face off in a televised debate on May 14 as VoteVets spends $7 million supporting Turek; the open-seat race features major endorsements from Sen. Warren and Pete Buttigieg ahead of Iowa's June 2 primary.

KY.title: No-excuse early voting begins in Kentucky
KY.summary: No-excuse in-person early voting opened statewide in Kentucky on May 14 for the May 19 primary, running through Saturday May 16 and covering races including the open U.S. Senate seat vacated by Mitch McConnell.

KY.title: Voting in the Kentucky primary? Early voting polls open May 14
KY.summary: Early voting opened May 14 for Kentucky's May 19 primary, with the Secretary of State noting more early voting locations than in November 2024; 12 Republicans and 7 Democrats are competing for McConnell's Senate seat.

KY.title: Early voting for Kentucky primary elections begins Thursday
KY.summary: The Kentucky Lantern reports that no-excuse absentee early voting began Thursday, May 14, ahead of the May 19 primary, with polling at county clerks' offices and designated satellite locations statewide through Saturday May 16.

LA.title: Louisiana redistricting fight heads to full Senate vote
LA.summary: Louisiana's full Senate took up a new congressional map on May 14 that would eliminate one majority-Black district and give Republicans a 5-1 House advantage, following the Supreme Court ruling that struck down the state's prior map.

LA.title: Louisiana senators take up new US House map while South Carolina plans for extra redistricting work
LA.summary: The Louisiana Senate considered a redistricting bill that would dissolve Rep. Cleo Fields' majority-Black 6th District; the measure must pass both chambers by June 1 before suspended House primaries can be rescheduled.

LA.title: Who's winning the 2026 redistricting war? Not voters
LA.summary: NPR examines how Louisiana's suspension of congressional primaries — invalidating tens of thousands of already-cast absentee ballots — is fueling voter cynicism, with advocates warning the instability reinforces the perception that elections are rigged.

LA.title: A majority-Black district in Louisiana traces a long fight over the Voting Rights Act
LA.summary: In-depth account of Louisiana's 6th Congressional District and decades-long legal battles over majority-Black representation that culminated in the April 2026 Supreme Court ruling weakening the Voting Rights Act, prompting the current redistricting fight.

ME.title: JD Vance expected to address anti-fraud efforts during Bangor visit
ME.summary: Vice President Vance traveled to Bangor on May 14 to highlight the Trump administration's election-fraud investigations ahead of Maine's June 9 primary, also campaigning for Republican 2nd-district congressional candidate Paul LePage.

MD.title: Maryland passes first state law including ranked choice voting
MD.summary: Governor Wes Moore signed SB848/HB1448 on May 12, marking the first time ranked choice voting has been written into Maryland law; the bipartisan bill sets new election administration requirements for RCV elections in Maryland cities.

MA.title: Amid a deluge of ballot questions, Massachusetts' high court could dramatically shape the November ballot
MA.summary: The Massachusetts SJC is weighing legal challenges to multiple 2026 ballot initiatives on a compressed timeline, including the all-party primary proposal that would eliminate party primaries and reshape how voters participate in Massachusetts elections.

MI.title: After MI Senate special election, what's ahead for Legislature and November midterms?
MI.summary: Following Democrat Chedrick Greene's decisive win in the Michigan Senate District 35 special election, this piece examines what the restored 20-18 Democratic majority means for the legislative session and what the result signals for November midterms in a competitive state.

MI.title: Democratic U.S. Senate candidates escalate attacks as Michigan primary intensifies
MI.summary: With Michigan's August 4 primary approaching, the three-way Democratic contest for the U.S. Senate seat has grown sharply contested in a state considered a key Senate battleground.

MI.title: Your 2026 Michigan voting guide
MI.summary: A comprehensive guide covering Michigan's 2026 election calendar, voter registration rules (including Election Day registration), absentee voting procedures, and key statewide races including governor, U.S. Senate, and all 13 congressional districts.

MS.title: Democrats get a last-minute reprieve on 2026 redistricting
MS.summary: Mississippi Gov. Tate Reeves canceled a planned special session to redraw state Supreme Court voting districts after the 5th Circuit vacated the redistricting order, giving Black Democratic incumbents a temporary reprieve while the governor signaled plans to pursue congressional redistricting after the midterms.

MO.title: Missouri's new congressional map is set. Who's running for Kansas City's 5th District?
MO.summary: Following the Missouri Supreme Court's unanimous ruling upholding the GOP-gerrymandered congressional map, this report examines the crowded candidate field in the redrawn 5th District—where incumbent Rep. Emanuel Cleaver faces six Republican challengers—ahead of the August 4 primary.

MO.title: Missouri redistricting foes want Hoskins to decide on referendum now. Here's why that's not likely
MO.summary: People Not Politicians is pressing Secretary of State Denny Hoskins to certify referendum petition signatures and suspend the gerrymandered congressional map, but Hoskins has until August 4 to verify signatures—the same day as the primary—creating potential legal chaos around Missouri elections.

MT.title: 2026 Primary Election: Incumbent Challenged for Republican Nomination in House District 13
MT.summary: With absentee ballots already mailed and Montana's June 2 primary underway under new voter ID rules, incumbent Rep. Linda Reksten faces a primary challenger in House District 13 amid GOP intraparty conflict over her voting record on Medicaid expansion and nonpartisan courts.

NE.title: Denise Powell wins Democratic primary for battleground Nebraska seat
NE.summary: Political organizer Denise Powell defeated State Sen. John Cavanaugh by about 2 percentage points to win the Nebraska 2nd District Democratic primary, setting up a competitive general election against Republican Brinker Harding in Omaha's 'blue dot' district seen as a key House battleground.

NE.title: Denise Powell wins Democratic primary for Nebraska's 2nd congressional district
NE.summary: The AP called the Nebraska NE-02 Democratic primary for Denise Powell in a close six-person race in an Omaha-area district considered one of Democrats' top opportunities to flip a House seat in the 2026 midterms.

NV.title: Why Nevadans should care about the Supreme Court dismantling protections for fair representation of Black voters
NV.summary: Nevada officials and advocates warn that the Supreme Court's 6-3 ruling gutting Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act threatens fair electoral representation in Nevada, where voters of color make up more than 50% of the electorate in three of the state's four congressional districts.

NV.title: Nevada Secretary of State gives voter roll update ahead of midterm primaries
NV.summary: Nevada Secretary of State Francisco Aguilar reported that spring voter roll maintenance designated 119,533 voters inactive and canceled 7,583 registrations, with early voting for the June 9 primary set to begin May 23.

NJ.title: Newark Mayor Ras Baraka Wins The Mayoral Race
NJ.summary: Ras Baraka won re-election as Newark mayor with over 70% of the vote in New Jersey's largest city's nonpartisan May 12 municipal election, securing a fourth term over seven challengers.

NJ.title: Baraka wins fourth term as Newark mayor
NJ.summary: New Jersey Globe reports that Baraka captured 70.34% of the vote in Newark's nonpartisan municipal election, decisively defeating seven opponents in the city's most-watched 2026 local election.

NY.title: NY Elections, Census and Redistricting Update 05/11/26
NY.summary: CityLand's weekly elections update covers New York's mid-decade redistricting push after the Supreme Court weakened the Voting Rights Act, including proposed constitutional amendments to allow the legislature to redraw congressional maps before 2028.

NY.title: Redistricting war isn't over, Democrats say as Jeffries calls a meeting this week
NY.summary: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries called New York among states expected to respond to the Supreme Court's Voting Rights Act ruling with a 'massive Democratic redistricting counteroffensive,' directly affecting how New York's congressional voters will be represented.

NC.title: North Carolina voters have until July to comment on proposed election rules
NC.summary: The North Carolina State Board of Elections opened public comment through July 14 on four sets of proposed administrative rules covering absentee voting procedures, photo ID requirements for mail-in ballots, recount processes, and voting site administration.

NC.title: North Carolina Senate Primary 2026 Live Results: Cooper, Whatley Win
NC.summary: Former Gov. Roy Cooper and former RNC Chair Michael Whatley won their May 12 runoff primaries, setting up a high-profile U.S. Senate general election battle for North Carolina's open seat expected to be a key race for Senate control.

ND.title: What to know before the June 9 primary election in North Dakota
ND.summary: A comprehensive voter guide for North Dakota's June 9 primary covers two constitutional ballot measures on term limits and initiative petition rules, more than 765 positions on the ballot, and new mail-in ballot rules requiring ballots to be received by Election Day.

OH.title: Catching Our Eye News Roundup, May 13, 2026
OH.summary: Post-primary roundup covers the emerging November matchup between Vivek Ramaswamy and Amy Acton for governor, analysis of school levy failures at the May 5 primary, and expert commentary on whether Ohio is returning to battleground status given tight polling in governor and Senate races.

OR.title: Today is the last preferred day to return ballots by mail in Oregon. What to do after
OR.summary: Oregon election officials warned that May 14 is the last recommended day to mail ballots for the May 19 primary due to U.S. Postal Service delivery concerns, advising voters who miss the window to use official drop boxes or request a manual USPS postmark.

RI.title: Supreme Court voting rights ruling set to reshape local power from statehouses to school boards
RI.summary: Pew Stateline reports on the broad impact of the Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais decision weakening the Voting Rights Act, noting Rhode Island is among at least 10 states that introduced their own state-level voting rights bills this year in response to eroding federal protections.

SC.title: S.C. governor calls special session for redistricting despite concerns
SC.summary: South Carolina Gov. Henry McMaster called a special legislative session to vote on congressional redistricting on May 14, bypassing the two-thirds Senate threshold that blocked the effort in regular session, with the proposed map set to redraw Rep. James Clyburn's district and give Republicans an advantage in all seven U.S. House seats.

SC.title: South Carolina Governor Plans Special Session to Redraw House Maps
SC.summary: Gov. McMaster's special session announcement came after the Senate failed a 29-17 vote to extend the regular session; a new map could shift South Carolina's June 9 congressional primaries to August and would favor Republicans across all seven districts.

TN.title: Who's winning the 2026 redistricting war? Not voters
TN.summary: NPR examines the wave of mid-decade redistricting following the Supreme Court's voting rights ruling, including how Tennessee's newly enacted congressional map splitting the state's only majority-Black, Democrat-held Memphis district into three affects voters amid ongoing federal court challenges.

TN.title: NAACP alleges new Tennessee congressional map intentionally discriminates on basis of race
TN.summary: The NAACP filed a federal civil rights lawsuit arguing Tennessee's redrawn congressional map deliberately cracks Memphis's majority-Black district across three districts to dilute Black voting power in violation of the Fourteenth and Fifteenth Amendments, with a federal court hearing scheduled for May 20.

TX.title: Will Texas get another MAGA attorney general? Or something new?
TX.summary: Ahead of the May 26 Republican primary runoff, this report examines the Texas attorney general race—one of the most-watched contests—where candidates compete to succeed Ken Paxton, with early voting starting May 18.

UT.title: Redrawn district, narrow convention margin set up competitive House Republican primary in Utah
UT.summary: Under Utah's newly court-ordered congressional map, incumbent Rep. Celeste Maloy narrowly beat Phil Lyman at the Republican convention and now faces him again in the June 23 primary, setting up one of the most competitive House races in the state's history.

VT.title: Vermont's U.S. Rep. Becca Balint announces reelection campaign
VT.summary: Rep. Becca Balint officially launched her reelection bid for Vermont's sole U.S. House seat, setting up a rematch with Republican Mark Coester ahead of the August 11 primary and November general election.

VA.title: SCOTUS is dismantling voting rights, but Virginia offers examples of a way forward
VA.summary: In the wake of a U.S. Supreme Court ruling weakening the Voting Rights Act, Virginia leaders warn that minority representation could erode under future Republican-controlled redistricting, while pointing to Virginia's 2021 state Voting Rights Act as a model for protecting voters.

WV.title: Primary Election Post Mortem
WV.summary: WV MetroNews analyzes West Virginia's May 12 primary: voter turnout hit 21%, slightly below 2022; independent voters are credited with ousting all three incumbent judges; and Republicans now hold a registration majority in Monongalia County for the first time.

WI.title: Wisconsin GOP looks to Trump's die-hard fans to brighten election prospects
WI.source: Wisconsin Watch / Milwaukee Neighborhood News Service
WI.summary: Ahead of the May 15-17 Republican State Convention in Wisconsin Dells, this report examines GOP strategy to mobilize Trump supporters for the November midterms after their party's 20-point loss in the April Supreme Court election.

DC.title: DC Mayor Race 2026 — Candidate Tracker
DC.summary: With DC's June 16 primary ballots now in the mail and ranked choice voting being used for the first time in DC history, this tracker profiles all seven candidates competing in the open mayoral race following Mayor Muriel Bowser's retirement.

AL.title: Election Day: What to bring to vote in Alabama's May 19 primary
AL.summary: Alabama voters heading to the polls for the May 19 statewide primary must present a valid photo ID; the article outlines accepted forms of identification and explains provisional ballot options for voters without ID, ahead of a primary that also involves ongoing redistricting uncertainty for four congressional districts.

FL.title: Judge to hear challenge to new congressional districts
FL.summary: A Leon County circuit court judge was set to hear arguments from plaintiffs challenging Florida's newly signed congressional redistricting map, which critics say violates the state's Fair Districts constitutional amendments and is designed to give Republicans four additional seats.

FL.title: Florida judge to hear consolidation arguments in state redistricting lawsuits
FL.summary: A Leon County circuit judge heard arguments on consolidating three separate lawsuits seeking to block Florida's new congressional map, with plaintiffs arguing it violates the Fair Districts amendments voters adopted in 2010 to curb partisan gerrymandering and protect minority voting rights.

GA.title: Early voting ends today in Georgia's Democratic, GOP primaries
GA.summary: Georgia's early in-person voting period concluded on May 15 ahead of the May 19 primary election, with more than 700,000 voters having already cast ballots — a roughly 28% increase over the comparable point in the 2022 primary cycle.

GA.title: Georgia early voting ends Friday as turnout surges ahead of 2026 primary election
GA.summary: The final day of Georgia's early voting period drew record-breaking participation ahead of the May 19 primary, driven by competitive statewide races for governor, secretary of state, and a crowded Republican contest for the U.S. Senate seat held by Jon Ossoff.

GA.title: Georgia election 2026: Early voting ends Friday for primary elections
GA.summary: WSB-TV reported on the close of Georgia's early voting window on May 15 and provided voter guidance on polling locations and rules for the upcoming May 19 primary, noting turnout was outpacing 2022 levels significantly.

HI.title: Judge weighs Democrats' bid to block Trump's executive order on voting
HI.summary: A federal judge heard arguments from Democratic Party lawyers seeking to block Trump's March 31 executive order on elections, which would restrict mail-in voting and require citizenship proof to register — Hawaii, which operates an all-mail voting system under state law, joined 19 other attorneys general in suing to block the order.

ID.title: Friday is the deadline to early vote in Idaho ahead of 2026 primary election
ID.summary: Idaho's early in-person absentee voting window closes May 15 ahead of the May 19 primary; voters who missed the early voting or pre-registration deadlines can still register and cast a ballot in person on Election Day with valid photo ID and proof of residence.

ID.title: Friday is the deadline to early vote in Idaho
ID.summary: The Coeur d'Alene Press reminded north Idaho voters that May 15 is the last day for early in-person voting before Idaho's May 19 primary election, which features contested races for governor, both U.S. House seats, and a U.S. Senate seat.

IL.title: Right-wing group sues Illinois in first post-Callais attack on a state Voting Rights Act
IL.summary: The Public Interest Legal Foundation filed a federal lawsuit seeking to strike down Illinois' Voting Rights Act, arguing it unconstitutionally uses race as a primary factor in drawing legislative maps, in what Democracy Docket calls the first direct challenge to a state-level voting rights act following the U.S. Supreme Court's Callais ruling.

LA.title: Louisiana Senate approves new map that would scrap majority-Black district
LA.summary: The Louisiana Senate passed a new congressional map eliminating one of the state's two majority-Black districts, shifting the state's delegation from a 4-2 to a 5-1 Republican advantage following the Supreme Court's Callais decision invalidating race-based district drawing.

MN.title: House Approves Final Elections Committee Bills
MN.source: Minnesota House of Representatives Session Daily
MN.summary: The Minnesota House gave final approval to two elections bills (HF4239 and HF4240), voting to concur with Senate amendments and sending them to Governor Walz for signature; the bills modernize election administration, streamline procedures, and standardize use of the statewide voter registration system.

MO.title: Missouri's gerrymandered map sows electoral confusion
MO.summary: Following the Missouri Supreme Court's unanimous ruling upholding the GOP-drawn congressional map, election officials remain in limbo as the Secretary of State has not yet opened the voter registration system to reflect new district boundaries ahead of the August primary.

MO.title: Missouri map confusion leaves Jackson County, local election officials in limbo
MO.summary: Missouri's newly upheld gerrymandered congressional map splits Kansas City into three districts, leaving Jackson County and local clerks unable to update voter rolls while a referendum petition that could still block the map remains pending.

MS.title: Mississippi redistricting debate continues despite canceled special session
MS.summary: After Gov. Tate Reeves canceled the planned special session to redraw Mississippi's judicial districts, advocacy groups including the Mississippi Center for Justice announced a May 20 day of action and vowed to continue fighting any redistricting that would dilute Black voting power.

NH.title: Under new law, NH's state primary election to move up to June starting in 2028
NH.summary: Governor Kelly Ayotte signed a law moving New Hampshire's state primary from September to the second Tuesday in June beginning in 2028. Supporters say the earlier date gives non-incumbent candidates more time to campaign before the general election.

NH.title: Under new law, NH's state primary election to move up to June starting in 2028
NH.summary: Valley News coverage of New Hampshire's newly signed law shifting the state primary to the second Tuesday in June starting in 2028, noting Secretary of State David Scanlan's commitment to executing the new schedule despite having favored an August primary date.

NJ.title: Insider NJ's 2026 Nonpartisan May Municipal Elections Publication
NJ.summary: Post-election coverage of New Jersey's May 12 nonpartisan municipal elections, reporting results including Mayor André Sayegh's reelection in Paterson and the Newark mayoral race, conducted under the state's newly expanded early voting law for May municipal contests.

NM.title: Semi-open primary in New Mexico enables more participation
NM.summary: New Mexico's June 2 primary is the state's first semi-open primary under Senate Bill 16, allowing over 330,000 unaffiliated 'decline to state' voters to request a Democratic or Republican ballot without changing their party registration, a historic expansion of primary participation.

NY.title: Hakeem Jeffries pushes New York to join redistricting battle
NY.summary: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries dispatched Rep. Joe Morelle to Albany to lobby for a mid-decade redistricting constitutional amendment in response to the Supreme Court's Voting Rights Act decision, arguing it is necessary to protect minority voting representation in congressional maps.

NY.title: Gianaris: Chances of passing budget next week 'very slim' as negotiations mesh with redistricting push
NY.summary: Deputy Senate Majority Leader Mike Gianaris and Assembly Speaker Carl Heastie confirmed New York will advance a constitutional amendment potentially enabling mid-decade redistricting as a response to GOP map-drawing in red states, though the amendment would not affect election maps before 2028.

PA.title: Pa. primary election 2026: What you need to know before you vote
PA.summary: Comprehensive voter guide for Pennsylvania's May 19 primary covering registration status, mail ballot deadlines, closed primary rules, and key statewide races including governor and all 17 congressional districts.

PA.title: Pennsylvania voting rights: what to know for May 19 election
PA.summary: Outlines voter rights for Pennsylvania's May 19 primary including ID requirements only for first-time voters at a polling location, provisional ballot access, and protections flowing from recent Pennsylvania Supreme Court rulings on flawed mail ballots.

PA.title: Your last-minute guide to voting in the 2026 PA primary election
PA.summary: Last-minute voting guide for Pennsylvania's May 19 primary covering polling hours, ballot return deadlines, how to find your polling place, and an overview of statewide races on the ballot.

PA.title: What you need to know about voter intimidation in Pennsylvania
PA.summary: Explains state and federal laws prohibiting voter intimidation in Pennsylvania ahead of the May 19 primary, including how voters can report incidents to county election offices and the Office of the Attorney General.

SC.title: The State House Gavel: Gov orders lawmakers to return for special session to take up redistricting
SC.summary: Gov. McMaster ordered the South Carolina legislature back for a special session on May 15 to attempt to redraw congressional maps and eliminate the state's only majority-Black district held by Rep. Jim Clyburn, after the Senate blocked a supermajority procedural vote during the regular session.

SC.title: South Carolina redistricting: Governor forces lawmakers back to session to eliminate lone majority-Black district
SC.summary: Gov. McMaster invoked executive authority to reconvene the South Carolina legislature for a redistricting special session aimed at dismantling the state's sole Democratic congressional seat, part of a broader GOP push following the Supreme Court's weakening of Voting Rights Act protections.

SC.title: South Carolina governor calls special session on redistricting
SC.summary: CBS News covers South Carolina's governor calling a special legislative session to enact a new congressional map that would give Republicans all seven congressional seats and eliminate Rep. James Clyburn's majority-minority district ahead of the November 2026 midterms.

TN.title: Challengers seek restraining orders for new voting map as US House candidate deadline approaches
TN.summary: Multiple civil rights organizations — including the ACLU and NAACP — sought temporary restraining orders on May 15 to block Tennessee's new congressional map that eliminates the state's only majority-Black district in Memphis, as the U.S. House candidate qualification deadline arrived.

TX.title: Early voting in Texas' primary runoff election begins May 18. Here's what to know.
TX.summary: With May 15 as the mail-ballot application deadline and early voting set to begin May 18, Texas voters prepare for the May 26 primary runoff featuring the high-profile U.S. Senate race between incumbent John Cornyn and Attorney General Ken Paxton.

TX.title: Texas Secretary of State Encourages Voters to Review Official Information ahead of the May 26 Primary Runoff Election
TX.summary: Texas Secretary of State Jane Nelson issued official guidance ahead of the May 26 runoff, reminding voters that early voting runs May 18-22, that May 15 is the last day to request a mail ballot, and that photo ID is required at all polling locations.

VA.title: NAACP asks U.S. Supreme Court to overturn Virginia redistricting decision
VA.summary: The NAACP filed a brief supporting Virginia Democrats' emergency appeal to the U.S. Supreme Court to overturn the Virginia Supreme Court's May 8 ruling that voided the voters' approval of a redistricting referendum, arguing the ruling discarded over 3.1 million ballots.

VT.title: Vermont constitutional amendment on equal protection of the law headed to November ballot
VT.summary: The Vermont House voted 128-14 on May 13 to send Proposal 4, a constitutional amendment on equal protection, to the November 2026 ballot — part of the state's legislative response to the Supreme Court's weakening of federal voting rights protections.

WA.title: Bill strengthening protections on Washington's voter database takes effect
WA.summary: A new Washington law making it a felony for election officials to disclose private voter data — enacted in response to the Trump administration's 2025 request for the state's complete voter rolls — took effect, with only the Secretary of State's office authorized to respond to voter database requests.

WI.title: Wisconsin will likely see limited, local effects from Voting Rights Act ruling — at least for now
WI.summary: Wisconsin will face limited immediate fallout from the Supreme Court's Voting Rights Act ruling, though Milwaukee-area local district boundaries and future redistricting battles could be affected as progressive groups continue legal challenges to the state's congressional map.

WI.title: Wisconsin plays role in national redistricting fights
WI.summary: Wisconsin is a focal point in national redistricting litigation, with progressive law firm Law Forward vowing to appeal a court dismissal of a challenge to the state's Republican-gerrymandered congressional map to the state Supreme Court, which now has a 5-2 liberal majority.

WY.title: Wyoming voters face looming deadline for party affiliation changes
WY.summary: Wyoming voters had until 5 p.m. on May 13 to change their party registration before the primary election under Wyoming's crossover voting restrictions, after which changes cannot be made until after the August 18 primary.

AL.title: Thousands attend protests in Selma and Montgomery for voting rights
AL.summary: Thousands rallied in Selma and Montgomery on May 16 to protest the U.S. Supreme Court's decision allowing Alabama to use a previously blocked congressional map; the 'All Roads Lead to the South' demonstrations drew over 5,000 people calling for new federal voting rights protections.

AL.title: Thousands rally in birthplace of Civil Rights Movement to defend Black political representation
AL.summary: PBS NewsHour covered the Selma-to-Montgomery marches on May 16, reporting on protesters' opposition to the Supreme Court ruling clearing Alabama to use its previously struck-down congressional map and calls for new federal voting rights legislation.

AL.title: In the birthplace of Civil Rights Movement, groups rally to defend Black political representation
AL.summary: AP reported on the May 16 rally in Montgomery and Selma following the Supreme Court's decision to let Alabama use a congressional map federal courts had ruled racially discriminatory, with Gov. Ivey scheduling a special primary in four affected districts for August 11.

AZ.title: Everyone who filed to run for Arizona's state, legislative and federal offices in 2026
AZ.summary: Arizona Mirror published a comprehensive roundup of the 260-plus candidates who filed ahead of the deadline for the July 21 primary, covering all 90 legislative seats, seven statewide offices, and nine U.S. House races.

CA.title: Amid rising fears of rolling back voter rights, Black lawmakers announce new Voting Rights Act for California
CA.summary: California's Black Legislative Caucus announced a new state bill to mirror the federal Voting Rights Act of 1965, in direct response to the Supreme Court's ruling in Louisiana v. Callais that sharply limited Section 2 protections against voter discrimination.

CO.title: Election denier Tina Peters will get clemency after admitting she 'made a mistake,' Colorado's Democratic governor says
CO.summary: Colorado Gov. Jared Polis granted clemency to convicted Mesa County clerk Tina Peters, cutting her 9-year sentence in half and enabling her release by June 1; the decision drew sharp condemnation from Secretary of State Jena Griswold.

CO.title: Colorado governor grants election denier Tina Peters clemency, reduces sentence
CO.summary: Democracy Docket reported on Polis commuting Peters' sentence following her conviction for copying election system software, and covered reaction from election officials warning the decision validates the election-denial movement.

CT.title: CT GOP opens convention, nominating down-ballot candidates
CT.summary: Connecticut Republicans opened their two-day nominating convention at Mohegan Sun, with delegates choosing statewide candidates ahead of the August primary and determining which candidates qualify for the ballot under state endorsement rules.

CT.title: Ryan Fazio wins the CT GOP nomination for governor
CT.summary: State Sen. Ryan Fazio won the Connecticut Republican Party's gubernatorial endorsement with 92% of delegate votes, leaving challenger Betsy McCaughey far below the 15% threshold needed to force an August primary.

CT.title: CT Dems endorse Lamont for 3rd term, but he faces primary
CT.summary: Gov. Ned Lamont secured the Democratic convention endorsement but challenger Josh Elliott surpassed the 15% threshold for an August primary ballot spot, making this the first competitive Democratic gubernatorial primary in Connecticut in years.

CT.title: What to expect from CT's Democratic and Republican conventions
CT.summary: Preview of Connecticut's two party conventions explaining how the state's endorsement-then-primary ballot-access system works and how the 15% delegate threshold determines which candidates proceed to the August primary.

DE.title: Voter Turnout Shapes Key Delaware School Board Races as Challengers Score Major Wins
DE.summary: Covering the May 12 school board elections, turnout more than doubled compared to 2024 with over 12,100 voters casting ballots; incumbent board members largely lost to challenger candidates running on transparency platforms.

DE.title: School Board Overhauls — Appo, Red Clay presidents lose, former State Board president falls in Delmar
DE.summary: WDEL reported on the sweep of incumbent school board presidents in the Appoquinimink, Red Clay, and Delmar districts in the May 12 elections, driven by a dramatic voter turnout surge.

FL.title: Court fight over Ron DeSantis' new congressional map kicks off in Florida
FL.summary: A Leon County circuit court held a hearing on whether to block DeSantis' new congressional map — which shifts four seats toward Republicans — with voting rights groups arguing it violates Florida's Fair Districts Amendments.

GA.title: Georgia early voters top 1M, breaking primary election record
GA.summary: More than 1,023,000 Georgians voted early ahead of the May 19 primary, shattering the previous record of 857,401 set in 2022, with Democrats holding a roughly 150,000-ballot advantage over Republicans.

GA.title: Georgia primary: Early voting breaks record as Democratic ballot selection leads
GA.summary: Early voting closed May 15 with record-breaking participation and a notable Democratic ballot selection advantage ahead of the May 19 primary featuring competitive races for governor, U.S. Senate, secretary of state, and attorney general.

GA.title: Georgia voters: What you need to know about Tuesday's primary election
GA.summary: Voter guide covering polling hours, ID requirements, absentee ballot deadlines, and runoff rules for Georgia's May 19 primary across competitive statewide and congressional races.

GA.title: What to know about Georgia's primary as Republicans set sights on Senate
GA.summary: Overview of Georgia's May 19 primary covering the competitive Republican field to challenge Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff and the open governor's race, with early voting showing record Democratic turnout advantage.

HI.title: Hawaii sticks with its mail-in voting system despite Trump's order
HI.summary: Hawaii officials confirmed they will continue following state law requiring all-mail elections despite President Trump's executive order on voting; the state attorney general joined a 19-state federal lawsuit challenging the order as unconstitutional.

ID.title: Friday is the deadline to early vote in Idaho ahead of 2026 primary election
ID.summary: Early and in-person absentee voting closed at 5 p.m. on May 15 statewide ahead of the May 19 primary; voters who missed the window can still register and vote on Election Day at their designated polling place.

ID.title: Primary election voters have a unique chance to determine Idaho's future
ID.summary: With more than 430 contested positions on the May 19 primary ballot — including governor, U.S. Senate, and all legislative seats — the Idaho Capital Sun highlighted that fewer than one in four eligible voters participated in the 2024 primary, giving each vote outsized influence.

IN.title: Possible recounts of tight state Senate races could extend into July
IN.summary: The Indiana Recount Commission convened as the petition window opened for close primary races; candidates have until May 19 to file recount petitions, and any state legislative recount could take months under the court-supervised process.

IN.title: Indiana State Recount Commission preparing in case vote recounts are requested
IN.summary: The Recount Commission unanimously appointed attorney Jessica Dickinson as recount director ahead of the May 15-22 petition window; Senate District 23 decided by three votes between Deery and Copenhaver is the most likely candidate for a formal recount request.

IN.title: Indiana GOP primary recount procedures approved
IN.summary: The Indiana Recount Commission approved procedures for potential recount petitions from the May 5 primary; Secretary of State Diego Morales confirmed he will remain commission chair despite Democratic calls for recusal.

IN.title: Morales says he'll remain commission chair for any recount proceedings
IN.summary: Indiana Secretary of State Diego Morales publicly stated he would not step aside as Recount Commission chair despite Democratic pressure, pledging to conduct any proceedings carefully, deliberately, and transparently.

IA.title: Turek, Wahls spar over reproductive rights in second U.S. Senate Democratic primary debate
IA.summary: Democratic U.S. Senate candidates Josh Turek and Zach Wahls held their second televised debate, clashing on reproductive rights and outside PAC spending, ahead of the June 2 Iowa primary for Joni Ernst's open seat.

IA.title: Iowa Democratic Senate candidates clash over bipartisan approach to abortion policy
IA.summary: Turek and Wahls disagreed on whether bipartisan compromise is possible on reproductive rights during their second debate; with early voting underway since May 13 and heavy outside PAC spending, the June 2 primary is heating up.

KY.title: While many Kentuckians choose early voting, others opting to wait
KY.summary: Reports on early voting participation patterns as Kentucky's May 19 primary approaches, with many voters opting for in-person early voting at expanded locations while others choose to wait for Election Day.

KY.title: More than 50,000 Kentuckians cast early votes on first day of primary voting
KY.summary: Over 50,000 Kentucky voters cast early ballots on the first day of no-excuse early voting — more than 30,000 Republicans, 20,000 Democrats, and 515 independents — representing a 75% increase over the previous election cycle.

KY.title: Kentucky sees record early voting turnout ahead of primary election
KY.summary: Jefferson County recorded record early voting numbers for the 2026 primary, with 23,575 people voting early across the three-day early voting window, reflecting elevated civic engagement statewide.

KY.title: Kentucky's rural counties seeing record early voting turnout
KY.summary: Rural Kentucky counties are seeing historically high early voting ahead of the May 19 primary, with Hardin County expanding from 4 to 15 polling locations to meet demand from voters.

KY.title: Early in-person voting begins, 2026 Kentucky primary could see record turnout
KY.summary: Reports on early in-person voting opening for Kentucky's May 19 primary, with projections of record overall statewide turnout based on first-day early voting numbers.

LA.title: Widespread confusion surrounds Louisiana's May 16 election, leaving voters 'frustrated'
LA.summary: Voters and poll workers across Louisiana experienced significant confusion under the state's new closed primary system, with registered Democrats receiving inconsistent ballots and 'No Party' voters unable to cast ballots in the Republican primary without extra paperwork.

LA.title: May 16 election results: Louisiana voters reject all 5 amendments; see full results
LA.summary: Louisiana voters rejected all five state constitutional amendments on the May 16 ballot, including measures on civil service, education funding, and teacher stipends, in an election already roiled by controversy over the governor's postponement of U.S. House races.

LA.title: Louisiana primary election results 2026
LA.summary: Incumbent Sen. Bill Cassidy was eliminated in Louisiana's first closed Republican Senate primary, with Trump-endorsed Rep. Julia Letlow (44%) and State Treasurer John Fleming (28%) advancing to a June 27 runoff.

LA.title: RESULTS: Letlow, Fleming head to runoff in Republican Senate primary
LA.summary: Final unofficial results from Louisiana's May 16 primary confirm Letlow and Fleming advancing to the June 27 runoff in the Republican U.S. Senate race under the state's newly adopted closed primary system.

LA.title: Sen. Bill Cassidy loses reelection bid as Julia Letlow and John Fleming advance to Louisiana Senate runoff, CNN projects
LA.summary: CNN projected that Sen. Cassidy failed to advance to the runoff after being defeated in Louisiana's first closed Republican Senate primary, with Julia Letlow and John Fleming advancing to the June 27 contest.

MD.title: Slate of Maryland election reform bills set to go into law before November midterms
MD.summary: Gov. Wes Moore signed a package of election reform bills including plain-language ballot requirements, extended mail-in ballot counting, and faithless elector prevention, all taking effect before the November general election.

MD.title: 'No Kings Act,' 'Mason's Law' among more than 200 bills signed into law
MD.summary: Among 200-plus bills signed by Gov. Moore was election legislation including a ranked choice voting administration bill (SB848/HB1448), setting statewide standards for RCV contests in municipal elections.

MO.title: What you need to know about the Missouri Legislature's bills passed, not passed this session
MO.summary: The Missouri House passed an omnibus elections bill that restores voting rights to some people on parole/probation, requires explicit donor consent for recurring campaign contributions, allows email election notifications, and makes other election administration changes.

MO.title: Missouri legislative session ends without property tax reform
MO.summary: The Missouri Legislature adjourned May 15 after passing an omnibus elections bill; a constitutional amendment that could put an income tax elimination on the ballot was also advanced, with Gov. Kehoe yet to decide whether to place it before voters in August or November.

MS.title: Groups rally to defend Black political representation
MS.summary: Thousands gathered in Mississippi to protest the dismantling of majority-Black congressional districts following the Supreme Court's ruling weakening the Voting Rights Act; civil rights leaders warned of coordinated attacks on Black political power ahead of redistricting efforts.

MS.title: In the Birthplace of Civil Rights Movement, Groups Rally to Defend Black Political Representation
MS.summary: AP reported on the 'All Roads Lead to the South' rally as civil rights organizations mobilized against Republican redistricting plans targeting Mississippi's lone majority-Black congressional district, with Gov. Reeves confirming plans to redraw the district before 2028.

MT.title: End of the line for writing in Montana unofficial candidates
MT.summary: The 2025 Legislature passed HB 207 requiring write-in candidates to file during the regular March window, resulting in write-in ovals and lines being removed from 2026 primary ballots for the first time in Montana history.

MT.title: Montana voters will be able to register to vote on Election Day, judge rules
MT.summary: A Montana judge blocked SB 490, which would have ended voter registration at noon on Election Day for federal elections, finding the law would disproportionately burden Native American and young voters; registration remains open until 8 p.m. through the June 2 primary.

NE.title: Douglas County counts last early ballots; Powell still wins NE-02
NE.summary: After Douglas County finished counting over 5,000 outstanding ballots from the May 12 primary, Denise Powell's lead in the NE-02 Democratic House primary widened enough to avoid an automatic recount; official results will be certified May 29.

NE.title: Election 2026: John Cavanaugh concedes Nebraska's 2nd Congressional District Democratic race
NE.summary: State Sen. John Cavanaugh formally conceded the closely contested NE-02 Democratic primary to Denise Powell after final ballot counts from Douglas County clarified the margin, with Powell advancing to the November general election.

NM.title: As expanded early voting opens, most New Mexico independents choose Democratic ballot
NM.summary: With expanded early voting beginning May 16, 75.6% of independent voters in New Mexico's first-ever semi-open primary have chosen Democratic ballots; Democrats account for 62% of the 27,351 total votes cast statewide so far.

NM.title: New Mexico independents largely picking Democratic ballots in state's first semi-open primary
NM.summary: Independent voters are participating at a lower rate than party-affiliated voters in New Mexico's inaugural semi-open primary, with analysts pointing to the competitive Democratic governor's race as the main draw for independents selecting a Democratic ballot.

NM.title: Early Voting expands on Saturday
NM.summary: New Mexico expanded early voting to alternate locations beyond county clerk offices starting May 16, running through May 30 ahead of the June 2 primary, with same-day voter registration available at all in-person voting sites.

ND.title: Statewide candidates, voters hold bipartisan forum discussing energy, agriculture issues
ND.summary: Republican and Democratic candidates challenging incumbent statewide officeholders gathered for a bipartisan voter forum in Lincoln, ND, drawing nearly 75 attendees ahead of the June 9 primary, with candidates for U.S. House, Public Service Commission, and secretary of state participating.

OH.title: Catching our eye: News roundup, May 14, 2026
OH.summary: Ohio Capital Journal's May 14 news roundup covers Ohio Democrats in Congress sending a letter to Secretary of State Frank LaRose demanding he explain what sensitive voter registration data for nearly 8 million Ohioans was shared with the federal government and under what legal authority.

OR.title: Your guide to ballot drop sites, big issues, races Oregonians to decide on Tuesday
OR.summary: Pre-election voter guide covering official ballot drop-box locations, Ballot Measure 120, and the contested Republican gubernatorial primary ahead of Oregon's May 19 primary, with key information on returning ballots by the 8 p.m. deadline.

PA.title: How Pennsylvania's May 19 primary is going so far
PA.summary: Spotlight PA's overview of mail ballot administration problems across Pennsylvania counties, with election officials bracing for lower-than-usual turnout given uncontested top-of-ticket races and hot weather on primary day.

PA.title: Here's what is happening in Pennsylvania ahead of this week's election
PA.summary: Pre-primary roundup covering mail ballot errors in multiple Pennsylvania counties affecting thousands of voters — including 4,000-plus in Lehigh County and wrong-district ballots in York County — plus Luzerne County's switch to hand-marked paper ballots.

RI.title: US Supreme Court ruling heightens the need for a R.I. Voting Rights Act, advocates say
RI.summary: Following the Supreme Court's ruling gutting federal Voting Rights Act minority-district protections, Rhode Island advocates and legislators are pressing for passage of a state Voting Rights Act (S 3143 / H 8334) to preserve anti-discrimination voter protections at the state level.

TX.title: May 26 Primary Runoff Election: Your TPR guide to voting in San Antonio and Texas
TX.summary: Comprehensive voter guide for the May 26 Texas primary runoff covering early voting dates (May 18-22), the marquee Cornyn vs. Paxton U.S. Senate contest, and party restrictions on runoff eligibility.

TX.title: Travis County voter guide for May 26 primary runoff election
TX.summary: Voter guide for Travis County detailing polling locations, early voting schedule (May 18-22), and contested races in the May 26 Texas primary runoff election.

TX.title: Texas primary runoff: Key races on the May 26 ballot
TX.summary: Covers the major statewide races in the May 26 primary runoff, including the Cornyn vs. Paxton Republican U.S. Senate contest, with details on voter eligibility and party crossover restrictions.

VA.title: Virginia Democrats who lost redistricting fight still look to flip seats
VA.summary: Following the U.S. Supreme Court's denial of Virginia Democrats' emergency redistricting appeal on May 15, state Democrats assess their strategy to flip congressional seats in November under the existing GOP-favorable map.

VT.title: Vermont Supreme Court upholds Burlington noncitizen voting in school elections
VT.summary: The Vermont Supreme Court issued a split ruling affirming Burlington's charter amendment allowing noncitizens to vote in local school budget elections does not violate the state constitution's voter-eligibility requirements.

WA.title: Federal judge asked to ditch WA legislative district maps
WA.summary: Challengers filed a motion asking a federal judge to throw out Washington state's legislative district maps drawn in 2024, arguing the recent U.S. Supreme Court ruling in Louisiana v. Callais undermines the legal basis used to create them.

WI.title: Judge orders Madison to count 23 late-arriving absentee ballots in state Supreme Court race
WI.summary: A Dane County judge ruled that 23 absentee ballots that arrived late to Madison polling places during the April 7 Wisconsin Supreme Court election must be counted, overturning a Wisconsin Elections Commission order to exclude them.

WY.title: Casper City Council candidate filing period opens May 14
WY.summary: Wyoming's statewide candidate filing period opened May 14 for state, county, and municipal offices ahead of the August 18 primary, with Casper City Council among the local races open for candidate filing through May 29.

AL.title: Alabama state primary elections 2026: A voter guide to the race
AL.summary: Comprehensive voter guide for Alabama's May 19 primary election covering key races for governor and U.S. Senate, published amid a congressional redistricting fight that has split primaries between May 19 and an August 11 special election for four districts affected by the Supreme Court's reversal of an injunction against the state's 2023 map.

AZ.title: Injunction Sought in Arizona Elections Manual 'Punishing' Political Speech Lawsuit
AZ.summary: Voters filed for a preliminary injunction against Arizona's 2025 Election Procedures Manual, alleging provisions empower election workers to remove or arrest people near polling locations based on political speech or apparel — echoing Ninth Circuit precedent from 2025 that enjoined similar provisions in the prior EPM.

AR.title: Arkansas ballot measure groups remain optimistic ahead of petition deadline
AR.summary: Three ballot initiative campaigns are racing to collect signatures to qualify for the November 2026 ballot before the July 3 deadline, including two competing direct-democracy reform amendments aimed at protecting citizen initiative rights that have been curtailed by GOP-led legislation in recent years.

CA.title: Amid rising fears of rolling back voter rights, Black lawmakers announce new Voting Rights Act for California
CA.summary: California's Black Legislative Caucus announced a new state Voting Rights Act that would strengthen protections against voter suppression and vote dilution, expand language access for limited-English proficient voters, and provide new enforcement tools for the state Attorney General — introduced in response to the Supreme Court's ruling weakening the federal VRA in Louisiana v. Callais.

CO.title: 'Federal overreach' inspired these Colorado bills during the 2026 session
CO.summary: A summary of Colorado's 2026 legislative session election bills driven by concerns about federal interference, including HB 1113 which extends the mail ballot window from 22 to 29 days before Election Day to guard against postal delays, adds election disruption emergency powers, and bans election-offense convicts from serving as poll watchers.

CT.title: Here's what CT's 2026 'emergency certified' bill means for towns
CT.summary: Connecticut's 2026 emergency-certified omnibus bill includes a significant change to early voting procedures: early voters must now insert their ballots directly into a tabulator instead of sealing them in envelopes, enabling daily vote counts, faster results, and reduced opportunities for tampering.

DC.title: How D.C. is teaching residents about ranked-choice voting
DC.summary: DC election officials and community organizations launched a voter education campaign ahead of the District's historic first use of ranked-choice voting in the June 16 primary, logging over 130 educational sessions at high schools, neighborhood meetings, and online forums, with outreach targeting older and low-propensity voters.

GA.title: In Georgia primary, Republicans dominate spending and Democrats drive record turnout
GA.summary: Ahead of Georgia's May 19 primary, over one million voters cast early ballots — a record for a Georgia primary — with Democrats outpacing Republicans by roughly 15 percentage points. Many marquee races, including the Republican Senate primary to challenge Sen. Jon Ossoff, are expected to head to June runoffs.

IA.title: The Supreme Court avoids taking up a fight over Voting Rights Act enforcement for now
IA.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court declined to take up a new Voting Rights Act enforcement case, leaving unresolved questions about Section 2 challenges following Louisiana v. Callais, which raised the bar for proving racial discrimination in redistricting — a ruling with implications for redistricting challenges nationally, including in Iowa.

IA.title: Why the Supreme Court's voting rights ruling could play a big role at the local level
IA.summary: Following the Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais decision narrowing the Voting Rights Act, at least 17 active legal fights over state and local voting maps now face a higher bar for proving minority vote dilution — affecting redistricting law and local election systems across the country, including in Iowa.

ID.title: AP Decision Notes: What to expect in Idaho's primaries
ID.summary: The AP previews Idaho's May 19 primary, covering contests for governor, both U.S. House seats, one U.S. Senate seat, and all 105 state legislative districts. The Republican Party holds a closed primary while the Democratic primary is open to all registered voters.

IL.title: How the Supreme Court's voting rights decision could impact Illinois and explaining Dick Durbin's 'John Lewis Voting Rights Act'
IL.summary: The Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais ruling has direct Illinois implications: state Democrats shelved a planned redistricting constitutional amendment, and a new federal lawsuit challenges the Illinois Voting Rights Act as an unconstitutional racial gerrymander under the ruling's tightened standard.

KS.title: Trump administration promotes program to check voter eligibility. Critics fear a midterm purge
KS.summary: The Trump administration is promoting expanded use of the SAVE database to check voter rolls for noncitizens ahead of the 2026 midterms. Kansas, which enacted the SAVE Kansas Act, is among the states formally using the system; critics warn the effort could wrongly flag eligible citizens for removal before November.

KY.title: Massie, Gallrein and more candidates make final pleas to Kentucky voters ahead of primary
KY.summary: Candidates in Kentucky's May 19 primary made final pitches to voters ahead of the open U.S. Senate race and competitive House contests, with record early voter turnout reported statewide before Election Day.

KY.title: Kentucky sees record early voting turnout ahead of primary election
KY.summary: Jefferson County set a record for early primary voting with 23,575 ballots cast, and Secretary of State Michael Adams reported 57,380 Kentuckians voted early on Friday — a 75% increase over the comparable point in the 2022 primary cycle, signaling high engagement ahead of the May 19 primary.

MN.title: Minnesota lawmakers race to pass bills before end of session on Sunday
MN.summary: Minnesota lawmakers scrambled to pass remaining legislation before the session's Sunday deadline, including a state government and elections omnibus bill that modifies absentee voting procedures and allocates $3.86 million for elections administration in the 2026-27 biennium.

MN.title: Minnesota Legislature closing out on 2026 session with marquee bills still up in the air
MN.summary: The 2026 Minnesota legislative session concluded with the House and Senate passing a state government and elections bill that includes changes to absentee ballot application requirements, chain-of-custody plans for election materials, and new identity verification requirements for absentee voters.

MO.title: Missouri's 2026 legislative session leaves abortion and income tax decisions to voters
MO.summary: The Missouri legislature ended its 2026 session sending several major measures to voters in November, including a constitutional amendment that would raise the threshold for citizen-led ballot initiatives to pass, which could affect how voters use direct democracy to make election-related law.

MO.title: 6 takeaways from a less contentious 2026 Missouri legislative session
MO.summary: Missouri's legislative session concluded May 16 having passed a wide-ranging elections bill (HB1871) and referred multiple constitutional amendments to voters, including one that would require approval in each congressional district for citizen-initiated constitutional amendments — a change that could limit future ballot initiative campaigns.

MS.title: Mississippi redistricting woes make Bennie Thompson safe
MS.summary: Gov. Tate Reeves abandoned plans to call a special legislative session to redraw Mississippi's congressional districts, which he had sought partly to eliminate the majority-Black 2nd Congressional District; the delay means redistricting will not affect the 2026 elections.

MS.title: FAQ: Mississippi redistricting. Why does it matter? What's being considered?
MS.summary: Mississippi Today explains the redistricting fight unfolding in Mississippi, where state leaders are weighing how to redraw congressional, legislative, and judicial districts following the Supreme Court's weakening of the Voting Rights Act, with recommendations expected from study committees before the 2027 session.

MS.title: US Supreme Court reverses ruling against Mississippi legislative redistricting
MS.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court vacated a federal district court ruling that had found Mississippi's state legislative maps violated the Voting Rights Act by diluting Black voting power, sending the case back to lower courts to reconsider under the new standard set in Louisiana v. Callais.

MT.title: Buttigieg rallies for Montana election initiative, stays mum on political plans
MT.summary: Former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg appeared in Butte to campaign for Montana Initiative 194, a proposed ballot measure that would ban corporations from contributing to state and local candidate and ballot measure campaigns; signature gatherers have until July 17 to qualify for the November ballot.

MT.title: 2026 Primary Election: A Northwest Montana Voter's Guide to Local and Statewide Races
MT.summary: With Montana's June 2 primary approaching, the Flathead Beacon published a comprehensive voter guide covering local and statewide races, noting that write-in lines have been removed from primary ballots for the first time under a new 2025 state law requiring write-in candidates to declare in advance.

ND.title: Supreme Court tosses racial redistricting rulings in Mississippi and North Dakota
ND.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court vacated federal court rulings in both Mississippi and North Dakota that had found state legislative maps violated the Voting Rights Act by diluting minority voting power, ordering lower courts to reconsider the cases under the weakened standard from Louisiana v. Callais.

ND.title: Why the Supreme Court's voting rights ruling could play a big role at the local level
ND.summary: NPR's analysis finds at least 17 active legal fights over voting maps that must now reckon with the Supreme Court's ruling in Louisiana v. Callais, including the North Dakota tribal redistricting case involving the Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa and Spirit Lake Nation.

NH.title: Why the Supreme Court's voting rights ruling could play a big role at the local level
NH.summary: NHPR reports that the Supreme Court's ruling weakening the Voting Rights Act threatens the power of minority voters in at least 17 state and local governments, with active legal fights over voting maps now shaped by the new, harder-to-prove intentional-discrimination standard.

OR.title: Oregon's primary features packed governor's race, a gas tax hike and more
OR.summary: OPB previews Oregon's May 19 vote-by-mail primary election, with nearly 513,000 ballots already cast; voters will weigh in on a crowded Republican governor's race and Measure 120, which would raise gas taxes and vehicle fees to fund transportation infrastructure.

RI.title: The Supreme Court avoids taking up a fight over Voting Rights Act enforcement for now
RI.summary: The Supreme Court declined on May 18 to rule on whether private individuals can sue under Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, leaving enforcement questions unresolved and reinforcing advocates' calls for Rhode Island to pass its own state-level voting rights act.

RI.title: Why the Supreme Court's voting rights ruling could play a big role at the local level
RI.summary: NPR reports that the Supreme Court's VRA Section 2 ruling threatens at least 17 state and local voting maps, raising pressure on states including Rhode Island — which has introduced a state-level Voting Rights Act — to enact their own protections for minority voters.

SC.title: Redistricting debate shifts to South Carolina as Republicans seek clean sweep of US House seats
SC.summary: South Carolina's legislature began a special session to consider mid-decade congressional redistricting that would eliminate the state's only majority-minority district held by Rep. Jim Clyburn, potentially giving Republicans a 7-0 sweep of the state's U.S. House seats.

TN.title: Election officials move quickly to adjust districts for August primary in Tennessee
TN.summary: Tennessee county election administrators are racing to update voter rolls and notify affected constituents after the legislature passed a new congressional map on May 7, splitting the state's only majority-Black district ahead of the August 6 primary.

TN.title: Who's running in Tennessee's new 2026 U.S. Congress races
TN.summary: Following Tennessee's congressional redistricting that split Rep. Steve Cohen's Memphis district across three Republican-leaning areas, this roundup tracks which candidates confirmed their new districts ahead of the May 15 qualifying deadline.

TX.title: What to know about voting early in the 2026 Texas primary runoff election in Bexar County
TX.summary: Early voting for the May 26 Texas primary runoff opened May 18 through May 22, with high-profile contests including the Republican U.S. Senate race between incumbent John Cornyn and challenger Ken Paxton.

TX.title: Here are the key races in Texas' May primary runoff election
TX.summary: Texas voters head back to the polls May 26 for 38 primary runoff races, including the Republican U.S. Senate contest between Cornyn and Paxton and runoffs for attorney general and lieutenant governor.

TX.title: Early voting begins May 18 across Coastal Bend for Texas primary runoff election
TX.summary: Early voting opened statewide on May 18 for the May 26 Texas primary runoff, covering races where no candidate cleared 50 percent in the March 3 primary.

VA.title: Spanberger says the midterm elections will be under the old maps
VA.summary: Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger confirmed the 2026 congressional elections will proceed using the current 2021 maps after the U.S. Supreme Court declined to reinstate the voter-approved Democratic redistricting plan, ending the months-long legal fight.

VT.title: Vermonters will vote on equal protection amendment to state constitution this fall
VT.summary: The Vermont House gave final approval to Proposal 4, a constitutional amendment guaranteeing equal protection regardless of race, sex, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, and other characteristics; voters will decide it on November 3.

WI.title: Republicans call for unity, endorse Tom Tiffany, at annual state convention
WI.summary: The Republican Party of Wisconsin unanimously endorsed Rep. Tom Tiffany for governor at its May 15-17 state convention, calling for unity after a 20-point loss in the April Wisconsin Supreme Court election.

WI.title: At annual convention, Wisconsin GOP's old guard urges party to engage young voters
WI.summary: At the Republican Party of Wisconsin's state convention, veteran Republicans urged expanded outreach to younger voters ahead of November midterm elections, citing polling showing Democrats leading among under-30 voters 45 to 26 percent.

WV.title: Judge Copenhaver Dies And The Primary Wraps Up, This West Virginia Week
WV.summary: West Virginia Public Broadcasting's weekly roundup covers the conclusion of the May 12 primary election, where 20.9 percent of registered voters cast ballots in the state's first election requiring photo ID, with Sen. Shelley Moore Capito winning her Republican primary.

WY.title: How one Wyoming county is preparing to hand count ballots
WY.summary: Wyoming counties are assembling audit boards ahead of the August 18 primary to manually count 5 percent of ballots under a new state law, requiring comparison of hand-count results to electronic voting machine totals for at least one federal and one statewide race.

AK.title: Alaska Legislature rejects Gov. Mike Dunleavy's pick for attorney general
AK.summary: Alaska lawmakers voted 29-31 to reject Gov. Dunleavy's attorney general appointee Stephen Cox, partly over his role assisting the state in releasing voter rolls to the federal government and his failure to support the state's absentee voting program.

AK.title: Alaska Legislature rejects Dunleavy's pick for attorney general, Stephen Cox
AK.summary: The Alaska Legislature voted 29-31 to deny confirmation to acting AG Stephen Cox; legislators cited Cox's support for turning over state voter rolls to federal authorities and his refusal to support the state's absentee voting program as key reasons for rejection.

AK.title: Alaska U.S. Senate candidate Mary Peltola calls for congressional term limits
AK.summary: Democratic Senate challenger Mary Peltola rallied in Juneau to announce a platform plank calling for 12-year congressional term limits and stricter campaign finance rules, as she campaigns against Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan ahead of Alaska's August 18 nonpartisan primary.

AL.title: Alabama announces special primary elections for four U.S. House races, New Hampshire moves 2028 primary date
AL.summary: Alabama announced special primary elections scheduled for August 11 for four U.S. House districts after the U.S. Supreme Court cleared the way for the state to use its previously blocked 2023 congressional map.

CA.title: Southern California voters urged to register by Monday for Primary Election
CA.summary: California Secretary of State Shirley Weber urged voters to register by May 18 for the June 2 primary, the last day to receive a mail ballot; eligible voters who miss the deadline may still cast ballots through conditional same-day registration at in-person voting locations.

CA.title: California Secretary of State reminds voters of midnight online voter registration deadline for June 2, 2026, Primary Election
CA.summary: The California Secretary of State issued a reminder that May 18 is the midnight deadline to register online to vote in the June 2, 2026 primary election; the state has 3,546 polling locations, 2,758 drop-box locations, and 1,988 early voting sites statewide.

DC.title: Fact check: Donation and voting record claims surface at DC mayoral debate
DC.summary: Fox 5 DC fact-checked claims made during the DC Democratic mayoral primary debate—the first held under DC's new ranked-choice voting system ahead of the June 16 primary—including candidates' voting records and campaign donation sources.

FL.title: Why the Supreme Court's voting rights ruling could play a big role at the local level
FL.summary: WGCU reported how the Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais decision weakening Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act is affecting at least 17 active voting-map and election-system legal fights in Florida and other states, with Republican-led states racing to redraw congressional maps.

GA.title: Election coverage: The latest on Georgia's primary elections, judicial races
GA.summary: Live coverage of Georgia's May 19 primary election covering more than 1,275 races, including the crowded Republican gubernatorial and U.S. Senate primaries and contested nonpartisan Georgia Supreme Court races that drew heightened attention following the Supreme Court's ruling weakening the Voting Rights Act.

GA.title: Georgia's 2026 Primary Election: Live results and updates from GPB News
GA.summary: Georgia Public Broadcasting provided live election-day results for the May 19 primary, covering Republican primaries for governor and U.S. Senate, the Democratic gubernatorial field led by former Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms, and closely watched state Supreme Court races.

GA.title: Georgia primary could be the starting gun for Democratic and Republican runoffs
GA.summary: With Georgia's law requiring a majority to win outright, multiple crowded primaries are expected to send top-two finishers into a June 16 runoff, including the Republican U.S. Senate primary and the open governor's race on both sides.

ID.title: Here are Idaho's 2026 primary election results
ID.summary: Idaho held its May 19 primary with Sen. Jim Risch seeking a fourth term against three Republican challengers, Gov. Brad Little running for a third term, and incumbents Russ Fulcher and Mike Simpson defending their House seats in the state's closed party primaries.
