MI.summary: Starting June 1, Michiganders automatically registered to vote at a Secretary of State branch office will receive a mailed opt-out notice, bringing the department into compliance with state election law. The change fulfills Michigan's 2018 constitutional mandate for automatic voter registration while allowing residents to decline registration.

MI.title: Michigan opens voting for 2026 'I Voted' sticker contest
MI.summary: Michigan's Secretary of State opened public voting June 1–30 for the 2026 'I Voted' sticker contest, which drew more than 2,000 submissions. Winning designs will be distributed to local election clerks for use at polling places during the November 2026 general election.

MN.title: Secretary Simon Highlights 2026 Election Dates as Candidate Filing Period Closes
MN.summary: Minnesota's candidate filing period for state and federal offices closes June 2, and absentee voting for the August 11 primary opens June 26. Secretary Simon reminded voters that advance registration by July 21 avoids Election Day lines, with same-day registration also available.

MT.title: Why Tuesday's primary matters — maybe even more than November
MT.summary: Montana Free Press analyzed the high stakes of the June 2 primary, with open U.S. Senate and House seats drawing crowded fields and new voter ID requirements alongside court-preserved Election Day registration reshaping turnout expectations.

MT.title: The June primary election is underway in Montana
MT.summary: Montana voters went to the polls June 2 to select nominees for state and federal offices under new photo ID requirements, while a court order continues to preserve Election Day voter registration after a judge blocked a Republican-backed restriction law.

MT.title: Haven't voted in Montana's primary election yet? Here's how
MT.summary: The Daily Montanan published a practical voting guide for the June 2 Montana primary, covering new photo ID requirements, the court-preserved Election Day registration option, and the new rule requiring mail ballot return envelopes to include the voter's birth year.

NC.title: Old North State Report – May 29, 2026
NC.summary: North Carolina voters will decide in November on multiple constitutional amendments passed by Republican legislators, including a property tax revenue cap and a state income tax rate ceiling of 3.5%. The amendments are expected to appear alongside competitive congressional and legislative races on the November ballot.

ND.title: Early Voting Opens for the June 9 Primaries in North Dakota
ND.summary: Early voting opened June 1 across North Dakota for the June 9 primary, with 20,050 of 36,866 requested absentee ballots already returned. Officials remind voters that under a new state law eliminating the prior 13-day grace period, all mail ballots must arrive by poll close on Election Day to count.

ND.title: Early voting for June 9 primary and Fargo city election starts Tuesday
ND.summary: In-person early voting opened in Cass County on June 2 for North Dakota's statewide primary and the Fargo city election, where voters will decide mayoral and commission races and a ballot question on continuing the city's 1% Infrastructure Sales Tax.

NJ.title: New Jersey election 2026: Primary voters are heading to the polls. Here's what to know
NJ.summary: New Jersey's closed primary is underway June 2 with polls open 6 a.m.–8 p.m. Voters choose nominees in all 12 U.S. House races and a contested Republican Senate primary; four GOP candidates compete to face incumbent Democratic Sen. Cory Booker in November.

NJ.title: Live updates: Polls open for the New Jersey Primary Election
NJ.summary: New Jersey primary polls opened June 2 with notable races including 14 candidates in the 12th Congressional District and a competitive 7th District contest. Mail ballots must be received by June 8 if postmarked by Election Day, or by June 4 if not postmarked.

NM.title: Polls open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Tuesday for New Mexico primary election
NM.summary: New Mexico holds its first semi-open primary on June 2, allowing unaffiliated voters to choose a major party ballot without changing registration under Senate Bill 16 enacted in 2025. Nearly 140,000 voters cast early ballots ahead of Election Day.

NY.title: 2026 primary elections in New York: What you need to know about registration, absentees and early voting
NY.summary: Comprehensive voter guide for New York's June 23 primary covering registration deadlines (June 13), early voting period (June 13–21), and absentee ballot rules. More than 1,160 offices are on the ballot in this closed primary, including congressional and statewide races.

OH.title: If Ohio's the election 'gold standard,' why are lawmakers going for desperate, duplicative changes?
OH.summary: Ohio Republicans are fast-tracking a constitutional amendment to enshrine the state's existing voter photo ID law in the state constitution, despite it being law since 2023. Critics say the move is redundant and politically motivated, with Ramaswamy and GOP leaders seeking to put it on the November ballot by mid-June.

OH.title: Ohio photo voter ID amendment prompts pushback across political spectrum
OH.summary: More than 80 witnesses submitted testimony on Ohio's proposed voter photo ID constitutional amendment; only two supported it and neither appeared in person. Opponents include voting rights advocates concerned the measure lacks the free ID provision in current law, potentially constituting a poll tax.

OH.title: Republicans deny juicing votes as they attempt to put already existing law on midterm ballot
OH.summary: Ohio GOP leaders deny that placing an existing voter photo ID law on the November ballot as a constitutional amendment is a turnout-boosting strategy, framing it as protection against future rollback. Senate President McColley, running for lieutenant governor on the Ramaswamy ticket, is pushing the effort.

OK.title: In deeply red Oklahoma, minimum wage's biggest 2026 election cycle fight is about to be decided
OK.summary: State Question 832, appearing on Oklahoma's June 16 primary ballot, would raise the state's minimum wage from $7.25 to $15 an hour by 2029, with economic analysts estimating the change would boost wages for about one-fifth of the state's workforce.

OK.title: Thousands of Oklahomans switched party affiliation ahead of primary elections
OK.summary: More than 13,000 Oklahoma voters changed their party affiliation ahead of the state's closed June 16 primary, with independents comprising the largest shifting group. All recognized parties have kept their 2026 primaries closed to unaffiliated voters.

SC.title: EARLY VOTING TRACKER: Record turnout continues for SC primaries
SC.summary: South Carolina's early voting for the June 9 primary surpassed the entire 2024 early voting total within the first week, with more than 151,670 ballots cast. Richland, Charleston, and Greenville counties led the state in turnout, with early voting continuing through June 5.

SC.title: South Carolina sees record early voting surge ahead of primary day
SC.summary: South Carolina continued to shatter early voting records ahead of its June 9 primary, with nearly 120,000 ballots cast as of June 1 and the early voting period set to close June 5.

SD.title: Election Day brings possible runoff drama in South Dakota governor primary
SD.summary: South Dakota voters headed to the polls June 2 in a tightly contested four-way Republican gubernatorial primary, with pre-election polls placing all candidates in the 20s and raising the prospect of the state's first runoff since 1985 if no one clears the 35% threshold.

TN.title: Plaintiffs vow appeal after Tennessee court dismisses congressional maps challenge
TN.summary: Following a state three-judge panel's dismissal of the NAACP's challenge to Tennessee's redrawn congressional maps, plaintiffs vowed to appeal, while three separate federal lawsuits against the maps that split majority-Black Memphis into three districts remain pending ahead of the August 6 primary.

TX.title: Republicans brace for money problems in Texas after Ken Paxton's win
TX.summary: National Republicans are alarmed by Ken Paxton's fundraising weakness following his May 26 Senate runoff win, with Paxton holding only $2.3 million while Democrat James Talarico has raised over $40 million, potentially forcing the GOP to spend $100 million or more in Texas and divert resources from other states.

UT.title: Rural Utah takes center stage as Maloy, Lyman battle for 3rd District GOP nomination
UT.summary: Incumbent Rep. Celeste Maloy and challenger Phil Lyman debated June 1 ahead of Utah's June 23 primary, with the redrawn 3rd Congressional District drawing attention as Democrats eye the neighboring new District 1 as a potential pickup under the court-ordered redistricting map.

UT.title: Maloy, Lyman talk ICE, data centers in debate for Utah's new 3rd Congressional District
UT.summary: Utah's 3rd District Republican candidates Celeste Maloy and Phil Lyman clashed over ICE detention, data centers, and public lands in a primary debate, with the winner set to face Democrat Kent Udell in November under court-ordered maps.

UT.title: It's not too late to register to vote in Utah's primary election
UT.summary: With primary ballots beginning to mail June 2, Utah election officials reminded voters that registration remains open through June 12 online or by mail and through Election Day June 23 in person, covering 383 races from U.S. House to local school boards.

VA.title: 5th district will have both a Democratic and Republican congressional primary in August
VA.summary: Virginia's 5th Congressional District is the only one with primaries for both major parties on August 4, 2026, with three Democrats competing and Republican incumbent John McGuire facing a challenger. Independents still have until June 16 to file for the fall ballot.

VT.title: Legislative session wrap-up
VT.summary: Vermont Public covers the close of the 2026 legislative session, highlighting lawmakers' approval of a constitutional equal-protection amendment (PR.4) that will go to voters in November 2026, and the opening of the election season with multiple candidates filing for governor and other statewide offices.

WI.title: Wisconsin governor's race filing deadline arrives with no Democratic dropouts
WI.summary: As Wisconsin's June 1 nomination paper filing deadline passed, all seven major Democratic candidates for governor remained in the race, setting up a wide-open August 11 primary. Republican Tom Tiffany, backed by former President Trump, faces only one GOP opponent.

WV.title: Harrison County affirms McNeely as Republican nominee for District 71
WV.summary: Harrison County officials confirmed Tim McNeely as the Republican nominee for the West Virginia House of Delegates District 71 seat after a daylong recount showed he defeated incumbent Del. Laura Kimble by six votes, matching the canvassed margin from the May 12 primary.

WV.title: McNeely stays on top after recount in Harrison House race
WV.summary: A full recount in West Virginia's House District 71 Republican primary confirmed Tim McNeely defeated incumbent Del. Laura Kimble by six votes, preserving canvassed results from the May 12 primary; McNeely will face Democrat Robert Garcia in November.

WV.title: McNeely looks toward November vote after recount victory
WV.summary: Tim McNeely said he is now focused on the November general election after his six-vote recount victory over incumbent Del. Laura Kimble in the West Virginia House District 71 Republican primary.

WY.title: Wyoming's primaries are crowded. These are the races to watch
WY.summary: With candidate filing closed May 29, Wyoming faces a crowded August 18 primary featuring about a dozen candidates for the sole U.S. House seat, competitive governor and secretary of state races, and roughly 20 state legislative districts where Freedom Caucus incumbents face challengers.

AL.title: A new congressional map is enacted in Louisiana, blocked in Alabama, and dead in South Carolina
AL.summary: A federal court blocked Alabama's Legislature-drawn congressional map as a racial gerrymander, with the case going to the Supreme Court; if Alabama's map takes effect, the state's U.S. House delegation would shift from a 5-2 to a 6-1 Republican-Democrat split.

AR.title: Pulaski County data center fight — District 44's special election
AR.summary: Election Day coverage of the Arkansas House District 44 special primary on June 2, 2026, called to fill the vacancy after Rep. Stan Berry's death; a Pulaski County data center dispute emerged as a key campaign issue among the four Republican candidates.

AR.title: Here's who is winning in the Arkansas special election races
AR.summary: Live vote-count results from the Arkansas House District 44 special primary on June 2, 2026; official results are to be certified by county election commissioners by June 12, with a potential runoff scheduled for June 30.

CT.title: Glastonbury trends blue, and a moderate Democrat is rejected
CT.summary: A Democratic state representative in Glastonbury's 31st House District lost the party's endorsement to a progressive challenger in a local caucus, highlighting intra-party dynamics ahead of Connecticut's August 11, 2026 primary.

CT.title: Judge: CT Democrat Who Received More Votes Than Opponent Must Be Awarded Town Council Seat
CT.summary: A Connecticut Superior Court judge ruled that South Windsor Democrat Harrison Amadasun must be seated on the town council after receiving more votes than any Republican, in a case turning on a disputed charter change that altered majority-representation rules after the election.

DC.title: How D.C. is teaching residents about ranked-choice voting
DC.summary: The D.C. Board of Elections has held over 30 voter education sessions since January to prepare residents for the District's first use of ranked-choice voting in the June 16 primary, with targeted outreach to older voters who research shows are more likely to struggle with the new system.

DC.title: New poll shows tight race in DC mayoral primary with Lewis George leading McDuffie
DC.summary: A City Cast DC poll shows Councilmember Janeese Lewis George leading the Democratic mayoral primary at 39% to Kenyan McDuffie's 34%, with McDuffie holding a meaningful lead in second-choice rankings under DC's new ranked-choice voting system.

DC.title: 2026 Election Guide: Everything DC voters need to know ahead of 2 June 16 elections
DC.summary: Comprehensive guide to DC's June 16 primary and simultaneous special election, covering ranked-choice voting procedures, mail ballot deadlines, and candidate fields for mayor, at-large council, attorney general, and the special election to fill Kenyan McDuffie's vacated council seat.

FL.title: Florida mail-in ballot requests lag ahead of August primary
FL.summary: Voting rights advocates warn that Florida mail-in ballot requests are significantly below prior cycles because all previous requests expired and must be renewed under a 2021 state law requiring renewal each election cycle — a barrier particularly affecting seniors and people with disabilities ahead of the August 18 primary.

GA.title: Voter engagement pushes ahead of Georgia's runoff elections
GA.summary: Voter outreach efforts are ramping up ahead of Georgia's June 16 primary runoff elections for governor and U.S. Senate, with early voting set to begin June 6-8 depending on county, as high-profile Republican runoffs drive engagement campaigns.

IA.title: Live Iowa primary election results 2026 for Senate, House and governor
IA.summary: Iowa held its 2026 primary election on June 2, with voters choosing nominees for U.S. Senate, governor, and congressional seats; key races include the Democratic Senate primary between Josh Turek and Zach Wahls, and Rep. Randy Feenstra in the Trump-endorsed Republican governor race.

IA.title: Tuesday is a big primary day. Here are key races to watch
IA.summary: NPR's election day coverage highlights Iowa's June 2 primaries, with the Democratic Senate primary and Republican governor race identified as the top races; Iowa's open Senate seat is seen as a potential Democratic pickup opportunity.

IA.title: Three Democrats compete for Iowa's 2nd Congressional District nomination
IA.summary: Three Democratic candidates — Lindsay James, Clint Twedt-Ball, and Kathy Dolter — are competing in Iowa's 2nd Congressional District primary on June 2, vying for the nomination to replace Rep. Ashley Hinson, who is running for U.S. Senate.

IA.title: Iowa 2026 live primary election results
IA.summary: ABC News provides live results coverage for Iowa's June 2 primary elections, tracking races for U.S. Senate, governor, and congressional districts as polls closed at 8 p.m. CT.

IA.title: Live Results: Iowa midterm primaries
IA.summary: PBS NewsHour tracks live results from Iowa's June 2 midterm primary elections, covering the competitive Senate and governor races that will determine the fall ballot for Iowa's most consequential 2026 contests.

KS.title: Candidates officially file for Kansas governor's race, bringing total to 10
KS.summary: The June 1 filing deadline finalized a field of 10 candidates for Kansas governor, including Overland Park Mayor Curt Skoog joining the Democratic primary; former Governor Jeff Colyer notably failed to file despite having announced his campaign weeks earlier.

KS.title: Filing deadline for 2026 elections has passed: here's the slate for statewide and Douglas County races
KS.summary: Kansas's June 1 filing deadline closed the candidate field for all 2026 races including governor, U.S. Senate, all four U.S. House seats, and every seat in the Kansas House, with the primary set for August 4.

KS.title: Who's running for Kansas governor? The field is officially set
KS.summary: Following the June 1 filing deadline, KCUR reviews the full field of Kansas gubernatorial candidates — three Democrats and multiple Republicans vying to succeed term-limited Governor Laura Kelly in the November election.

KY.title: Kentucky AG to hold draw for post-election inquiries on Tuesday
KY.summary: Kentucky Attorney General Russell Coleman will hold a random draw to select 12 counties for mandatory post-primary reviews following the May 19 primary, after the AG's office received 154 election-law complaints on primary day.

KY.title: Barr vs. Booker: Candidates in Kentucky's U.S. Senate race advance to November election
KY.summary: Post-primary analysis of the Kentucky U.S. Senate matchup: Trump-backed Republican Andy Barr will face Democratic nominee Charles Booker for the open seat vacated by retiring Sen. Mitch McConnell in November.

LA.title: A new congressional map is enacted in Louisiana, blocked in Alabama, and dead in South Carolina
LA.summary: Louisiana enacted a new congressional map signed by Gov. Jeff Landry that eliminates one of the state's two majority-Black districts, shifting the expected congressional delegation from a 4-2 to a 5-1 Republican-Democrat split; the map follows the Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais ruling and is expected to face immediate legal challenges.

MA.title: Mass. voters might face 11 ballot questions this fall. Here's where each measure stands.
MA.summary: As Massachusetts ballot initiative campaigns enter the final stretch to collect second-round signatures by June 17, the article surveys all 11 certified measures including same-day voter registration, nonpartisan primaries, and a voter ID proposal, several of which also face court challenges.

MD.title: Hale calls for color-coded mulligan on mail-in ballot mix-up
MD.summary: Maryland state officials respond to the fallout from a vendor error that sent wrong-party primary ballots to thousands of voters ahead of the June 23 primary, with calls for color-coded ballot envelopes to prevent future mix-ups.

MD.title: Tuesday is last day to change party affiliation for Maryland primary
MD.summary: June 2 is the final deadline for Maryland voters to change party affiliation or register ahead of the June 23 gubernatorial primary, as the state prepares for early voting starting June 11.

MD.title: When the primary is the real election, some Maryland voters change parties
MD.summary: In heavily Democratic jurisdictions like Baltimore City and Prince George's County, Republican and unaffiliated voters are switching party registrations ahead of the June 23 primary to influence races that are effectively decided before the general election.

MO.title: Missouri judge rejects effort to strike Kehoe's tax overhaul plan from the August ballot
MO.summary: A Cole County judge rejected a lawsuit seeking to remove Gov. Mike Kehoe's income tax overhaul ballot amendment from Missouri's August 4 primary, ruling the measure addressed a single central subject and its ballot summary was not misleading.

MO.title: Judge rejects effort to strike Kehoe's tax plan from the August primary ballot
MO.summary: Missouri's Amendment 5, which would allow the legislature to expand sales taxes to replace the income tax, will remain on the August 4 primary ballot after a Cole County judge rejected opponents' legal challenges on June 2.

MS.title: How the Callais Ruling Erased a Key Mississippi Voting Rights Victory
MS.summary: A federal appeals court vacated a ruling requiring Mississippi to redraw its Supreme Court judicial districts to give Black voters fairer representation, after the U.S. Supreme Court's Callais decision raised the bar for proving Voting Rights Act violations and eliminated the prospect of special state Supreme Court elections in 2026.

NC.title: North Carolina voters to decide on two measures on property and income tax limits in November
NC.summary: The North Carolina General Assembly referred two constitutional amendments to the November 3 ballot — one capping the income tax rate at 3.5% and another limiting property taxes — joining a previously referred photo voter ID amendment that NC voters will also decide on this fall.

ND.title: Early voting is underway in North Dakota
ND.summary: Cass and Grand Forks counties began in-person early voting on June 2, one week before North Dakota's June 9 primary; eight counties total are offering early voting options on staggered start dates.

NE.title: A new era for Nebraska elections is coming, but why did GOP voters pick Petersen over Evnen?
NE.summary: Analysis of why Nebraska Republican primary voters ousted two-term Secretary of State Bob Evnen in favor of Scott Petersen, who pledged to restrict mail voting and conduct hand counts; Democratic nominee Sarah Slattery says she is running to protect Nebraskans' voting rights.

NH.title: Deadline to Change Party Affiliation in New Hampshire: June 2, 2026
NH.summary: June 2 is the final day for New Hampshire voters to change party affiliation ahead of the September 8 primary; after the deadline, registered Democrats and Republicans are locked into their party primaries while undeclared voters may still choose.

NV.title: Turnout for Nevada's 2026 primary is low. Is it breaking any records?
NV.summary: Early voting turnout for Nevada's June 9 primary stands at about 8 percent as of early June, but is slightly up in Clark and Washoe counties compared to prior cycles, with Washoe County up roughly 30 percent from two years ago.

NV.title: Nevada Secretary of State's Office announces voter resources as early voting kicks off for June Primary election
NV.summary: The Nevada Secretary of State's Office announced voter resources including ballot tracking at MyBallot.NV.gov as in-person early voting commenced for the June 9 primary, with all active voters automatically receiving mail ballots.

NV.title: Nevada voters pick governor, 2nd Congressional District candidates in primary
NV.summary: Preview of Nevada's June 9 primary highlighting the governor's race between incumbent Joe Lombardo and Democratic frontrunner Aaron Ford, and the competitive 2nd Congressional District race that Democrats see as a pickup opportunity.

OH.title: How changes to Ohio's voting laws affected the May 2026 election
OH.summary: Ohio's May 5 primary was the first conducted after the legislature eliminated the mail ballot grace period, requiring ballots to be received — not just postmarked — by 7:30 p.m. on Election Day; the article examines how this change affected voter participation.

OK.title: Everything you need to know about Oklahoma primaries on June 16
OK.summary: A comprehensive guide to Oklahoma's June 16 primary covering more than 635 races from U.S. Senate and governor down to local judges, plus State Question 832 on raising the minimum wage, with early voting June 11-13.

OK.title: Oklahoma Voice launches voter guide ahead of June 16 primary election
OK.summary: Oklahoma Voice published its 2026 primary voter guide covering statewide and legislative candidates and the State Question 832 minimum wage ballot measure ahead of the June 16 partisan primary.

PA.title: PA primary election results: Gaming-targeted senators win
PA.summary: Three Pennsylvania Republican state senators targeted by skill-games industry money survived their primary challenges on May 19, 2026, as counties began official canvassing; gaming and gambling interests spent more than  million statewide ahead of the primary.

SC.title: South Carolina's Trump-backed redistricting push fails in the state Senate amid GOP opposition
SC.summary: The South Carolina Senate defeated a Trump-backed congressional redistricting map that would have eliminated the state's majority-Black district, with GOP opponents arguing it was improper to redraw districts while early voting for the June 9 primary was already underway.

SC.title: EARLY VOTING TRACKER: Record turnout continues for SC primaries
SC.summary: South Carolina continued to post record early voting numbers heading into the final week before the June 9 primary, with cumulative totals already surpassing the full 2024 primary's early vote total.

SD.title: 'The least bad option': South Dakotans explain their primary election voting decisions
SD.summary: On primary day in South Dakota, voters described their rationale for choosing among the four Republican candidates for governor, with the race potentially heading to a July 28 runoff if no candidate reaches the 35% threshold.

SD.title: South Dakota Primary Election Day: GOP governor race could head to July 28 runoff
SD.summary: Voters cast ballots June 2 in South Dakota's primary, where the four-way Republican gubernatorial race between Gov. Larry Rhoden, Rep. Dusty Johnson, House Speaker Jon Hansen, and Toby Doeden could trigger a runoff if no candidate wins 35%.

SD.title: When to expect results from today's South Dakota primary election
SD.summary: The South Dakota Secretary of State's office planned to begin releasing June 2 primary results just after 8 p.m. CT, with eastern time zone counties reporting first followed by the western part of the state.

TN.title: Tennessee's 2026 candidate lists finalized for state and federal races
TN.summary: The Tennessee Secretary of State released the complete list of candidates for 2026 state and federal races following the filing deadline, covering the open governor's race, all 99 House seats, and 17 Senate districts under the newly redrawn congressional maps.

WI.title: Filing deadline narrows Wisconsin governor's race to 9 candidates
WI.summary: After Wisconsin's June 2 nomination paper deadline, nine candidates qualified for the governor's race on the August 11 primary ballot — eight Democrats and Republican Tom Tiffany — while two others were disqualified for failing to submit signatures.

WI.title: Wisconsin's crowded governor's race remains crowded after filing deadline
WI.summary: The June 2 filing deadline produced no dropout wave from Wisconsin's Democratic gubernatorial field; the Elections Commission will certify the final ballot-qualified candidate list at its June 9 meeting.

WI.title: Nomination paper deadline for August governor primary passes on Monday
WI.summary: Wisconsin's June 2 deadline for nomination papers closed the candidate field for the August 11 primary; candidates for governor needed at least 2,000 valid signatures and challenges are allowed through June 4.

WV.title: Overpaying for the status quo in West Virginia's primary election
WV.summary: An analysis of West Virginia's May 12 primary finds that millions in campaign spending yielded only 21% voter turnout, raising concerns about political engagement and the effectiveness of outside money in mobilizing West Virginia voters ahead of November.

AL.title: Supreme Court reinstates Republican-favored Alabama congressional districts
AL.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court cleared the way for Alabama to use a Republican-drawn congressional map for the 2026 midterms, eliminating one of two majority-Black congressional districts and making the state's delegation six Republican-leaning seats to one Democratic-leaning seat.

AZ.title: Gov. Hobbs and Rep. Biggs exchange attacks ahead of Arizona primary
AZ.summary: Arizona Governor Katie Hobbs and Republican primary frontrunner Rep. Andy Biggs traded campaign attacks with the July 21 primary seven weeks away, as Biggs unveiled an ethics platform targeting Hobbs and her campaign launched an opposition website attacking his record.

CA.title: California's primary for governor is undecided as candidates vie to be in the top two
CA.summary: California's June 2 gubernatorial primary remained too close to call the following morning, with Republican Steve Hilton at 27%, Democrat Xavier Becerra at 26%, and Democrat Tom Steyer at 20% in the top-two contest, with weeks of ballot-counting ahead.

CO.title: Colorado's 3 Republican candidates for governor square off in first full debate
CO.summary: State Rep. Scott Bottoms, State Sen. Barb Kirkmeyer, and ministry leader Victor Marx held a contentious televised debate in Denver ahead of Colorado's June 30 Republican gubernatorial primary, clashing over qualifications, character, and unusual topics including exorcisms and alleged federal indictments.

CT.title: As Ned Lamont touts record, Josh Elliott's campaign strengthens
CT.summary: Progressive challenger Josh Elliott's campaign for Connecticut governor is growing stronger, with incumbent Gov. Ned Lamont leaning into budget accomplishments and early education investments as the two face off in an August 11 Democratic primary, with a candidate filing deadline of June 9.

DC.title: A voter's guide to the 2026 D.C. primary election
DC.summary: With DC's historic June 16 primary two weeks away, this guide covers the first-ever open mayoral race using ranked-choice voting, the race to succeed 36-year congressional delegate Eleanor Holmes Norton, and multiple D.C. Council contests.

DE.title: In Fenwick Island, Delaware, nonhumans can still vote
DE.summary: A Delaware Superior Court dismissed the ACLU's constitutional challenge to Fenwick Island's charter allowing corporations, LLCs, and trusts to vote in municipal elections; the ACLU announced it will appeal to the Delaware Supreme Court, with 214 artificial entities comprising 12% of the town's registered voters.

FL.title: Florida appeals court rejects bid to send redistricting challenge to state Supreme Court
FL.summary: Florida's First District Court of Appeal rejected a motion to fast-track to the state Supreme Court a challenge to Gov. DeSantis's Republican-drawn congressional gerrymander, leaving the new 24-4 GOP-favoring map in place for the 2026 elections while litigation continues.

IA.title: MAHA-backed Zach Lahn defeats Trump-backed Randy Feenstra in Iowa GOP primary for governor
IA.summary: Zach Lahn, backed by Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s MAHA movement, defeated incumbent Rep. Randy Feenstra, who had Trump's endorsement, in the Iowa Republican gubernatorial primary. Lahn will face the Democratic nominee in November.

IA.title: Lahn edges past Feenstra to win Iowa GOP Primary for governor
IA.summary: Zach Lahn won the Iowa Republican primary for governor, edging out Rep. Randy Feenstra in a race that pitted MAHA-aligned candidates against Trump-backed incumbents across Iowa's 2026 primary ballot.

IA.title: Iowa primary results: Trump-backed Feenstra concedes to Lahn in governor primary; Hinson and Turek will compete for open Senate seat
IA.summary: Iowa's June 2 primary results show Feenstra conceded the GOP gubernatorial race to Zach Lahn. In the open U.S. Senate race, Ashley Hinson and Marco Turek advanced to face off in the general election.

LA.title: Will Louisiana's last majority-Black district survive Callais? A court will decide
LA.summary: A federal court is set to rule on Louisiana's newly redrawn congressional map, which created a second majority-Black district. The case centers on whether the new map will survive a legal challenge that could eliminate the state's last majority-Black congressional district.

ME.title: Despite national stakes, 2nd District Democrats struggle to gain an edge
ME.summary: With Maine's June 9 primary approaching, the four-way Democratic primary in the 2nd Congressional District — where candidates Joe Baldacci, Matt Dunlap, Paige Loud, and Jordan Wood compete to replace Rep. Jared Golden — has remained subdued despite the national stakes of the open seat race.

MI.title: Michigan opens voting for 2026 'I Voted' sticker contest through June 30
MI.summary: Michigan Secretary of State opened public voting for the official 2026 'I Voted' sticker design contest through June 30, with winning designs to be distributed at polling stations statewide for November's general election.

MN.title: More candidates file on last day for county, state house and senate seats
MN.summary: Minnesota's candidate filing period for the 2026 election closed June 2 with a wave of last-minute filings for local county, state house, and state senate seats. Candidates have until June 4 to withdraw before the Secretary of State certifies the field for the August 11 primary.

NH.title: Federal judge strikes down part of New Hampshire's documentary proof of citizenship law
NH.summary: A federal judge struck down New Hampshire's law requiring documentary proof of citizenship for voter registration (HB 1569), finding it imposed an excessive burden on the right to vote ahead of the state's September 8 primary; the state attorney general plans to appeal.

NJ.title: Rebecca Bennett wins New Jersey Democratic primary, to face Trump ally Kean
NJ.summary: Former Navy helicopter pilot Rebecca Bennett won the New Jersey 7th Congressional District Democratic primary, setting up a November race against Republican Rep. Tom Kean Jr., whose months-long unexplained absence from Congress drew intense attention during the campaign.

NM.title: Deb Haaland snags the Democratic nomination for governor against Sam Bregman
NM.summary: Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland won New Mexico's Democratic gubernatorial primary with about 72% of the vote over Bernalillo County DA Sam Bregman in the state's first semi-open primary, and will face Republican Rio Rancho Mayor Gregg Hull in November.

OR.title: After Oregonians reject gas tax, governor's transportation workgroup fixates on messaging, not math
OR.summary: Following Oregon voters' overwhelming rejection of Measure 120's gas and vehicle fee increases in the May 19 primary, Governor Kotek's transportation workgroup focused on public communication strategy rather than revising the funding proposal itself.

PA.title: Chris Rabb's campaign was a massive win for Philly progressives. Now, he wants to replicate it across the country.
PA.summary: After his decisive May 19 Democratic primary victory in Pennsylvania's 3rd Congressional District, State Rep. Chris Rabb announced endorsements for progressive candidates in other states, reflecting the broader national impact of his Philadelphia-area congressional primary win.

SC.title: SCETV to host Democratic gubernatorial primary debate tonight
SC.summary: South Carolina Educational Television hosted a Democratic gubernatorial primary debate ahead of the June 9 primary, with early voting ongoing through June 5 and record turnout reported.

SD.title: Doeden and Rhoden advance to runoff in Republican governor primary, Johnson falls to third
SD.summary: Results from South Dakota's June 2 Republican gubernatorial primary show businessman Toby Doeden and Lt. Gov. Tony Rhoden advancing to a July 28 runoff after neither candidate reached the required 35% threshold; former Lt. Gov. Larry Johnson finished third.

TX.title: National Democrats aim to flip 12 Texas House seats under newly expanded target list
TX.summary: The Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee expanded its Texas target list to 12 Republican-held state House districts ahead of the November 2026 elections, focusing resources on seats in suburban areas where Democratic performance has improved.

WA.title: WA urges US Supreme Court to take redistricting case
WA.summary: Washington state officials are urging the US Supreme Court to take up a redistricting case involving legislative district maps in the Yakima Valley region, where plaintiffs allege the maps dilute Latino voter representation in violation of the Voting Rights Act.

HI.title: Unopposed races scattered across Hawaii's primary election ballot
HI.summary: After Hawaii's June 2 candidate filing deadline closed, about 23 of 100+ races on the August 8 primary ballot will run unopposed, prompting accountability concerns from political analysts.

HI.title: Familiar faces reemerge as Hawaii's primary election takes shape
HI.summary: With filing now closed, Hawaii's 2026 primary ballot is set for August 8, featuring a rematch between Honolulu Council Chair Tommy Waters and Trevor Ozawa, whose 2019 contest was invalidated by the Hawaii Supreme Court.

IL.title: Illinois Lt. Gov. candidate Mitchell says he's ready to step in if Pritzker leaves office
IL.summary: Illinois Lt. Gov. candidate Christian Mitchell addressed questions about continuity if Gov. JB Pritzker pursues a 2028 presidential run, as Illinois heads toward a November gubernatorial rematch between Pritzker and Republican Darren Bailey.

IL.title: Illinois legislature wraps 2026 with $55.9 billion budget, new corporate taxes and rideshare union rights
IL.summary: The Illinois General Assembly ended its 2026 session May 31; voting-access items included a permanent vote-by-mail checkbox requirement and expanded early voting at public university campuses heading toward the November election.

MD.title: Several Maryland Laws Took Effect June 1
MD.summary: Multiple new Maryland election laws took effect June 1 ahead of the June 23 gubernatorial primary, including measures criminalizing AI-generated deepfakes used to spread election misinformation and expanding election officials' authority to police polling places.

MS.title: How the US Supreme Court's Callais ruling erased a key Mississippi voting rights victory
MS.summary: A federal appeals court vacated a ruling requiring Mississippi to redraw its Supreme Court election maps, ending Black voters' hopes for fairer representation and special court elections in fall 2026, after the Callais decision raised the standard for proving racial discrimination in voting.

MT.title: 2026 Montana primary election winners
MT.summary: Montana Public Radio published a full roundup of June 2 primary results: Republican Kurt Alme and Democrat Alani Bankhead won Senate nominations, Aaron Flint won the Republican western U.S. House nomination, and Democrat Brian Miller won the eastern U.S. House Democratic primary.

NY.title: NY Elections, Census, and Redistricting Update — Special Update June 2, 2026
NY.summary: New York legislative leaders introduced a constitutional amendment to permit mid-decade congressional redistricting by simple majority and remove the ban on partisan gerrymandering; expected to be voted on June 4 before session adjournment.

NY.title: Breaking down New York's proposed redistricting amendment
NY.summary: Analysis of New York's proposed redistricting constitutional amendment details how it would limit the Independent Redistricting Commission to map-drawing hearings only, allow simple majority approval of maps, and remove requirements that districts not favor particular parties or incumbents.

OK.title: Advocates challenge the rejection of Oklahoma open primaries initiative petition
OK.summary: Supporters of State Question 836, a top-two open primary initiative, appealed to the Oklahoma Supreme Court after the Secretary of State rejected their petition for insufficient valid signatures, disputing the signature verification methodology.

OK.title: Answering your questions about the Oklahoma June 16 primary
OK.summary: A voter guide answers key questions about Oklahoma's June 16 primary including voter ID requirements, early voting dates (June 11-13), absentee ballot deadlines, and information about the minimum wage state question.

RI.title: 2026 Rhode Island Elections: Candidate Filing and Voting Schedule
RI.summary: Rhode Island's candidate filing period opens June 22-24 for the September 9 primary and November 3 general election; early voting for the primary runs August 20 through September 8.

TN.title: Tennessee enacts bill changing voter restoration requirements for individuals convicted of a felony, 10 other election bills in 2026 regular session
TN.summary: Tennessee Governor Bill Lee signed 11 election-related bills; the key change (SB 336) eases felony voting rights restoration by removing requirements that ex-felons pay all court costs and be fully current on child support before regaining the vote.

UT.title: Voter registration deadline for 2026 primary is June 12
UT.summary: Utah's voter registration deadline for the June 23 primary is June 12 at 5 p.m.; mail ballots began arriving June 2 to all active registered voters, with early voting running June 9-19 at Vote Centers statewide.

WY.title: A second Wyoming Democrat is running for U.S. Senate
WY.summary: A second Democratic candidate entered Wyoming's open U.S. Senate race, adding competition on the Democratic side as Rep. Harriet Hageman vacates her House seat to seek the Senate seat ahead of the August 18 primary.

AK.title: There are two Dan Sullivans running for Dan Sullivan's Senate seat — and Dan Sullivan is annoyed
AK.summary: Republican U.S. Sen. Dan Sullivan faces a same-named challenger on Alaska's August primary ballot, accusing Democrats and the Peltola campaign of a 'dirty trick' to confuse voters. The two will appear as 'Dan S. Sullivan' and 'Dan J. Sullivan' under state election law requiring middle-initial differentiation.

AK.title: Sullivan vs. Sullivan: Senator accuses Peltola of 'rigging' election — but evidence of her involvement is unclear
AK.summary: Sen. Dan Sullivan and the NRSC are demanding removal of Petersburg resident Dan J. Sullivan from the Alaska Senate primary ballot, citing alleged false party affiliation claims and a metadata link to a Democratic consultant — though direct coordination with the Peltola campaign remains unconfirmed.

AR.title: Republican nominee selected to run for late Arkansas lawmaker's House seat
AR.summary: Bill Teeter won the Republican nomination for Arkansas House District 44, left vacant by the death of Rep. Stan Berry, and will run unopposed in November. Teeter also advanced to a June 30 special election runoff against Nikki Phillips to fill the remainder of Berry's current term.

CA.title: 2026 Primary Election: Steve Hilton, Xavier Becerra hold leads in tight, still too-close-to-call California governor's race
CA.summary: With roughly 55% of ballots counted from California's June 2 primary, Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra hold the top two spots in the governor's race at 28% and 26% respectively, with Democrat Tom Steyer at 20% and the contest still too close to call.

DC.title: D.C. mayor's race voter guide: What to know about the candidates
DC.summary: With D.C.'s June 16 Democratic mayoral primary using ranked-choice voting for the first time, Axios profiles the seven candidates seeking to replace Mayor Muriel Bowser, highlighting frontrunners Janeese Lewis George and Kenyan McDuffie, with early voting opening June 8.

GA.title: Georgia Runoff Elections: Who's on the ballot, how can you vote?
GA.summary: Voter guide covering Georgia's June 16 primary runoff election, including the Republican contests for governor (Burt Jones vs. Rick Jackson) and U.S. Senate (Mike Collins vs. Derek Dooley). Details the June 5 absentee ballot request deadline and early voting schedule of June 6-12.

GA.title: WSBTV's June 16 Georgia Runoff Voter Guide
GA.summary: Comprehensive guide to Georgia's June 16 primary runoff election, covering the Republican gubernatorial runoff (Lt. Gov. Burt Jones vs. Rick Jackson) and Senate GOP runoff (Rep. Mike Collins vs. Derek Dooley), including early voting locations and absentee ballot procedures.

ID.title: Idaho state audit confirms Ada County primary election results
ID.summary: A hand-count audit of Ada County ballots by Idaho Secretary of State officials and Boise State University accounting students confirmed the reported May 19 primary results were accurate. Eight counties were randomly selected for post-election audits before the Board of Canvassers certifies results on June 9.

ID.title: Idaho election officials audit primary results
ID.summary: Idaho election officials conducted post-election audits comparing hand-counted paper ballots against reported results in eight randomly selected counties following the May 19 primary. Final certified results are expected after the Board of Canvassers meets June 9.

IN.title: Banks staffer Engling says decision on secretary of state's race came quickly
IN.summary: Max Engling, a staffer for U.S. Sen. Jim Banks who entered Indiana's Republican secretary of state race, discusses his campaign ahead of the June 20 GOP state convention. Four candidates are competing after top GOP officials withdrew support from incumbent Diego Morales over concerns about his office's hiring practices.

KS.title: Kansas governor's race takes shape with 10 candidates after filing deadline
KS.summary: Following the June 1 filing deadline, the Kansas governor's race is set with seven Republicans including Trump-endorsed Senate President Ty Masterson and three Democrats. The primary is August 4, with voters choosing the successor to term-limited Democratic Gov. Laura Kelly.

NC.title: State Board Provides Tips for Voters as Mid-Term Election Approaches
NC.summary: The North Carolina State Board of Elections issued guidance ahead of the November 2026 general election, noting roughly 370,000 voter registration application mailings are being sent statewide and reminding voters to verify their registration status ahead of the October 9 deadline.

ND.title: Local issues driving turnout in North Dakota primary early voting
ND.summary: Nearly 30,000 votes have been cast ahead of North Dakota's June 9 primary, with local contests — particularly the Fargo mayor's race — driving unexpectedly strong turnout even though no statewide offices appear on the ballot for the first time since 2014.

NJ.title: The missing Rep. Tom Kean Jr. finally speaks … sort of
NJ.summary: Rep. Tom Kean Jr., absent from Congress since early March, issued a statement promising a return to in-person work within weeks, raising questions about his fitness to run in New Jersey's 7th Congressional District against newly nominated Democrat Rebecca Bennett in November.

NM.title: Thousands of independent voters voice their opinion for the first semi-open primary in New Mexico
NM.summary: About 33,000 of New Mexico's independent voters participated in the state's first-ever semi-open primary on June 2, with most choosing Democratic ballots. Party leaders noted independents did not materially swing outcomes, as Deb Haaland won the Democratic governor primary with 72% of the vote.

NV.title: Nevada Primary Election: Early Voting Ends Friday
NV.summary: Nevada's in-person early voting period for the June 9 primary ends Friday, June 5; the Secretary of State reminded voters that online registration closes June 4 and same-day registration remains available in person during early voting and on Election Day.

NV.title: Turnout for Nevada's 2026 primary is low. Is it breaking any records?
NV.summary: Primary participation in Nevada stands at about 8% with days remaining before the June 9 election, though Washoe County early-vote turnout is up roughly 30% compared to two years ago. The Nevada Independent projects 150,000–180,000 ballots per partisan side.

OH.title: Ohio Senate advances its fast-tracked voter ID amendment
OH.source: The Statehouse News Bureau / WOSU Public Media
OH.summary: The Ohio Senate passed Senate Joint Resolution 10 on a 22-9 vote to place a constitutional amendment on the November 2026 ballot that would enshrine existing photo voter ID requirements in the state constitution; the measure now needs a House vote, and drew near-unanimous opposition from 80+ public witnesses.

OH.title: Ohio Senate advances photo voter ID amendment measure
OH.summary: Ohio Capital Journal reported on the Ohio Senate's fast-tracked constitutional amendment to enshrine photo voter ID requirements, noting Republican critics say it fails to extend ID requirements to absentee voters, while voting rights advocates argue it simply duplicates existing law.

VA.title: Virginia voting applications stuck in limbo for many with felony convictions
VA.summary: Following a federal court order in King v. Youngkin, Virginia elections officials directed local registrars not to deny voter registration applications from people with non-common-law felony convictions but instructed them to hold applications pending further guidance, leaving thousands of prospective voters in limbo.

WA.title: WA urges U.S. Supreme Court to take redistricting case
WA.summary: Washington state filed a brief asking the U.S. Supreme Court to accept and remand a challenge to its redrawn legislative district maps, arguing the case must be reconsidered under the Court's recent Louisiana v. Callais ruling that significantly curtailed the use of race in drawing electoral boundaries.

WI.title: Some high-profile election hopefuls fall short of ballot requirements
WI.summary: More than 300 candidates filed for Wisconsin's August 11 primary, but several high-profile hopefuls failed to meet signature thresholds; gubernatorial candidate Kirk Bangstad fell short with only 1,504 valid signatures against the required 2,000, and the Wisconsin Elections Commission will finalize ballot qualification decisions the following week.

WI.title: Wisconsin ballot curing lawsuit seeks uniform voter rules
WI.summary: The League of Women Voters of Wisconsin's lawsuit against the Wisconsin Elections Commission seeks to require all clerks to uniformly notify voters about defective absentee ballots and allow them to cure signature or address errors before rejection, arguing the current discretionary system treats voters unequally across municipalities.

WI.title: Wisconsin governor's race takes shape as candidates file for ballot
WI.summary: Following Wisconsin's June 1 candidate filing deadline, seven Democrats and two Republicans qualified for the August 11 primary ballot in the wide-open governor's race, with incumbent Tony Evers having declined to seek a third term.

WY.title: 26,000 fewer voters registered in Wyoming
WY.summary: Wyoming's biennial voter roll purge has reduced registered voters from 296,703 to approximately 270,925 ahead of the August 18 primary; AARP Wyoming is urging residents to verify their registration, as state law removes voters who did not participate in the 2024 general election.

AL.title: Supreme Court allows Alabama to use congressional map that eliminates a majority-Black district
AL.summary: The Supreme Court, in a 6-3 ruling along ideological lines, granted Alabama's emergency request to use its 2023 congressional map that eliminates one of two majority-Black districts ahead of the 2026 midterms, reversing a lower court finding that the map was the product of intentional racial discrimination in violation of the Voting Rights Act.

AL.title: Alabama governor sets special election dates for four congressional districts impacted by redistricting decision
AL.summary: Following the Supreme Court's decision allowing Alabama's 2023 congressional map, Governor Kay Ivey set special primary elections for August 11, 2026, in the 1st, 2nd, 6th, and 7th congressional districts, which had their primaries postponed due to the redistricting dispute.

AZ.title: 2026 Election: Arizona Congressional District 5 Democratic candidates debate
AZ.summary: Three Democratic primary candidates debated for Arizona's 5th Congressional District in a Citizens Clean Elections Commission-sponsored forum covering key issues for East Valley voters ahead of the July 21 primary, with voter registration closing June 22.

CO.title: GOP primary debate goes off the rails
CO.summary: CPR News reported on the first three-way debate among Colorado's Republican gubernatorial candidates — Sen. Barbara Kirkmeyer, Rep. Scott Bottoms, and Victor Marx — noting extraordinary false claims and infighting at the University of Denver forum ahead of Colorado's June 30 primary, for which all active registered voters will receive mail ballots starting June 8.

GA.title: State Election Board passes resolution allowing counties to switch to hand-marked ballots
GA.summary: Georgia's State Election Board passed a 3-1 non-binding resolution allowing counties to switch to hand-marked paper ballots ahead of a July 1 deadline banning QR codes from ballot counting, conflicting with the Secretary of State's office which maintains current voting system equipment must continue to be used.

KY.title: Coleman picks 12 counties for post-primary election audit
KY.summary: Kentucky Attorney General Russell Coleman randomly selected 12 counties — including Rowan, Oldham, Franklin, Daviess, and Laurel — for post-primary election integrity inquiries following the May 19 primary, with investigations conducted by the AG's Department of Criminal Investigations.

LA.title: Louisiana approves new congressional map, dismantling majority-Black district
LA.summary: Louisiana's legislature passed and Gov. Landry signed Act 2 of the 2026 Regular Session, a new congressional map eliminating the Baton Rouge-area majority-Black district held by Rep. Cleo Fields, redrawing lines to favor five Republicans and one Democrat in response to the Supreme Court's Callais ruling.

LA.title: Louisiana's new congressional map to go before panel of federal judges on June 17
LA.summary: A three-judge federal panel scheduled a June 17 hearing in Shreveport to review Louisiana's newly enacted congressional map (Act 2 of 2026), which eliminates one majority-Black district; the court will assess whether the new map meets legal requirements following the Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais ruling.

LA.title: Louisiana June runoff election: Important dates, what no-party voters should know
LA.summary: A voter guide to the June 27 Senate runoff elections covers early voting dates (June 12–20, excluding Juneteenth), explains how Louisiana's new closed primary system affects no-party-affiliated voters who cannot participate in the runoff, and outlines key candidate matchups.

MA.title: The quiet parts get loud in Markey-Moulton Senate primary
MA.summary: Following Markey's dominant 73% win at the Massachusetts Democratic convention, both Senate primary candidates sharpened their attacks ahead of the September 1 primary, with Markey targeting Moulton on trans issues and Moulton challenging Markey on age and AI policy.

MA.title: Massachusetts Permit Same-Day Voter Registration Initiative (2026)
MA.summary: The same-day voter registration ballot initiative is in its second signature-gathering round, with a June 17 deadline to submit 12,429 certified signatures; if it qualifies, Massachusetts voters will decide in November whether to allow election-day registration at polling places.

MA.title: 2026 Massachusetts ballot measures include voter ID and same-day registration questions
MA.summary: Massachusetts voters could face competing ballot questions in November on both same-day voter registration and a voter ID requirement, setting up a significant debate over voting access in a state with no current ID mandate.

MD.title: Maryland Board of Elections pushes back on Trump's claim of 500,000 fake mail-in ballots
MD.summary: The Maryland State Board of Elections rebutted President Trump's characterization of the mail-ballot vendor error as evidence of fraud, clarifying that affected ballots were voided in the registration system and replacement ballots were sent ahead of the June 23 gubernatorial primary.

MD.title: Maryland Lt. Gov. responds to ballot error saying 'It happens almost in every election'
MD.summary: Lt. Governor Aruna Miller defended the state's handling of the mail-in ballot vendor error, rejecting Trump's call for a DOJ investigation while a Congressional committee requested answers from the Board of Elections by June 9 ahead of the June 23 primary.

MD.title: Voter who received three ballots raises new concerns as mail-in ballot canvassing begins
MD.summary: At least one Maryland voter reported receiving three separate ballots ahead of the June 23 primary, raising fresh questions about oversight as county boards of election began the formal canvassing process for returned mail-in ballots.

ME.title: New poll taken before sexting saga shows Graham Platner up by 5 points over Susan Collins
ME.summary: A UMass Lowell/YouGov poll shows Democratic candidate Graham Platner leading incumbent Sen. Susan Collins 48%–43% in Maine's U.S. Senate race, though the poll was conducted before revelations about Platner's personal conduct that could complicate his path through the June 9 Democratic primary.

ME.title: Poll: Graham Platner maintains lead over Susan Collins in Maine Senate race
ME.summary: The Bangor Daily News reports that Platner's lead over Collins remains intact in early general election polling, with analysts noting his lower name recognition makes voters more persuadable as new information about his personal conduct emerges ahead of June 9 voting.

MN.title: Demuth enters GOP governor primary after challenging convention vote
MN.summary: Minnesota House Speaker Lisa Demuth officially filed to run in the August GOP primary for governor after questioning the electronic voting process that endorsed rival Kendall Qualls at the Republican state convention, setting up a three-way Republican primary alongside Qualls and Mike Lindell.

MN.title: Minnesota GOP clears path for Demuth to stay in governor's race
MN.summary: The Republican Party of Minnesota released endorsed candidates from their pledge to exit before the primary, freeing House Speaker Lisa Demuth to continue her race after a glitch in the convention's electronic voting system cast doubt on the legitimacy of endorsement results.

MN.title: Get up to speed on a crucial Minnesota primary election
MN.summary: The Star Tribune published an explainer on Minnesota's crowded August 11 primary, detailing contested governor and Senate races on both sides and noting that early primary voting begins June 26 via absentee ballot, mail, or in-person options statewide.

MO.title: Appellate court set to consider challenge to Missouri income tax overhaul
MO.summary: The Missouri Court of Appeals for the Western District was set to hear oral arguments challenging Amendment 5, the proposed constitutional amendment to phase out the income tax, with legal questions required to be settled by June 9 ahead of the August 4 primary ballot.

MS.title: Q&A with attorney Carroll Rhodes on Mississippi redistricting
MS.summary: Civil rights attorney Carroll Rhodes discusses the implications of the U.S. Supreme Court's Callais ruling for Black voters in Mississippi, including the loss of court-ordered special elections for Mississippi Supreme Court seats that had been won under the Voting Rights Act.

NC.title: State elections board issues guidance on voter drives, mailings ahead of midterms
NC.summary: The North Carolina State Board of Elections issued guidance about a wave of third-party voter registration drives and approximately 370,000 mass mailings arriving in North Carolina homes, advising voters how to identify legitimate communications and properly submit registration forms ahead of the November midterms.

NY.title: Inside New York's 12th Congressional District Primary
NY.summary: A deep-dive feature on the crowded June 23 Democratic primary in NY-12 (Manhattan), examining candidates including George Conway, Jack Schlossberg, and Micah Lasher vying to succeed retiring Rep. Jerry Nadler, with recent polling showing Lasher with a slight lead.

OR.title: 2026 Oregon midterm election results
OR.summary: OPB's primary results tracker, updated June 3, shows Christine Drazan leading the GOP gubernatorial primary heading to a November rematch with Gov. Tina Kotek, while Measure 120 (gas tax/transportation funding) was overwhelmingly rejected by voters; results to be certified June 25.

SC.title: DECISION 2026: What to know about primary elections in South Carolina
SC.summary: A voter guide for South Carolina's June 9 primary covering ballot races (U.S. Senate, governor, U.S. House), photo ID requirements, polling hours (7am–7pm), and early voting details — following record-breaking early turnout surpassing 177,000 ballots in the first week, already exceeding the entire 2024 primary early voting total.

SD.title: Incumbent Larry Rhoden and Toby Doeden advance to first-ever primary runoff for South Dakota governor
SD.summary: With no candidate reaching the required 35% threshold in the June 2 Republican gubernatorial primary, incumbent Gov. Larry Rhoden (25%) and political newcomer Toby Doeden (31%) advance to a July 28 runoff — the first gubernatorial primary runoff in South Dakota since the 35% rule was adopted in 1985.

SD.title: Lower turnout, shifting loyalties may drive results in GOP primary runoff for South Dakota governor
SD.summary: Analysis of how the July 28 runoff between Doeden and Rhoden may play out: lower runoff turnout and the likely shift of Rep. Dusty Johnson's 23% vote share toward incumbent Rhoden could be decisive factors in the first gubernatorial primary runoff in South Dakota history.

SD.title: Analysis: 'Republicans have chosen quite different people' in gubernatorial run-off
SD.summary: Political analysis contrasts the July 28 runoff candidates: incumbent Gov. Larry Rhoden, a career politician, versus Toby Doeden, a self-described outsider and Aberdeen vehicle dealership owner who branded himself as Trump's 'fiercest supporter.'

SD.title: Absentee voting for gubernatorial runoff begins next week
SD.summary: The South Dakota Secretary of State announces absentee voting for the July 28 Republican gubernatorial runoff opens June 12; voters who did not request a primary absentee ballot must apply to their county auditor by July 27 at 5 p.m., and voter registration closes July 13.

WA.title: Foes of Washington income tax race to collect initiative signatures
WA.summary: Opponents of Washington's new 9.9% income tax on earnings above $1 million are racing to collect at least 308,911 valid voter signatures by a July 2 deadline to qualify an initiative for the November ballot; as of June 4 they had gathered roughly 165,000 signatures.

CA.title: California's race for governor, other key House primaries remain unsettled as vote count continues
CA.summary: Three days after California's June 2 primary, the governor's race between Steve Hilton and Xavier Becerra remains unresolved with roughly 57% of ballots counted, illustrating the state's mail-ballot counting rules that allow returns postmarked by Election Day to arrive through June 9.

CA.title: 2026 Primary Election: Slow California vote count criticized by Trump and Republican governor hopeful Steve Hilton
CA.summary: President Trump announced a DOJ investigation into California's vote-counting process, alleging fraud without evidence, while gubernatorial candidate Steve Hilton called the slow count 'a complete disgrace'; election officials and Gov. Newsom defended the process as prioritizing accuracy over speed.

CO.title: Bennet, Weiser debate again ahead of ballots dropping in Colorado Democratic primary for governor
CO.summary: U.S. Sen. Michael Bennet and Attorney General Phil Weiser squared off in a second Democratic primary debate on June 4 as mail ballots begin going to voters on June 8 for Colorado's June 30 primary election.

FL.title: Pro-voting groups ask Florida Supreme Court to block GOP gerrymander
FL.summary: Voting rights groups filed an emergency petition with the Florida Supreme Court asking it to halt the DeSantis-signed congressional map before candidate qualifying opens June 8, arguing the map violates Florida's Fair Districts Amendment banning partisan gerrymandering.

GA.title: Secretary of state opposes proposed election change
GA.summary: The Georgia Secretary of State's office publicly opposed the State Election Board's June 4 resolution authorizing counties to switch to hand-marked paper ballots, calling the SEB action an overreach that interferes with the legislative process ahead of the June 17 special session to address the July 1 QR-code ban deadline.

ID.title: Voting Audit is Underway for Primary Election
ID.summary: Idaho election officials are conducting required post-primary hand-count audits in eight randomly selected counties, with Butte and Power counties audited June 4 and Owyhee County scheduled for June 5. All audits so far have confirmed machine tabulation results matched hand counts; the Idaho Board of Canvassers will certify results on June 9.

IL.title: The Supreme Court has left limited alternatives for protecting minority voting rights
IL.summary: Following the Supreme Court's Callais ruling gutting Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, Illinois Democrats paused their redistricting constitutional amendment while a new federal lawsuit challenges the Illinois Voting Rights Act itself as unconstitutional. State-level voting rights legislation like Illinois's pending SB3170 is now seen as an increasingly uncertain backstop for minority voter protections.

LA.title: Will Louisiana's last majority-Black district survive Callais? A court will decide
LA.summary: A federal three-judge panel scheduled a June 17 hearing in Shreveport to determine whether Louisiana's newly enacted congressional map complies with the Supreme Court's Callais ruling, with challenge briefs due June 5. The original Callais plaintiffs argue the new map—which already eliminated one majority-Black district—may still rely too heavily on race in drawing the remaining one.

MT.title: Eight incumbent Montana legislators lose primary elections
MT.summary: Eight Republican incumbent Montana state legislators—two senators and six representatives—were defeated in the June 2 primary by more conservative challengers within their party, including Senate Majority Whip Barry Usher, signaling a rightward shift in the state GOP caucus ahead of November.

NE.title: Nebraska Board of State Canvassers set to certify primary election results
NE.summary: Nebraska's Board of State Canvassers is scheduled to meet June 8 to officially certify the May 12 primary results; no automatic recounts are anticipated for statewide races, though a June 15 contingency meeting is set if any race triggers a recount threshold.

NV.title: Nevada Primary Election: Early Voting Ends Friday
NV.summary: Early in-person voting for Nevada's June 9 primary concluded Friday June 5, with turnout running historically low; the article outlines Election Day poll locations, mail-ballot postmark deadlines, and same-day registration options still available to voters.

OK.title: Why Oklahoma's minimum wage question might look strange to voters
OK.summary: State Question 832, on Oklahoma's June 16 primary ballot, contains outdated language referencing 2025 as the start date for minimum wage increases—a result of Gov. Kevin Stitt delaying the vote by nearly two years. Despite the confusing ballot language, if passed the minimum wage would still rise to /hour by 2029 on a delayed schedule.

OK.title: Farm groups are concerned about Oklahoma's state question raising the minimum wage
OK.summary: Agricultural groups in Oklahoma are urging voters to reject State Question 832, which would raise the state minimum wage to /hour by 2029, ahead of the June 16 primary election. Opponents argue the increase would harm small farms and rural businesses.

PA.title: Study: Ballot curing helps more mail ballots get counted
PA.summary: A University of Pennsylvania study of the 2024 election found that notifying voters of mail ballot errors significantly reduced the share of rejected votes, with voters informed about issues far more likely to have their ballots counted. The findings have implications for how Pennsylvania administers mail ballot curing heading into the 2026 general election.

PA.title: Student poll workers help run elections in Pennsylvania
PA.summary: Pennsylvania's student poll worker program reached its highest-ever participation rate in the 2026 primary, with 633 students receiving the Governor's Civic Engagement Award for serving at polling places. The program is seen as one solution to the state's ongoing poll worker shortage.

SD.title: Absentee voting for South Dakota GOP governor runoff begins June 12
SD.summary: Absentee voting opens June 12 for South Dakota's first-ever gubernatorial runoff election, set for July 28 between incumbent Gov. Larry Rhoden and Toby Doeden after neither cleared the 35% threshold in the June 2 primary. Voters who did not request an absentee ballot for the primary must submit a new application by July 27; voter registration closes July 13.

VT.title: Vermont lawmakers have adjourned for the year. Here's what they did — and didn't do — in 2026
VT.summary: Vermont's 2026 legislative session adjourned, sending several voting-related bills to Gov. Phil Scott, including S.298 (the Voter Protections Act) delivered to the governor on June 2. The bill prohibits discrimination in voting, expands voter intimidation protections, and strengthens election administration safeguards statewide.

DC.title: Understanding ranked choice voting ahead of its DC debut in June primary
DC.summary: DC's June 16 primary will mark the first use of ranked choice voting in the District following voters' approval of Initiative 83 in 2024. The article explains the RCV process to voters ahead of a historic election that includes the first open mayoral race in 12 years and the first new congressional delegate race in 36 years.

AR.title: Republican nominee selected to run for late Arkansas lawmaker's House seat
AR.summary: Retired firefighter Bill Teeter won the Republican nomination in the special primary for Arkansas House District 44, vacated by the death of Rep. Stan Berry; he will face a June 30 runoff for the remainder of Berry's term and will run unopposed in November for the full term.

CT.title: Surveillance, immigration and greyfields: CT politics news
CT.summary: Attorney General William Tong became the first 2026 candidate to qualify for a public general-election grant through Connecticut's Citizens' Election Program, raising $100,700 in small-dollar contributions; the State Elections Enforcement Commission also approved public financing grants for 15 General Assembly candidates.

HI.title: Hawaii incumbents with no challengers will cruise to victory
HI.summary: After the June 2 candidate filing deadline, 21 incumbent state legislators and council members have no primary opponents and will return to office after the August 8 primary; election-reform advocates expressed concern about the high number of uncontested races.

IA.title: Unofficial 2026 Iowa primary turnout up from 2022
IA.summary: Iowa's unofficial post-primary figures show 411,525 total ballots cast — up from 356,140 in 2022 — with overall turnout rising to over 19% of registered voters; absentee ballot use dipped slightly compared to 2022.

ME.title: Graham Platner isn't going anywhere in Maine Senate race after latest controversy
ME.summary: With Maine's June 9 ranked-choice primary days away, Democratic Senate candidate Graham Platner is facing calls to exit the race following new reporting about his personal conduct but is declining to drop out, dividing Maine Democratic leaders ahead of the primary.

MN.title: Here are the candidates who did — and didn't — file for Minnesota's statewide races
MN.summary: Following the June 2 filing deadline and June 4 withdrawal deadline, this report documents which candidates secured ballot access for Minnesota's governor, U.S. Senate, and other statewide races ahead of the August 11 primary.

NH.title: NH News Recap: Final State House votes, 2026 hopefuls, and an exploding meteor
NH.summary: NHPR's June 5 recap covers the close of the 2026 legislative session including final votes on election-related bills, and reports that Governor Kelly Ayotte and Democratic challenger Cinde Warmington both filed their 2026 campaigns with the state.

SC.title: Early voting: Record turnout continues for S.C. primaries
SC.summary: As final-day early voting closes for South Carolina's June 9 primary, over 250,000 votes have been cast statewide — a record for a primary early voting period — with Richland, Charleston, and Greenville counties leading turnout.

SC.title: Final day to vote early in South Carolina's primary election
SC.summary: June 5 is the last day of early voting ahead of South Carolina's June 9 primary, with early voting centers open 8:30 a.m.–5 p.m.; the piece reminds voters of polling locations and June 9 primary hours of 7 a.m.–7 p.m.

SC.title: DECISION 2026: What to know before you vote in South Carolina primaries
SC.summary: A voter guide published on the final day of early voting covering what South Carolina voters need to know for the June 9 primary, including polling locations, ID requirements, and the runoff schedule for June 23.

UT.title: Republicans Eryn Russo and Darren Croft vie for GOP nomination in Utah's House District 41 primary
UT.summary: Profiles the two Republican candidates competing in the June 23 primary for Utah's House District 41 seat, part of pre-primary coverage of competitive state legislative races ahead of the August primary cycle.

VT.title: Windsor County Senate race heats up in Vermont
VT.summary: Multiple Democratic candidates are vying for three Windsor County Senate seats amid a broader wave of legislative retirements, reflecting significant candidate turnover across the Vermont Legislature ahead of the 2026 general election.

WY.title: Wyoming GOP sues state, challenges constitutionality of ban on pre-primary candidate endorsements
WY.summary: The Wyoming Republican Party filed a federal lawsuit challenging a state law that bars political parties from spending money to endorse primary candidates, seeking First Amendment protection to back specific Republicans in the August 18 primary.

AL.title: Secretary of State Wes Allen Reminds Alabamians of Absentee Voting Deadlines Ahead of June 2026 Primary Runoff Election
AL.summary: Alabama Secretary of State Wes Allen issued a formal reminder that absentee mail-in ballot applications must reach county managers by June 9 and completed mail-in ballots must arrive by noon on June 16 runoff day, the only pre-election-day voting option since Alabama does not offer in-person early voting.

AL.title: Alabama's June 16 Runoff Election: What Voters Need to Know
AL.summary: A voter guide ahead of Alabama's June 16 primary runoff covers key races including the Republican U.S. Senate contest, photo ID requirements, poll hours of 7 a.m.–7 p.m., and rules on party crossover voting.

AK.title: Sen. Dan Sullivan Accuses Democrats of Recruiting Alaska Senate Candidate With the Same Name
AK.summary: Incumbent Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan accused Democratic operatives of recruiting a same-named candidate, Dan J. Sullivan of Petersburg, to confuse voters in the August top-four primary; the NRSC threatened legal action while the Alaska Democratic Party denied involvement.

AZ.title: Voter Registration Deadline Is June 22 for Arizona's July Primary
AZ.summary: Arizona voters have until June 22 to register for the July 21 primary — the state's first under a new law that permanently moved it from August to the second-to-last Tuesday in July — with mail ballot distribution and early in-person voting beginning June 24.

CA.title: 5 Things to Know About California's Election Results
CA.summary: CalMatters highlighted key takeaways from California's June 2 primary as ballot counting continued: Democrat Xavier Becerra secured the top spot in the governor's race while the second general-election slot remained unresolved, with final certification not expected until July 2.

CA.title: Raman Overtakes Pratt in LA Mayoral Race; California Governor Contest Still Undetermined
CA.summary: Updated ballot counts show progressive Nithya Raman moved into second place in the Los Angeles mayoral race, while the California governor's second general-election spot between Hilton and Steyer remained too close to call as millions of mail ballots continued to be tabulated.

CO.title: Where the Three Republicans Running to Be Colorado's Next Governor Stand on the Top Issues
CO.summary: A voter guide profiles the three Republicans vying for the June 30 gubernatorial primary — state Sen. Barbara Kirkmeyer, state Rep. Scott Bottoms, and ministry leader Victor Marx — as mail ballots began dropping to voters statewide on June 8.

CO.title: Governor Candidate Conversations: Phil Weiser
CO.summary: KUNC published an in-depth interview with Democratic gubernatorial candidate Phil Weiser on the day Colorado county clerks began mailing primary ballots statewide and more than 350 drop boxes opened for the June 30 primary election.

DC.title: How Ranked-Choice Voting Works in D.C. and Why We May Not Know Winners Right Away
DC.summary: The Washington Post explained the mechanics of D.C.'s first-ever ranked-choice voting primary on June 16, including the multi-round tabulation process and the likelihood that winners in the competitive mayoral and council races may not be announced for days after Election Day.

FL.title: Candidate Qualifying Opens June 8 for Florida's 2026 Congressional and Statewide Races
FL.summary: Florida's official candidate qualifying period for federal, governor, cabinet, state legislative, and county offices opened at noon on June 8 and runs through noon June 12, determining who will appear on the August 18 primary and November 3 general election ballots.

FL.title: Florida Moving Toward Stricter Voting Requirements: What You Need to Know
FL.summary: A report on Florida's new SAVE Act — signed by Gov. DeSantis requiring proof of U.S. citizenship for voter registration — and ongoing legal challenges from the ACLU and League of Women Voters arguing the law will disenfranchise eligible citizens, including elderly voters and Puerto Ricans with pre-2010 birth certificates.

GA.title: Georgia election panel passes resolution allowing counties to use hand-marked ballots
GA.summary: Georgia's State Election Board passed a 3-1 resolution allowing counties to switch to hand-marked paper ballots if the legislature fails to resolve a July 1 deadline banning QR codes from the official ballot count, despite the Secretary of State's office contending the board overstepped its authority.
