GA.title: Early voting underway for June 16 runoff election in Georgia
GA.summary: Early voting opened statewide on June 8 for Georgia's June 16 primary runoff, featuring the Republican gubernatorial contest between Lt. Gov. Burt Jones and Rick Jackson and the GOP U.S. Senate runoff between Mike Collins and Derek Dooley.

IA.title: Lines of attack solidify against Iowa candidates for the general election
IA.summary: Days after Iowa's June 2 primary, campaigns and political organizations launched early attack ads targeting candidates in the governor's and U.S. Senate races, setting the tone for the November general election.

IA.title: Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear rallies with Iowa governor candidate Rob Sand
IA.summary: Democratic Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear campaigned in Des Moines for Iowa Democratic gubernatorial candidate Rob Sand, arguing his two wins in a heavily Republican state demonstrate a path to victory for Sand in Iowa.

IN.title: Beau Bayh defeats Blythe Potter for Democratic secretary of state nomination
IN.summary: Indiana Democrats selected Beau Bayh as their secretary of state nominee at the June 6 state convention, with Bayh earning 61% of delegate votes over Blythe Potter; Democrats also nominated candidates for state comptroller and treasurer.

MA.title: To avoid a costly ballot question fight, Massachusetts rent control supporters are floating a compromise
MA.summary: Supporters of a Massachusetts rent control ballot question offered a compromise to the Legislature: pass a bill repealing the statewide ban on rent control, and they will withdraw their ballot measure — a deal developed with major real estate developers that could reshape the November ballot landscape.

ME.title: Election Day is tomorrow. Some results likely won't be known until next week.
ME.summary: Ahead of Maine's June 9 primary, officials warn that several races — including governor and congressional primaries — are expected to require ranked-choice runoffs, with final results potentially not known until the week of June 19.

ME.title: Maine Election Day is Tuesday. Here's what you need to know.
ME.summary: Maine voters head to the polls June 9 to cast ranked-choice ballots in primaries for U.S. Senate, both congressional districts, governor, and dozens of legislative and local races.

ME.title: Politics chat: Maine to vote on Platner, California waits primary results
ME.summary: NPR discussed Democratic Senate primary candidate Graham Platner's decision to remain in Maine's June 9 race despite mounting controversies, as voters prepare to weigh in on his candidacy.

MT.title: 5 key takeaways from Montana's June 2 primary election
MT.summary: Montana Free Press analyzes results of the June 2 primary, where roughly 37.4% of registered voters participated; two federal candidates handpicked by retiring Republican predecessors won their primaries, while Democrats nominated Sam Forstag for the Western House seat over better-funded Ryan Busse.

NE.title: Nebraska Board of State Canvassers set to certify primary election results
NE.summary: Nebraska's Board of State Canvassers convened June 8 to officially certify the results of the May 12 primary, with the most notable result being the upset defeat of two-term Secretary of State Bob Evnen by Republican challenger Scott Petersen.

NJ.title: New Jersey primary election 2026: Here's who won and who lost, plus full results
NJ.summary: WHYY published a full recap of June 2 primary results including Justin Murphy winning the Republican Senate nomination to challenge Sen. Cory Booker, and key House race winners across all 12 districts heading to the November general election.

NJ.title: NJ Assembly passes state Voting Rights Act
NJ.summary: The New Jersey General Assembly passed the 'John R. Lewis Voter Empowerment Act of New Jersey,' creating a new Division of Voting Rights with broad investigative and enforcement authority aimed at prohibiting voter suppression and ensuring equitable ballot access regardless of race, language, or disability.

NM.title: Independent voters boost turnout in New Mexico's first semi-open primary election
NM.summary: More than 38,000 independent voters cast ballots in New Mexico's historic first semi-open primary on June 2, representing about 10% of registered independents, with more than three-quarters choosing Democratic ballots; the Secretary of State called the inaugural semi-open primary a success despite some voter awareness gaps.

ND.title: North Dakota launches new election results website ahead of primary
ND.summary: Ahead of the June 9 primary, North Dakota's Secretary of State launched a redesigned election results website featuring an interactive county and legislative district map, candidate search, and historical results dating back to 1889.

OH.title: Ohio House and Senate endorse a constitutional amendment for voter ID
OH.summary: The Ohio House joined the Senate in endorsing a constitutional amendment to enshrine photo voter ID requirements in the state constitution, clearing the way for the measure to appear on the November 2026 ballot.

OK.title: Oklahoma Voice launches voter guide ahead of June 16 primary election
OK.summary: Oklahoma Voice released a comprehensive voter guide ahead of the June 16 primary, covering over 635 races including the crowded U.S. Senate Republican primary to fill the seat left by Markwayne Mullin, with early in-person voting beginning June 11–13.

PA.title: Bob Brooks wins Pennsylvania's 7th District primary to take on Ryan Mackenzie in general election
PA.summary: Union leader Bob Brooks, backed by Gov. Josh Shapiro and national Democrats, won the competitive Democratic primary for Pennsylvania's 7th Congressional District, setting up a fall race against Republican incumbent Ryan Mackenzie in one of the state's most-watched battleground contests.

SC.title: SC Election Commission reports record-breaking early voting
SC.summary: The South Carolina Election Commission reported more than 318,600 ballots cast statewide during early voting for the June 9 primary, far surpassing 2024 totals of 120,178 and 2022 totals of 100,450, with officials crediting a competitive governor's race with no incumbent on the ballot.

SC.title: 2026 South Carolina primary election: What to know at the polls
SC.summary: South Carolina voters head to the polls June 9 to choose nominees for governor, U.S. Senate, Congress, and state legislative races, with polls open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. and runoffs set for June 23 if no candidate tops 50%.

VA.title: Virginia moves 2026 primary election date from June to August amid redistricting push
VA.summary: Virginia's August 4 primary will include primaries for U.S. Senate and several congressional districts, with early in-person voting starting June 19 and the independent candidate filing deadline for state offices remaining June 16.

WA.title: Foes of WA income tax race to collect initiative signatures
WA.summary: Opponents of Washington's new 9.9% tax on income above $1 million are racing to gather at least 308,911 valid voter signatures by a July 2 deadline to place a repeal initiative on the November ballot, with roughly 165,000 signatures collected as of early June.

WI.title: Wisconsin's crowded governor's race remains crowded after filing deadline
WI.summary: Eight Democrats and two Republicans qualified for Wisconsin's August 11 gubernatorial primary after the June 1 nomination paper deadline, with the Democratic field including Mandela Barnes, Lt. Gov. Sara Rodriguez, Joel Brennan, and Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley.

AL.title: Southern Baldwin County GOP primary heads to runoff
AL.summary: Incumbent Rep. Frances Holk-Jones and investment adviser Joe Freeman are headed to the June 16 Republican primary runoff for House District 95 in southern Baldwin County, after neither secured a majority in the May 19 primary.

CA.title: How to fix California's 'pig in a python' long vote-counting process
CA.summary: California's lengthy ballot-counting process has again drawn scrutiny after the June 2 primary, with final results from the governor and LA mayor races still not confirmed nearly a week later; the secretary of state has until July 10 to certify results.

CA.title: Nithya Raman overtakes Spencer Pratt for 2nd place in LA mayoral race, results show
CA.summary: As mail-in ballots continued to be counted in the June 2 Los Angeles primary, City Council member Nithya Raman overtook Republican Spencer Pratt for second place, putting her on track to advance to the November runoff against incumbent Mayor Karen Bass.

DC.title: Early voting begins in DC primary election
DC.summary: Early voting opened Monday, June 8 across Washington D.C. ahead of the June 16 primary, the first in the District to use ranked-choice voting; vote centers are open through June 14, with same-day voter registration available at all locations.

DC.title: Get to know all the candidates running for office in DC's primary election
DC.summary: With early voting underway ahead of D.C.'s June 16 primary, WTOP profiled all candidates running for mayor, delegate to Congress, attorney general, and council seats in the historic first election using ranked-choice voting in the District.

DE.title: Delaware seeks state-level voting rights legislation post U.S. Supreme Court decision
DE.summary: State Rep. Larry Lambert introduced HB 444, the Delaware John Lewis Voting Rights Act, which would prohibit discriminatory voting practices and give individuals, organizations, and the Attorney General standing to challenge such practices — making Delaware the first state to propose this type of protection following the Supreme Court's decision in Callais v. Louisiana.

HI.title: Can Tommy Waters Even Run For A Third Honolulu Council Term?
HI.summary: Election law scholars say the Honolulu City Charter's term-limits language is ambiguous as to whether Council Chair Tommy Waters is eligible to run for a third consecutive term, following a formal objection filed by a voter with the city clerk.

IA.title: Crawford County Supervisor Dave Muhlbauer picked as Rob Sand's gubernatorial running mate
IA.summary: Democratic gubernatorial nominee Rob Sand announced Crawford County Supervisor Dave Muhlbauer, a fifth-generation western Iowa farmer, as his running mate; Muhlbauer is set to be formally nominated at the Iowa Democratic Party state convention.

ID.title: Board of Canvassers Certify Election Results; Audit Results Reported
ID.summary: The Idaho State Board of Canvassers met June 9 to officially certify the May 19, 2026 primary election results, with final turnout recorded at 27.9% of registered voters; post-election audit results from eight counties were also presented to the board.

IN.title: Beau Bayh defeats Blythe Potter for Democratic secretary of state nomination
IN.summary: Indiana Democrats chose Beau Bayh as their secretary of state nominee at the June 6 state convention, with Bayh earning 61% of delegate votes; he pledged to conduct an independent audit of the office and expand voter participation, with the Republican convention nomination set for June 20 in Fort Wayne.

IN.title: Secretary of State race getting national attention ahead of the Indiana Republican Convention
IN.summary: The contest to choose the Republican nominee for Indiana Secretary of State has drawn national attention as 1,800 GOP convention delegates prepare to decide whether to renominate incumbent Diego Morales or select one of three challengers at the June 20 convention.

KS.title: Insults fly as Kansas GOP gubernatorial candidates compete for dominance during debate
KS.summary: Four Republican candidates for Kansas governor debated in Overland Park, with exchanges focused on property taxes, a proposed Kansas City Chiefs stadium deal, and abortion policy ahead of the August 4 primary.

LA.title: Louisiana U.S. Senate Race: Letlow, Fleming make case to Southwest Louisiana voters
LA.summary: Republican Senate runoff candidates Rep. Julia Letlow and State Treasurer John Fleming participated in a forum in Sulphur hosted by Republican Women Ambassadors, making their case to Southwest Louisiana voters ahead of the June 27 runoff election.

MD.title: An endorsement parade U-turn, an electric bill break — sort of — in political notes
MD.summary: Gov. Wes Moore issued a new round of endorsements ahead of the June 23 primary, including backing Montgomery County Councilmember Will Jawando for county executive, reversing course from his prior endorsement omission.

MD.title: After raft of appointments, District 16 voters will finally get their say
MD.summary: Democratic voters in Maryland's District 16 will cast ballots in the June 23 primary, marking the first voter say in the district after a series of appointments filled the seat.

MI.title: Federal government investigating potential noncitizen voters in Macomb County
MI.summary: Homeland Security Investigations has subpoenaed Macomb County as part of an active investigation into potential noncitizen voters after County Clerk Anthony Forlini identified 15 potentially registered noncitizens; the Michigan Department of State is also investigating whether any cast ballots.

MO.title: Missouri appeals court rewrites Amendment 5 language to make clear it allows new sales taxes
MO.summary: The Missouri Western District Court of Appeals rewrote the ballot summary for Amendment 5 — which would direct lawmakers to eliminate the income tax by expanding sales taxes — ruling the original summary did not sufficiently inform voters about the sales tax expansion mechanism.

MO.title: Missouri Supreme Court declines to hear appeal over Amendment 5 ballot summary
MO.summary: The Missouri Supreme Court declined to hear an appeal of the rewritten ballot summary for Amendment 5, leaving the appeals court language in place just before the June 9 deadline to finalize ballot language for the August 4 primary.

MO.title: Missouri Supreme Court keeps in place rewritten ballot language for August vote on state tax plan
MO.summary: The Missouri Supreme Court let stand the appeals court's revised ballot summary for Amendment 5's income-tax elimination plan, clearing the way for the measure to appear on the August ballot with updated language emphasizing the sales tax expansion component.

MT.title: Montana Senate race takes shape as Bankhead emerges from Democratic primary
MT.summary: Following the June 2 primary, the Montana U.S. Senate general election is set between Republican Kurt Alme, Democrat Alani Bankhead, and independent Seth Bodnar. Bankhead pledged to remain in the race despite pressure to clear the field for Bodnar against Trump-backed Alme.

ND.title: North Dakota's new election results website goes live for Tuesday's primary
ND.summary: North Dakota launched a redesigned election results website ahead of the June 9 primary, featuring enhanced filtering options, an interactive map, and multiple search methods for viewing results.

ND.title: North Dakota could become the 17th state to have a single-subject rule for ballot initiatives
ND.summary: North Dakota voters will decide on Constitutional Amendment 1 in the June 9 primary, which would create a single-subject rule for future constitutional amendments, requiring that each proposed amendment address only one topic.

ND.title: What North Dakotans need to know before Tuesday's primary
ND.summary: A voter guide covering the June 9 North Dakota primary, including contested statewide races for attorney general, secretary of state, and other offices, plus the constitutional ballot measure on single-subject rules for future amendments.

NH.title: NH Secretary of State clarifies court ruling pertains only to voters who use affidavits for proof of citizenship
NH.summary: New Hampshire Secretary of State Dave Scanlan clarified that the federal court's ruling striking down HB 1569 restores the use of affidavits only for proving citizenship at registration, while other provisions of the law remain in effect for the 2026 elections.

NH.title: Hitting the trail: Candidate filing period continues at NH State House
NH.summary: The New Hampshire candidate filing period for the September 8 primary is ongoing through June 12, with notable filings including Democrat Chris Pappas for U.S. Senate and both major gubernatorial candidates already in.

NV.title: Here's what to know for Nevada's 2026 state primary
NV.summary: A preview of Nevada's June 9 primary election, covering key races including the contested Republican gubernatorial primary with Gov. Joe Lombardo facing six challengers, the Democratic gubernatorial contest, and U.S. House and state legislature seats.

NV.title: More than 270,000 Nevadans have participated in the primary elections
NV.summary: More than 270,000 Nevadans had voted in person or returned mail ballots heading into the June 9 primary election day, with roughly equal participation from Democrats and Republicans at about 42% each.

NY.title: New York Democrats set stage for voter referendum to join redistricting fight
NY.summary: New York Democrats in the state legislature approved first passage of a constitutional amendment that would remove anti-gerrymandering prohibitions and allow mid-decade congressional redistricting, setting the stage for a statewide voter referendum if it passes again in 2027.

OK.title: Early voting begins this week ahead of June 16 primary election in Oklahoma
OK.summary: Early voting for Oklahoma's June 16 primary begins June 11-12 from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. and June 13 from 8 a.m. to 2 p.m., with key races including a new governor, U.S. Senate nominees, and a minimum wage ballot measure.

SD.title: SD RUNOFF ABSENTEE VOTING BEGINS FRIDAY
SD.summary: South Dakota Secretary of State Monae L. Johnson announced that absentee voting for the Republican gubernatorial runoff election begins Friday, June 12, ahead of the July 28 runoff between Gov. Larry Rhoden and businessman Toby Doeden. Voters who didn't request a primary absentee ballot must submit a new application to their county auditor by July 27.

TX.title: Election Races: June 13 North Texas runoff
TX.summary: North Texas voters head to the polls Saturday, June 13 for runoff elections stemming from May's local municipal races, with contested races for mayor and city council in Frisco, Grand Prairie, Irving, DeSoto, and other North Texas cities.

UT.title: 2026 primary elections in Northern Utah: candidate profiles for Weber, Davis counties
UT.summary: Candidate profiles for the June 23 primary races in Weber and Davis counties, covering state legislative districts and local school board seats. Ballots have been mailed to all active registered voters and early in-person voting opens June 9; the voter registration deadline is June 12.

WI.title: Democratic State Convention Could Narrow Field for Wisconsin Governor
WI.summary: Wisconsin Democrats gather in Madison June 13-14 for their annual state convention, where the crowded seven-way Democratic primary for governor takes center stage ahead of the August 11 primary. Democratic leaders hope the convention will serve as a clarifying moment among candidates.

WI.title: Wisconsin Democrats' convention could clarify field of candidates for governor
WI.summary: Democratic caucus and county party leaders told Wisconsin Watch they hope the upcoming June 13-14 state convention will be a clarifying moment in the seven-way Democratic primary for governor, with the Wisconsin Elections Commission set to certify ballot access for all candidates on June 9.

AK.title: State opens probe into Sen. Dan Sullivan's namesake challenger as he says he can legally run
AK.summary: Alaska officials opened an investigation into a Petersburg Republican named Dan J. Sullivan who filed to run for the U.S. Senate seat held by incumbent Dan S. Sullivan, with Lt. Gov. Dahlstrom citing credible allegations that the challenger coordinated with another campaign to confuse voters.

AK.title: Two Dan Sullivans: Alaska Lt. Gov. launches investigation into involvement of 'another candidate'
AK.summary: Alaska Lt. Governor Nancy Dahlstrom launched a formal investigation into whether Dan J. Sullivan, a GOP challenger sharing the incumbent senator name, filed his candidacy in coordination with another campaign to mislead voters ahead of the August 18 primary.

AL.title: 2026 Primary Election Runoff Voter Guide
AL.summary: June 9 is the deadline for mailed-in absentee ballot applications for Alabama's June 16 primary runoff. Runoff races include the U.S. Senate seat vacated by Tommy Tuberville and the Lieutenant Governor's Office.

AR.title: Arkansas judge tosses lawsuit challenging secretary of state GOP runoff results
AR.summary: Pulaski County Circuit Judge Tim Fox dismissed Bryan Norris's election challenge to the March 31 Republican runoff for Arkansas Secretary of State with prejudice, finding Norris failed to prove any election laws were violated after six recount verifications.

AR.title: Judge dismisses challenge to Arkansas secretary of state recount
AR.summary: A Pulaski County judge dismissed Bryan Norris's challenge to the Arkansas Secretary of State recount, affirming all six counties had identical vote totals after recounts, ending his legal effort to overturn Kim Hammer's 51%-49% primary runoff victory.

AZ.title: Outside counsel investigates 'theft' claims against Heap's office over voting equipment
AZ.summary: The Maricopa County Board of Supervisors hired outside counsel to investigate whether Recorder's Office employees improperly removed a pre-tabulation election scanner, resulting in a 0,000 replacement and criminal investigations of election workers ahead of the July 21 primary.

AZ.title: Maricopa County recorder, board clash over election equipment investigation
AZ.summary: Maricopa County Recorder Justin Heap filed an emergency court motion after armed sheriff's deputies visited election workers' homes as part of a criminal investigation, escalating the dispute with the Board of Supervisors over election equipment weeks before the July 21 primary.

CA.title: Nithya Raman advances over Spencer Pratt to face L.A. Mayor Karen Bass in a runoff
CA.summary: NBC News projected that Los Angeles City Councilmember Nithya Raman will advance to the November runoff against Mayor Karen Bass, after Raman overtook Spencer Pratt in continuing ballot counts from the June 2 California primary election.

CO.title: Colorado's primary election ballots are in the mail
CO.summary: Colorado county clerks began mailing June 30 primary election ballots to all active registered voters starting June 8, with drop boxes opened statewide; unaffiliated voters receive both party ballots but may only return one.

CO.title: County Clerks May Begin Mailing Ballots for the 2026 Primary Election
CO.summary: Colorado county clerks began mailing primary ballots June 8 for the June 30 primary; voters must return ballots by 7 p.m. on Election Day, with a June 22 registration deadline to receive a mailed ballot.

CT.title: CT Republicans Gather Petition Signatures For MacCormack Primary Challenge
CT.summary: Connecticut Republicans raced to collect 238 petition signatures by the June 9 filing deadline to place a primary challenger against their own endorsed House candidate Jadon MacCormack, who faced condemnation for anti-LGBTQ statements.

CT.title: Connecticut Republicans seek primary challenger to candidate over anti-gay posts
CT.summary: Connecticut Republicans were gathering petition signatures to get an alternative candidate on the August 11 primary ballot against endorsed House District 50 candidate Jadon MacCormack, who made extreme anti-LGBTQ statements, with the June 9 deadline driving an urgent signature drive.

DC.title: Ranked choice voting begins in DC: How to make sure your vote counts
DC.summary: With D.C.'s historic first use of ranked choice voting underway in early voting ahead of the June 16 primary, WJLA explains how voters can fill out ranked choice ballots. Under the new system, voters can rank up to five candidates in races with three or more candidates.

GA.title: Georgia House Special Runoff Election 2026 Live Results
GA.summary: Georgia held special election runoffs on June 9, including the congressional seat vacated by Marjorie Taylor Greene where Republican Clay Fuller, backed by President Trump, defeated Democrat Shawn Harris, and a Lowndes County state house race.

GA.title: Early voting begins in the 2026 Georgia primary runoffs | What's on the ballot and how to find your polling place
GA.summary: Early voting kicked off June 9 across Georgia ahead of the June 16 primary runoff election, with voters weighing in on the Republican governor's race between Lt. Gov. Burt Jones and Rick Jackson, and the GOP U.S. Senate runoff between Derek Dooley and Mike Collins.

HI.title: Hawaii's primary election unlikely to stir voter enthusiasm, turnout
HI.summary: Political analysts predict Hawaii will see continued low voter turnout for the 2026 primary, with the August 8 primary expected to draw less than a third of registered voters due to the absence of high-profile competitive races including no U.S. Senate contest.

HI.title: Primary elections unlikely to stir voter enthusiasm, turnout
HI.summary: Hawaii's August 8 primary is expected to see very low voter participation, with analysts noting only 32.3% of registered voters cast ballots in the previous primary. Party leaders express concern about voter apathy amid few competitive races.

HI.title: Suit challenges campaign spending activity law
HI.summary: The Grassroot Institute of Hawaii filed a federal lawsuit seeking to invalidate a new state law barring campaign spending activity by companies, labor unions, and other organizations in elections and ballot measures, less than a month after the bill was signed into law.

IN.title: Beau Bayh defeats Blythe Potter for Democratic secretary of state nomination
IN.summary: Beau Bayh won the Democratic nomination for Indiana secretary of state at the June 6 state convention, earning 61% of delegate votes over challenger Blythe Potter and positioning himself for a general election race against incumbent Republican Diego Morales.

IN.title: Closed primaries are in vogue with Indiana Republicans. But what would they look like?
IN.summary: Indiana Republicans have been pushing to close the state's open primary system following allegations of Democratic crossover voting in a state senate race, with multiple legislative attempts and growing momentum ahead of the June 20 GOP state convention.

KS.title: Kansas political battles await after 5 Republicans decline to seek reelection to Board of Education
KS.summary: Five Republican incumbents on the Kansas State Board of Education will not seek reelection in 2026, creating 14-candidate primary races for the August 4 primary and setting up a significant contest for control of the board in November.

KS.title: 5 Republicans are leaving Kansas Board of Education, setting up election fight for political control
KS.summary: The departure of five Republican Board of Education incumbents, including one who joined a gubernatorial ticket as a running mate, is opening the most competitive board races in years, with Democrats fielding candidates in all five open districts.

ME.title: It's primary day. Here's what Maine voters need to know.
ME.summary: Maine voters headed to polls on June 9 to choose Democratic and Republican nominees for governor, U.S. Senate, Congress, and dozens of legislative seats. Several crowded races are expected to require ranked-choice runoff tabulation, with final results possibly not known until mid-June.

ME.title: Maine Senate primary election live results: Embattled Graham Platner runs
ME.summary: Maine voters decided in the June 9 primary who will be the Democratic nominee to challenge incumbent Republican U.S. Sen. Susan Collins in November. Oyster farmer Graham Platner faced former state official David Costello in the Democratic primary, with results expected to take days due to ranked-choice counting.

ME.title: Here are Maine's 2026 primary election results
ME.summary: Maine held its June 9 primary with races for U.S. Senate, governor, and both congressional districts. Due to Maine's ranked-choice voting system, final results for several races may not be confirmed until the tabulation process is completed the following week.

ME.title: Maine 2026 live primary election results
ME.summary: ABC News tracked live results from Maine's June 9 primary election, covering contests for governor, U.S. Senate, and both congressional districts. The Democratic U.S. Senate primary featured Graham Platner, Janet Mills, and David Costello vying for the nomination to face Sen. Susan Collins in November.

ME.title: How Maine's Tuesday votes will be counted from Election Day to next week
ME.summary: Maine held its June 9 primary election using ranked-choice voting for governor, Congress, and state legislature races. Final results in several races may take up to two weeks as the secretary of state's office conducts ranked-choice tabulation in Augusta.

ND.title: LIVE BLOG: Read election coverage for June 9, 2026
ND.summary: The Grand Forks Herald ran live election coverage for North Dakota's June 9 all-mail primary, featuring the contested U.S. House race between Trump-endorsed Rep. Julie Fedorchak and NDGOP-endorsed Alex Balazs, plus statewide offices and a constitutional ballot measure.

ND.title: Key North Dakota primary races still too close to call, election official says
ND.summary: After North Dakota's June 9 all-mail primary, election officials reported several key races remained too close to call as counties continued tallying roughly 41,000 outstanding ballots on the state's new election results website.

ND.title: North Dakota voters to decide on single subject rule for ballot measures
ND.summary: North Dakota voters decided on Constitutional Measure 1 on June 9, which would require future constitutional amendments to address a single subject, a measure the legislature approved 75-26 in the House and 30-9 in the Senate.

ND.title: Here are North Dakota's 2026 primary election results
ND.summary: North Dakota voters headed to the polls June 9 for primary elections, with incumbent Republican U.S. Rep. Julie Fedorchak facing challenger Alex Balazs, and voters also deciding on Constitutional Amendment 1 that would create a single-subject rule for future constitutional amendments.

NV.title: Nevada primary election results 2026: Live updates
NV.summary: NPR's live coverage of Nevada's June 9 primary election, tracking results for contested races including the governor's race, attorney general, and U.S. House seats. Democratic AG Aaron Ford and Washoe County Commission Chair Alexis Hill were top contenders for the Democratic gubernatorial nomination.

NV.title: Nevada 2026 live primary election results
NV.summary: ABC News tracked live results for Nevada's June 9 primary, covering the governor's race, attorney general, and nonpartisan mayoral races in Henderson and North Las Vegas where the top two finishers advance to the general election.

NY.title: How to watch New York's 12th Congressional District debate on NY1
NY.summary: NY1 announced a live June 9 debate featuring Democratic candidates for the open NY-12 seat being vacated by retiring Rep. Jerry Nadler, including George Conway, Jack Schlossberg, and others, ahead of the June 23 primary.

NY.title: Trump looms large in New York House debate featuring George Conway, Jack Schlossberg
NY.summary: Coverage of the NY1-hosted debate for New York's 12th Congressional District Democratic primary, where candidates clashed over tech and crypto industry ties, super PAC funding, and Trump administration policies. Nine candidates compete in the June 23 primary to succeed Rep. Jerry Nadler.

OH.title: Ohio GOP's voter ID amendment remains unchanged, for now
OH.summary: The Ohio House general government committee reviewed the photo voter ID constitutional amendment (SJR 10) but adjourned without making changes, despite pressure from President Trump urging Republicans to place it on the November ballot.

OR.title: Oregon Primary Election Moves Toward Final Certification as Counties Complete Audits and Ballot Reviews
OR.summary: County election offices across Oregon are completing ballot reviews, audits, and canvassing required before statewide certification of the May 19 primary results, set for June 25. Officials are conducting mandatory post-election hand count audits required under Oregon law in all 36 counties.

SC.title: Here are South Carolina's 2026 primary election results
SC.summary: South Carolina held its June 9 statewide primary with polls open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Key races included the Republican governor's primary between Trump-endorsed Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette and Rep. Nancy Mace, plus U.S. Senate and attorney general contests; races without a majority head to a June 23 runoff.

SC.title: South Carolina primary election live results: Evette, Mace vie for governor
SC.summary: The Washington Post covered live results from South Carolina's June 9 primary, spotlighting the competitive Republican governor's race and noting record early voting turnout with more than 319,000 ballots cast before Election Day.

SC.title: South Carolina heads to the polls today: What to know about voting in the 2026 primary
SC.summary: Voters in South Carolina headed to the polls for the June 9 primary election, with polls open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., coming off a record-breaking early voting period in which more than 319,000 ballots were cast.

SC.title: Polls open in Columbia for primary election day. What to know if you're heading out to vote.
SC.summary: The Post and Courier reported on polls opening across South Carolina on June 9 for the state's first open governor's race in 16 years, with record early turnout of 319,000 ballots already cast before Election Day.

SC.title: SC Primary Election Day: Polling locations, what to bring and ballot changes
SC.summary: Live 5 News published an Election Day guide for South Carolina voters covering polling locations, required identification, and ballot changes in effect for the June 9 primary.

TX.title: Local Texas election officials await appointment of new secretary of state as midterm preparations ramp up
TX.summary: Following Secretary of State Jane Nelson's resignation effective July 17, local Texas election officials expressed concern that the transition could disrupt midterm preparations including voter registration processing, poll worker recruitment, and election guidance.

UT.title: Utah same-day voter registration: How to register to vote on election day
UT.summary: The Salt Lake Tribune explains how Utah voters can still register and cast a ballot for the June 23 primary using same-day registration at early voting locations (which begin June 9) or at polling places on election day with two forms of ID. The online registration deadline is June 12.

WV.title: Del. Kimble challenges election loss, says GOP ballots exceeded number of registered GOP voters
WV.summary: Del. Laura Kimble, R-Harrison, formally challenged her six-vote primary loss to Tim McNeely, filing a contest with the Harrison County Commission citing discrepancies where Republican ballots counted exceeded the number of registered Republicans who voted in multiple precincts.

WV.title: Kimble files election contest after primary loss
WV.summary: Incumbent Delegate Laura Kimble filed a formal election contest following her narrow six-vote loss to challenger Tim McNeely in the May Republican primary, alleging voting irregularities in Harrison County's 71st House District race.

WY.title: Judge fills Weston County clerk vacancy
WY.summary: A district court judge appointed James Michael Tooman as Weston County clerk after county commissioners failed to agree on a replacement for the former clerk, who resigned following two years of investigations into election administration mistakes.

MI.title: UAW endorsement of Benson, El-Sayed shakes up gubernatorial, U.S. Senate races in final stretch
MI.summary: The United Auto Workers union endorsed Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate and Jocelyn Benson for governor in a joint announcement, injecting major labor firepower into Michigan's August 4 Democratic primaries and potentially reshaping both races.

MI.title: Michigan's U.S. Senate primary highlights divisions within Democratic Party
MI.summary: With the August 4 primary approaching, candidates Haley Stevens, Mallory McMorrow, and Abdul El-Sayed are clashing over foreign policy, ICE abolition, and party leadership, reflecting deep divisions within Michigan's Democratic Party over its direction.

OK.title: Early voting for the Oklahoma primary election begins Thursday
OK.summary: Early in-person voting for Oklahoma's June 16 primary opens Thursday, June 11, covering federal, state, and local races plus State Question 832 to raise the minimum wage.

OK.title: Early voting starts Thursday in Oklahoma primaries
OK.summary: KTEN reports that early voting for the June 16 Oklahoma primaries begins Thursday at local county election boards, with races for governor, a new U.S. senator, congressional seats, and a minimum-wage ballot measure all on the ballot.

OK.title: Early voting starts Thursday ahead of the June 16 primary
OK.summary: Oklahoma Voice notes that in-person early voting for the closed June 16 primary opens June 11–13, with no independent voters permitted; races include governor, U.S. Senate, and a minimum-wage state question.

PA.title: UPenn Study: Ballot Curing Helps More Mail-In Ballots Get Counted
PA.summary: A University of Pennsylvania study of the 2024 election found that Pennsylvania voters notified of mail ballot errors were 25 percentage points more likely to have their votes counted, adding evidence for expanding 'notice and cure' policies statewide.

RI.title: Better luck next year, Rhode Island Voting Rights Act. Here's why it stalled this session.
RI.summary: Rhode Island's Senate President, House Speaker, and Secretary of State jointly announced the Rhode Island Voting Rights Act — which would have protected minority voters from suppression and racial gerrymandering — will not receive a vote before the end of the 2026 legislative session, with leaders pledging to bring it back in 2027.

RI.title: R.I. Assembly won't vote on a state Voting Rights Act this year
RI.summary: Rhode Island legislators confirmed they will not bring the state Voting Rights Act (S3143/H8334) to a floor vote in 2026, citing concerns from the Attorney General's office about enforcement scope and legal exposure, delaying a high-profile bipartisan initiative.

TN.title: Tennessee Democrats dropped their federal lawsuit challenging the state's new congressional map. Here's why
TN.summary: The Tennessee Democratic Party voluntarily dismissed its federal lawsuit challenging the state's redrawn congressional map — which carved majority-Black Memphis into three districts — after a judge denied expedited relief for the 2026 cycle, while three other federal redistricting challenges from the NAACP, ACLU, and League of Women Voters remain active.

TN.title: Federal lawsuit challenging Tennessee's new congressional map dismissed
TN.summary: A federal judge dismissed the Tennessee Democrats' lawsuit against the new gerrymander without prejudice, closing the case while leaving the congressional map in place for 2026, as the party chair said their focus has shifted to defeating Republicans at the ballot box in November.

VT.title: Governor Scott signs 16 bills, including H.930 and S.227
VT.summary: Vermont Gov. Phil Scott signed S.298, the Vermont Voter Protections Act, into law on June 8, 2026 — legislation that strengthens penalties for election interference, establishes a new offense for intimidating voters or election officials, and updates rules on voter checklist use, candidate disclosures, and election security.

WI.title: Wisconsin election: Governor candidates on August primary ballot
WI.summary: The Wisconsin Elections Commission certified nine candidates for the August 11 governor's primary on June 9: seven Democrats (including Mandela Barnes, David Crowley, Sara Rodriguez, Kelda Roys, Francesca Hong, Missy Hughes, and Joel Brennan) and two Republicans (Tom Tiffany and Andy Manske).

WI.title: Controversial liberal Kirk Bangstad denied ballot access in bid for Wisconsin governor
WI.summary: The Wisconsin Elections Commission voted unanimously on June 9 to deny Minocqua Brewing Co. owner Kirk Bangstad a spot on the August primary ballot after his campaign submitted only 1,504 of the required 2,000 valid signatures, partly due to circulators listing the wrong election date on nomination forms.

WI.title: Wisconsin governor's race set with 9 certified candidates on the ballot
WI.summary: Following the Elections Commission's June 9 ballot-access meeting, WKOW confirmed nine certified governor candidates for the August primary, alongside certification of independent candidates for the November general election.

CA.title: California governor's race narrows to Hilton, Becerra runoff
CA.summary: With 91% of ballots counted a week after California's June 2 primary, Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton have solidified their positions as the top two candidates advancing to the November general election for governor, as ongoing mail-ballot counting continues to shape final results.

CT.title: Ruth Fortune's hopes for congressional primary ride in a tote bag
CT.summary: Political outsider Ruth Fortune delivered thousands of petition signatures to registrars in an attempt to qualify for Connecticut's 1st Congressional District Democratic primary, potentially becoming the first candidate to force a primary via petition against an incumbent congressman in the state.

DC.title: Ranked choice voting will delay DC primary results
DC.summary: DC's first-ever ranked choice voting primary on June 16 means final results won't be known until at least June 26, as the Board of Elections must wait 10 days after Election Day to receive all mail ballots before completing tabulations through multiple elimination rounds.

DC.title: DC polls open for early voting: What to know
DC.summary: Early voting is underway at 25 locations ahead of DC's June 16 primary, the first election in the District to use ranked choice voting; same-day voter registration is available at all early vote centers with proof of residence.

DE.title: Delaware House Bill 430 could ban corporations from voting in municipal elections statewide
DE.summary: Delaware House Bill 430 would prohibit corporations from voting in any Delaware election, a direct legislative response to a May 26 court ruling that upheld Fenwick Island's town charter allowing corporations to cast ballots in local elections.

FL.title: Florida appeals court rejects bid to send redistricting challenge to state Supreme Court
FL.summary: Florida's First District Court of Appeal rejected a motion to bypass the appeals court and send the congressional map challenge directly to the state Supreme Court, keeping the gerrymandering lawsuit in the lower appellate track as candidate qualifying week begins.

GA.title: Georgia runoff election: More than 100,000 ballots cast as early voting begins
GA.summary: More than 130,000 Georgians had cast ballots in the June 16 primary runoff by June 10, with Republicans outpacing Democrats roughly 2-to-1 in early in-person voting ahead of a runoff featuring the Republican governor and U.S. Senate primaries.

IN.title: How GOP candidates are pitching themselves for Indiana secretary of state bid
IN.summary: Four Republican candidates including incumbent Secretary of State Diego Morales are making final pitches to roughly 1,800 delegates ahead of the June 20 Indiana GOP state convention, where the party will nominate its candidate for the state's top election official post.

MA.title: The Massachusetts legislative races to watch
MA.summary: An overview of competitive Massachusetts state legislative races in the 2026 cycle ahead of the September 1 primary, examining key contests across the state legislature that will shape the November ballot.

MA.title: Moulton, Deaton to participate in Massachusetts' first-ever interparty primary debate
MA.summary: Democratic Senate challenger Seth Moulton and Republican John Deaton agreed to participate in what is being described as Massachusetts' first-ever interparty primary debate, scheduled for June 16 on WBZ, while incumbent Sen. Ed Markey declined to participate.

MD.title: Voter Guide: 2026 Primary election
MD.summary: A comprehensive voter guide for Maryland's June 23 primary covering key races including Gov. Wes Moore's re-election bid, competitive congressional and state legislative races, and early voting details with voting centers opening June 11.

MD.title: Maryland 2026 election guide: Voting, deadlines and key races
MD.summary: A guide for Maryland voters covering voting options, registration, early voting beginning June 11, and key races including the gubernatorial contest and eight U.S. House seats on the June 23 primary ballot.

MN.title: The DFL backed Flanagan for Senate, but the money's on Craig
MN.summary: Despite winning the DFL endorsement for Minnesota's open U.S. Senate seat, Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan trails Rep. Angie Craig significantly in fundraising — nearly $5 million to $1 million — with heavy outside PAC spending expected before the August 11 primary.

MO.title: Amendment 5 ballot summary remains in place after Supreme Court declines to hear appeal
MO.summary: The Missouri Supreme Court declined to review changes to the ballot summary for Amendment 5, which would allow lawmakers to phase out the state income tax and expand sales taxes, leaving in place the revised ballot language for the August 4 primary.

MS.title: National redistricting battle turns to statehouses and city councils
MS.summary: Following the Supreme Court's Callais decision weakening the Voting Rights Act, redistricting battles are shifting to state legislatures and local governments, with the Court sending Mississippi's legislative redistricting cases filed on behalf of Black voters back to lower courts.

MT.title: More Montanans cast ballots in this election than any other midterm primary
MT.summary: Montana's June 2 primary drew more than 300,000 voters for the first time in a midterm primary year, setting a new raw-vote record even as the turnout rate as a share of registered voters declined to 37.9%, reflecting the state's growing electorate.

ND.title: Fedorchak wins North Dakota Republican primary
ND.summary: Congresswoman Julie Fedorchak won North Dakota's Republican primary with over 72% of the vote, defeating NDGOP-endorsed challenger Alex Balazs in the June 9 primary and advancing to face Democrat Trygve Hammer in the November general election.

ND.title: North Dakota voters approve single-subject amendment requirement
ND.summary: North Dakota voters approved Constitutional Measure 1 with about 66% in favor, requiring future constitutional amendments to address only a single subject and empowering the Secretary of State to reject initiative petitions covering more than one subject.

NJ.title: NJ election 2026: How did Hamawy win the 12th District primary?
NJ.summary: Army veteran Adam Hamawy won New Jersey's 12th Congressional District Democratic primary among 13 candidates, capitalizing on the elimination of the controversial county-line ballot system and outside PAC spending, setting up a general election race to succeed retiring Rep. Bonnie Watson Coleman.

NV.title: Here are Nevada's 2026 primary election results
NV.summary: Recap of Nevada's June 9 primary: Attorney General Aaron Ford won the Democratic gubernatorial nomination with 66% of the vote to face incumbent GOP Gov. Joe Lombardo in November, while key legislative and down-ballot primaries also concluded.

OK.title: Early Voting Begins Thursday for June 16 Election
OK.summary: Oklahoma's in-person early voting for the June 16 primary election opens June 11-13 at county election board locations statewide, with the primary featuring nine Republican gubernatorial candidates and ballot measure State Question 832 on raising the minimum wage.

OK.title: Everything you need to know about Oklahoma primaries on June 16
OK.summary: Oklahoma voters head to the polls June 16 in a closed primary featuring nine Republican and three Democratic gubernatorial candidates, plus State Question 832 which would raise the state minimum wage to $15 an hour by 2029.

SC.title: AP projects: Republicans Pamela Evette, Alan Wilson heading to runoff in 2026 South Carolina governor primary
SC.summary: Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette (Trump-endorsed) and Attorney General Alan Wilson advance to a June 23 Republican gubernatorial runoff after neither secured a majority in South Carolina's June 9 primary, with the runoff winner facing Democratic nominee state Rep. Jermaine Johnson in November.

SC.title: Nancy Mace concedes SC governor race, endorses AG Alan Wilson
SC.summary: U.S. Rep. Nancy Mace finished fifth in the Republican gubernatorial primary and conceded, endorsing Attorney General Alan Wilson for the June 23 runoff against Trump-backed Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette.

SC.title: South Carolina primary results: Several races head to runoff
SC.summary: South Carolina's June 9 primary sent multiple statewide races — including the governor's contest and agriculture commissioner — to June 23 runoffs after no candidate secured an outright majority.

TX.title: James Talarico leads Ken Paxton by 3 points in Texas Senate race poll
TX.summary: A Texas Pulse poll found Democrat James Talarico leading Republican Ken Paxton 47% to 44% in the U.S. Senate general election race, with Talarico holding an 18-point advantage among independent voters.

VA.title: Judge approves settlement over rejected Virginia student voter registrations
VA.summary: A federal judge approved a consent decree barring Virginia election officials from rejecting student voter registration applications solely for omitting dormitory-specific details like room numbers, resolving an NAACP-led lawsuit that found the practice disproportionately affected students at historically Black colleges.

WA.title: Why AG Nick Brown wants the Supreme Court involved in WA's redistricting fight
WA.summary: Washington Attorney General Nick Brown explained his request for the U.S. Supreme Court to accept and remand the state's legislative redistricting case, arguing that court-approved maps for Latino voters in the Yakima Valley must be re-evaluated under the new standard set by Louisiana v. Callais.

WI.title: The Democratic field for Wisconsin governor has been static for months. That could all change this week.
WI.summary: With all seven Democratic candidates certified for the Aug. 11 primary ballot, the state Democratic convention (June 13-14) is seen as a potential clarifying moment in the wide-open Wisconsin governor's race, as party leaders hope it narrows the field ahead of early voting starting in late July.

CO.title: As mail ballots arrive, here's how Colorado prepares for Election Day
CO.summary: Colorado's June 30 primary mail ballots are arriving in mailboxes, with election officials urging voters to return them early by mail or drop box as the state prepares Election Day logistics for its party primaries.

FL.title: Florida court allows use of new House districts drawn by Republicans for midterm elections
FL.summary: Florida's Supreme Court cleared the way for Republicans to use newly redrawn congressional maps in the 2026 midterm elections, rejecting a lower court challenge to the GOP-drawn districts.

ME.title: Graham Platner wins Maine primary election: Results and key takeaways
ME.summary: Democrat Graham Platner won Maine's U.S. Senate Democratic primary, while the governor's race between Janet Mills and Jared Golden is heading to ranked choice tabulation to determine which candidate advances.

MD.title: Early Voting Begins for Maryland Primary Election
MD.summary: Early in-person voting opened across Maryland for the June 23 gubernatorial primary, with polls open through June 19 at voting centers statewide; absentee ballot requests are due by June 17.

NY.title: 2026 Primary: Early voting starts Saturday. Who's on the ballot in Manhattan?
NY.summary: With New York's June 23 primary approaching and early voting starting June 13, the competitive NY-10 race between incumbent Dan Goldman and challenger Brad Lander heads a slate of contested congressional and local races across Manhattan.

OK.title: Early voting begins in Oklahoma today, here's what you need to know
OK.summary: In-person early voting opened in Oklahoma for the June 16 primary election, running June 11-13 at county election boards; voters must bring photo ID and no excuse is needed to vote early.

SC.title: Evette, Wilson trade barbs; Johnson moving on as SC governor field narrows
SC.summary: Pamela Evette and Alan Wilson are exchanging sharp attacks heading into South Carolina's June 23 Republican governor runoff while others from the primary field announce their next steps after not advancing.

AK.title: Alaska election official threatens to disqualify challenger Dan J. Sullivan in race against Sen. Dan Sullivan
AK.summary: Alaska's Division of Elections issued a preliminary decision that namesake Senate challenger Dan J. Sullivan of Petersburg is not eligible for the August primary ballot due to a party affiliation discrepancy; the challenger is contesting the ruling.

AK.title: In preliminary decision, state says namesake challenger to Sen. Dan Sullivan is not eligible to run
AK.summary: Alaska's Division of Elections director wrote to Dan J. Sullivan of Petersburg concluding that evidence does not support his eligibility for U.S. Senate, citing his registration as 'undeclared' at the time he declared as a Republican candidate.

AK.title: Dan Sullivan of Petersburg defends run for Alaska's U.S. Senate against state investigation
AK.summary: The Petersburg-based Senate candidate formally responded to Alaska's eligibility challenge on June 11, calling it an affront to his rights and denying any coordination with the Peltola campaign.

AK.title: Alaska election official threatens to disqualify Republican who shares name with Sen. Dan Sullivan
AK.summary: Alaska's election director warned Dan J. Sullivan that he may be removed from the August 18 Senate primary ballot, with incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan and national Republican groups accusing the challenger of being a sham candidate.

AL.title: Secretary of State Wes Allen Reminds Alabamians of Absentee Voting Deadlines Ahead of June 2026 Primary Runoff Election
AL.summary: Alabama's Secretary of State reminded voters that June 11 was the final day to hand-deliver absentee ballot applications ahead of the June 16 primary runoff, with no early in-person voting offered in Alabama.

AZ.title: Key dates and essential information for Arizona's Primary Election
AZ.summary: Arizona Public Media published a comprehensive voter guide for the July 21 primary, covering the June 22 voter registration deadline, June 24 early voting start date, and the new law permanently shifting Arizona primaries to the second-to-last Tuesday in July.

DC.title: Ranked choice voting will delay DC primary results
DC.summary: DC election officials warn that the District's first use of ranked-choice voting in the June 16 primary will delay final results until at least June 21 for the first tabulation round, with a final count expected no earlier than June 26 due to mail ballot receipt windows.

DC.title: Understanding ranked choice voting ahead of its DC debut in June primary
DC.summary: WTOP explains DC's newly adopted ranked-choice voting system for the June 16 primary: voters may rank up to five candidates for mayor, council, attorney general, and delegate to Congress, with votes redistributed in rounds until a candidate exceeds 50 percent.

DC.title: In their own words: Meet the DC candidates
DC.summary: As early voting enters its final days before the June 16 DC primary, WTOP profiles all candidates running in the District's first ranked-choice election, covering seven Democratic mayoral candidates and contested council and congressional seats.

FL.title: Florida Supreme Court lets new congressional map stand for 2026 elections
FL.summary: Following the Florida Supreme Court's June 10 ruling, the GOP-drawn congressional redistricting map that voting rights groups allege violates the state's anti-gerrymandering amendment will remain in effect for the November 2026 elections.

GA.title: Early voting underway for June 16 runoff election in Georgia
GA.summary: Fox 5 Atlanta reports early voting is active across Georgia through June 12 ahead of the June 16 runoff, where Republican voters will finalize their nominees for governor and Senate and Democrats will choose statewide candidates including secretary of state.

GA.title: Early voting begins in the 2026 Georgia primary runoffs
GA.summary: 13WMAZ provides a guide to Georgia's primary runoff early voting locations and ballot contents, with races for governor, U.S. Senate, and multiple other statewide offices heading to a second round of voting on June 16.

IA.title: Josh Turek's victory boosts Democratic hopes in Iowa Senate race
IA.summary: Following his June 2 primary win over state Sen. Zach Wahls, Democrat Josh Turek is energizing national Democratic hopes of flipping Iowa's open U.S. Senate seat, with the Cook Political Report shifting its rating from 'likely Republican' to 'lean Republican' and the Senate Majority PAC reserving $13.4 million in Iowa advertising.

KS.title: Kansas political battles await after 5 Republicans decline to seek reelection to Board of Education
KS.summary: With five Republican Kansas State Board of Education incumbents stepping aside, contested Republican primaries are expected in three of five open districts on August 4, potentially reshuffling partisan control of the board that could affect education and curriculum policy for years.

KY.title: Kentucky General Election 2026: A timeline
KY.summary: Forward Kentucky outlines Kentucky's November general election matchups set after the May 19 primaries, including the high-profile Senate race between Republican Andy Barr and Democrat Charles Booker for the seat being vacated by Sen. Mitch McConnell.

LA.title: Early voting starts for June 27 party runoffs
LA.summary: Early voting opened June 12 across Louisiana for the June 27 U.S. Senate party runoffs, with Republican Julia Letlow facing John Fleming and Democrat Jamie Davis facing Gary Crockett; polls are open 8:30 a.m. to 6 p.m. through June 20 excluding Sundays and Juneteenth.

LA.title: Early voting begins Friday for Senate race, other elections
LA.summary: Louisiana early voting began June 12 for the June 27 U.S. Senate runoffs; the Republican contest pits Julia Letlow against John Fleming while the Democratic contest features Jamie Davis against Gary Crockett for the seat vacated by Sen. Bill Cassidy.

LA.title: Gary Crockett, Jamie Davis poised to face off in U.S. Senate Democratic runoff
LA.summary: Gary Crockett and Jamie Davis qualified for Louisiana's June 27 Democratic U.S. Senate primary runoff after both fell short of a majority in the May 16 primary; the Democratic winner faces the Republican nominee in November for the seat held by Sen. Bill Cassidy.

MD.title: State election officials ask judge to block access to sensitive voter records
MD.summary: Maryland election officials argued in federal court that the DOJ should not receive an unredacted voter file containing personal data on 4.2 million registered voters, as the Trump administration's civil rights investigation tied to the earlier mail-ballot printing error pressed forward ahead of the June 23 primary.

MD.title: Early voting begins as DOJ investigates Maryland mail-in ballot mishap
MD.summary: Maryland's in-person early voting for the June 23 gubernatorial primary began June 11, even as the DOJ's civil rights investigation into a vendor error that sent incorrect party ballots to roughly 500,000 mail-in voters continued, with officials urging affected voters to use replacement ballots.

ME.title: Maine confirms ranked-choice recount as armed police secure locked 2026 primary ballots
ME.summary: Armed police transported sealed ballot boxes from across Maine to Augusta's Public Safety Building on June 11 ahead of the ranked choice tabulation starting June 12, with results in both gubernatorial primaries and the Democratic 2nd Congressional District primary expected by June 19.

MN.title: Minnesota Chippewa Tribe general election results are in
MN.summary: The six member nations of the Minnesota Chippewa Tribe held general elections on June 9 for tribal council leadership positions, with six incumbents ousted by challengers; results were reported June 11, 2026.

MO.title: Missouri Realtors spend $2 million to fight Amendment 4 limits on citizen initiative petitions
MO.summary: The Missouri Association of Realtors donated $2 million to Missourians for Fair Governance to oppose Amendment 4, which would require citizen-led constitutional amendments to win a majority in each of Missouri's eight congressional districts; the measure is on the August 4, 2026 primary ballot.

MS.title: Democratic super PAC investing $2M on Colom's challenge of Hyde-Smith, part of $50M national effort
MS.summary: American Bridge 21st Century announced it will spend $2 million on Mississippi's U.S. Senate race, backing Democrat Scott Colom's challenge to incumbent Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, part of a $50 million national campaign targeting 20 key House and Senate races.

MT.title: Montana GOP legislative primaries are over. What's next?
MT.summary: After millions of dollars in PAC spending, Montana's Republican legislative primaries concluded with both hardliner and centrist GOP factions winning roughly equal numbers of races, shaping the Republican caucus heading into the November general election.

NC.title: State elections board issues guidance on voter drives, mailings ahead of midterms
NC.summary: The NC State Board of Elections issued guidance on how voters should handle unsolicited third-party voter registration mailings, as roughly 370,000 mailers were being sent statewide by voter registration groups ahead of the November general election.

NC.title: NC Board of Elections discusses updating 2 photo ID rules
NC.summary: The North Carolina Board of Elections held a June 9 public hearing on proposed amendments to photo ID rules for in-person and absentee voting, including a controversial change shifting the provisional ballot rejection standard from a unanimous county board vote to a simple majority.

ND.title: North Dakota Republican leaders urge 'soul-searching' after contentious primary
ND.summary: Following the June 9 primary in which none of the NDGOP-endorsed statewide candidates won, North Dakota Republican leaders including the governor publicly called for party introspection, with the governor suggesting the state party failed to adequately support its endorsed candidates.

NE.title: Advocates end Nebraska property tax, winner-take-all, hand-count ballots petition effort
NE.summary: Advocates For All Nebraskans ended their 2026 petition campaign that had sought ballot measures requiring hand-counted paper ballots and winner-take-all Electoral College allocation, among others, after falling short of the required signature thresholds.

NE.title: Dan Osborn's Senate campaign submits 12,700 petition signatures, all but confirming a place on Nebraska's general election ballot
NE.summary: Independent U.S. Senate candidate Dan Osborn submitted 12,700 petition signatures — more than three times the 4,000 required — to confirm his place on Nebraska's November general election ballot against Republican incumbent Pete Ricketts.

NH.title: 2026 Candidate Filing Update: Who's in? Who's Out?
NH.summary: NH Journal tracked New Hampshire candidate filings ahead of the June 12 deadline, with former Sen. John Sununu expected to formalize his Republican U.S. Senate bid and Rep. Chris Pappas having filed as a Democrat to succeed retiring Sen. Jeanne Shaheen.

NJ.title: 2026 Primary Results: US House of Representatives
NJ.summary: NJ Spotlight News published a full recap of New Jersey's June 2 U.S. House primary results ahead of the June 12 county canvass certification, covering all 12 congressional districts including competitive contests in the 3rd, 7th, and 12th districts.

NM.title: The race is set: Deb Haaland to face off against Gregg Hull in New Mexico's open contest for governor
NM.summary: Following the June 2 primary, former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland (D) and former Rio Rancho Mayor Gregg Hull (R) are confirmed as the nominees for New Mexico governor; Haaland enters as the favorite and could become the first Native American woman elected governor.

NV.title: Nevada election officials report thousands of mail ballots still uncounted as primary tabulation continues
NV.summary: Two days after Nevada's June 9 primary, Clark and Washoe counties still had thousands of mail ballots to process; Washoe tabulated only 80% of mail ballots with 9,468 remaining, the statewide signature cure deadline is June 15, and the canvass must finish by June 18.

NV.title: Nevada updates primary ballot count as counties process remaining mail ballots, cures
NV.summary: Nevada's Secretary of State released an update on post-primary ballot processing, noting counties must accept mail ballots postmarked by Election Day through 5 p.m. Saturday; all results remain unofficial until the canvass completes on or before June 18.

OH.title: Ohio Republican lawmakers send constitutional amendment requiring voter photo ID to ballot
OH.summary: Ohio's Republican-controlled House passed Senate Joint Resolution 10 by 61-27, sending a constitutional amendment to enshrine a photo ID voting requirement to the November ballot; while Ohio law already requires photo ID by statute, this would add the requirement to the state constitution.

OH.title: Ohio voters will decide voter ID constitutional amendment
OH.summary: Ohioans will vote in November on a constitutional amendment requiring photo ID to vote; acceptable forms include driver's licenses, state IDs, passports, military IDs, and VA-issued IDs, with provisional ballot options for voters who cannot present ID at the polls.

OH.title: How changes to Ohio's voting laws affected the May 2026 election
OH.summary: A post-election review of how Senate Bill 293 — which eliminated the four-day post-Election Day mail ballot grace period and required more frequent voter-roll database verification — affected Ohio's May 2026 primary, the first election conducted under the new rules.

PA.title: Democratic registration drops in key midterm districts
PA.summary: An analysis found Democrats lost more than 275,000 registered voters across 28 congressional battleground districts since November 2024, with Pennsylvania's 1st, 7th, 8th, and 10th districts among those affected; the steepest declines were in PA-8, held by Republican Rep. Rob Bresnahan.

RI.title: Rhode Island lawmakers move at lightning speed on last night of session
RI.summary: On the final night of Rhode Island's 2026 legislative session, lawmakers rushed through numerous bills while the Rhode Island Voting Rights Act — which would have protected minority voters from ballot suppression and racial gerrymandering — was notably absent, confirming it was deferred to the 2027 session.

SD.title: Q&A: What to know about South Dakota's first gubernatorial runoff
SD.summary: South Dakota will hold its first-ever gubernatorial runoff on July 28 between Toby Doeden and Gov. Larry Rhoden after neither cleared the 35% primary threshold on June 2; absentee voting opens June 12 and the voter registration deadline for the runoff is July 13.

SD.title: Absentee voting for Republican gubernatorial runoff election opens on June 12
SD.summary: Ahead of South Dakota's historic first gubernatorial runoff on July 28, absentee voting opens June 12; voters who requested absentee ballots for the primary will automatically receive runoff ballots, while others must submit applications by July 27.

SD.title: What to know about SD's first gubernatorial runoff
SD.summary: An explainer on South Dakota's unprecedented first gubernatorial runoff between Toby Doeden (31%) and Gov. Larry Rhoden (25%), covering eligibility, key dates, and how the 35% runoff threshold triggered this historic election for the first time in state history.

TN.title: NAACP files for federal court injunction to stop new Tennessee congressional map
TN.summary: The NAACP, Lawyers' Committee for Civil Rights Under Law, and LDF filed a motion for a federal preliminary injunction to block Tennessee's redrawn congressional map, arguing it violates the 14th and 15th Amendments by splitting Memphis into three districts to eliminate the state's only majority-Black district and dilute Black voting power ahead of the 2026 elections.

UT.title: Can a progressive beat Ben McAdams? That's the big question in Utah Democrats' 1st District primary
UT.summary: With Utah's June 23 primary approaching and mail ballots already arriving, the article examines whether Ben McAdams — the last Utah Democrat to serve in Congress — can hold off progressive challengers in the new Democratic-leaning 1st Congressional District created by court-ordered redistricting.

UT.title: Utah primary elections: Why haven't I received a mail-in ballot?
UT.summary: Explains why some Utah voters may not have received mail-in primary ballots ahead of June 23, noting the voter registration deadline is June 12 for mail ballots, that unaffiliated voters must request a partisan ballot, and that a new state rule requires mail ballots to be physically received by 8 p.m. on Election Day rather than merely postmarked.

UT.title: Deadline looms for Utahns to request mail-in primary election ballot
UT.summary: Reports that Utah voters have until 5 p.m. on June 12 to register and receive a mail-in ballot for the June 23 primary, with early in-person voting already underway since June 9; unaffiliated voters must specifically request a Democratic or Republican primary ballot.

WA.title: Petition campaign to repeal Washington income tax may break records
WA.summary: Reports that Let's Go Washington has gathered over 242,699 signatures toward the 308,911 needed by July 2 to place Initiative IP26-645 on the fall ballot; the measure would repeal Washington's new 9.9% income tax on household income above $1 million, and the campaign is on pace to break state signature collection records.

WI.title: USPS ballot rule could affect state absentee voting
WI.summary: A proposed U.S. Postal Service rule would require states to share voter names and barcodes for all absentee voters or risk having mail-in ballots denied delivery; Wisconsin election officials warn this could delay ballots in rural areas where USPS facilities lack the required scanning equipment.

WI.title: Elections Commission grants ballot access to 7th CD candidates
WI.summary: The Wisconsin Elections Commission on June 11 finalized the August primary ballot by rejecting signature challenges against candidates in the crowded 7th Congressional District race to replace Rep. Tom Tiffany, clearing Democrat Fred Clark and Republicans Michael Alfonso and Kevin Hermening.

WV.title: All 55 counties certify Primary Election results as voter participation review planned
WV.summary: West Virginia Secretary of State Kris Warner announced all 55 counties have certified the May 12 primary results, reporting 21.02% voter turnout (252,008 of 1,198,934 registered voters), with early voting participation up over 8% from the 2022 midterm primary; a comprehensive voter participation report is expected this summer.

WY.title: Election Q&A: Betsy Erickson for Wyoming House District 37
WY.summary: A candidate Q&A with Betsy Erickson, a Republican running for Wyoming House District 37 in the August 18 primary, covering her policy positions; part of Oil City News's series interviewing 2026 election candidates ahead of Wyoming's primary.

AL.title: DECISION 2026: Races, sample ballots for runoff election set for June 16
AL.summary: Covers the races and sample ballots for Alabama's June 16 primary runoff election, including the contested U.S. Senate Republican runoff between Rep. Barry Moore and former Navy SEAL Jared Hudson.

AL.title: AP Decision Notes: What to expect in Alabama's state primary runoff
AL.summary: AP analysis previewing Alabama's June 16 primary runoff, covering the Republican U.S. Senate race between Rep. Barry Moore (with Trump's endorsement) and former Navy SEAL Jared Hudson, plus the Democratic Senate runoff.

AK.title: Alaska Division of Elections says Petersburg Sullivan is likely ineligible to run for U.S. Senate
AK.summary: Alaska's Division of Elections issued a preliminary ruling that Dan J. Sullivan of Petersburg is likely ineligible to appear on the U.S. Senate ballot, finding his same-name candidacy against incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan could be misleading to voters under state election law.

AK.title: Two Dan Sullivans: Petersburg candidate poised for removal from ballot by state
AK.summary: Reports on the Alaska election official's move to remove challenger Dan J. Sullivan of Petersburg from the U.S. Senate ballot, with details on the candidate's response and the preliminary nature of the disqualification decision.

AR.title: Where to sign direct democracy and education rights petitions in Central Arkansas this weekend
AR.summary: Reports on petition signature drives in Central Arkansas for the Arkansas Ballot Measure Rights Amendment, which would reverse legislative restrictions on the citizen initiative process, with canvassers racing toward a July 3 deadline to qualify for the November 2026 ballot.

AZ.title: Arizona ballot measure to change voting rules will be decided in 2026 election
AZ.summary: Arizona Republicans placed a November ballot referendum requiring mail voters to show ID, prohibiting foreign campaign contributions, and allowing early voters to have ballots counted faster — provisions that bypass Gov. Hobbs's repeated vetoes of similar election legislation.

DC.title: D.C. to hold first election using ranked-choice voting on June 16
DC.summary: Washington D.C. will use ranked-choice voting for the first time in its June 16 primary, allowing voters to rank up to five candidates for mayor, delegate to Congress, attorney general, and council seats under Initiative 83 approved by DC voters in 2024.

DE.title: Sen. Chris Coons announces his bid for a fourth term in the U.S. Senate
DE.summary: Delaware's two-term U.S. Senator Chris Coons officially launched his reelection campaign, seeking a fourth term ahead of the September 15 Democratic primary, running on an Opportunity, Security, and Justice platform with endorsements from the state's top Democratic officials.

GA.title: AP Decision Notes: What to expect in Georgia's state primary runoff
GA.summary: The Associated Press previews Georgia's June 16 primary runoff in which Republicans choose nominees for governor (Lt. Gov. Burt Jones vs. Rick Jackson) and U.S. Senate (Rep. Mike Collins vs. Derek Dooley), with winners advancing to November against Democratic nominees including Keisha Lance Bottoms.

IA.title: Iowa enacts five election bills in 2026, including prohibition on foreign donations in ballot measure elections
IA.summary: Iowa's governor signed five election-related bills including measures eliminating voter attestation for voters without acceptable ID, banning foreign contributions in ballot measure elections, requiring annual citizenship verification for voter rolls, and prohibiting satellite absentee voting stations on school property during school elections.

IL.title: Darren Bailey targets Pritzker's possible presidential ambitions in Illinois governor's race
IL.summary: Republican Darren Bailey is targeting incumbent Governor JB Pritzker's reported 2028 presidential ambitions as a key attack line in their November 2026 rematch for the Illinois governor's seat, with both candidates having won their respective primaries in March 2026.

IN.title: Beau Bayh says public service 'in his blood' as he runs for Indiana secretary of state
IN.summary: Democratic Secretary of State nominee Beau Bayh discusses his candidacy against Republican incumbent Diego Morales in the November election that will determine who oversees Indiana's elections, after winning his party's June 6 convention nomination.

KS.title: Johnson County faces backlash after cutting 8 early voting sites before primary election
KS.summary: Johnson County, Kansas removed 8 early in-person voting sites ahead of the August 4 primary election, drawing criticism from community organizers and elected officials who said the decision was made without public input or transparency.

LA.title: Early voting begins across Louisiana for party primary runoff election
LA.summary: Early voting got underway across Louisiana parishes for the June 27 party runoffs, including the Republican U.S. Senate runoff between Rep. Julia Letlow and State Treasurer John Fleming and a Democratic runoff between Gary Crockett and Jamie Davis.

MA.title: 3 takeaways from our interview with Gov. Maura Healey
MA.summary: Massachusetts Gov. Maura Healey said she will not endorse either candidate in the Democratic Senate primary between incumbent Sen. Ed Markey and challenger Rep. Seth Moulton ahead of the September 1 primary, staying neutral in one of the state's most closely watched election contests.

ME.title: Where Maine's elections stand going into a ranked-choice count
ME.summary: With no candidate winning a majority in the June 9 Democratic and Republican gubernatorial primaries or the Democratic CD-2 primary, Maine's ranked-choice voting tabulation process began June 12 at the Secretary of State's office in Augusta.

ME.title: With ranked-choice tabulations underway, here's what you need to know
ME.summary: Maine's Secretary of State is conducting ranked-choice voting tabulations for three races from the June 9 primary — the Democratic and Republican gubernatorial primaries and the Democratic primary for the 2nd Congressional District — a process open to the public and livestreamed.

MI.title: Michigan suspends Antrim County clerk's voter roll privileges
MI.summary: Michigan's Bureau of Elections revoked Antrim County Clerk Victoria Bishop's access to the state's central voter database after she made unauthorized changes and cancellations to voter registrations, the latest escalation in a months-long dispute affecting roughly 1,800 registered voters.

MI.title: Michigan revokes Antrim County clerk's access to voter roll after unauthorized cancellations
MI.summary: Michigan's director of elections formally notified Antrim County Clerk Victoria Bishop that her Qualified Voter File access was revoked after she changed or canceled voter registrations outside her legal authority, sending notices to roughly 1,800 voters — about 8% of the county's registered electorate.

MO.title: Missouri courts keep rewriting ballot language as fights over direct democracy intensify
MO.summary: Courts have repeatedly overruled Secretary of State Denny Hoskins' ballot summaries — five times in his tenure — including for the redistricting referendum, finding the language unfair or misleading, shaping how Missouri voters will weigh in on election-related measures in 2026.

MO.title: Missouri courts keep rewriting 'unfair' ballot language as fights over direct democracy intensify
