MO.summary: KCUR's coverage of the ongoing legal dispute in which Missouri courts have repeatedly rewritten Secretary of State Hoskins' ballot descriptions for measures including the redistricting referendum, raising concerns about fair voter access to accurate ballot information ahead of the August 4 primary.

NC.title: GOP groups claim victory in dispute over NC 'never resident' voters
NC.summary: A Wake County Superior Court judge ruled that U.S. citizens born overseas to North Carolina parents who never actually lived in the state cannot register or vote in any North Carolina election, a significant change to voter eligibility rules.

NC.title: Judge confirms GOP victory in voting dispute over 'never residents'
NC.summary: A North Carolina judge formally confirmed the ruling barring 'never resident' overseas voters from casting ballots in state and federal elections, affecting overseas military-adjacent families whose parents last lived in North Carolina but who themselves never established residency there.

ND.title: Prevailing PSC candidates say campaign work not done with Dem opponents on horizon
ND.summary: Republican candidates who won North Dakota's June 9 Public Service Commission primary races are looking ahead to November matchups against Democratic opponents, in a state where Democrats are contesting all major statewide races for the first time since 2020.

NE.title: Second former Nebraska lawmaker mulling nonpartisan run, including for secretary of state
NE.summary: Former state Sen. Bob Krist is considering a nonpartisan candidacy for Nebraska secretary of state, which could reshape the November contest between Republican Scott Petersen — who upset incumbent Bob Evnen in the primary — and Democrat Sarah Slattery in a race that will determine who oversees Nebraska's elections.

NH.title: 2026 NH elections to watch: Governor, US and state Senate, House fields are set
NH.summary: With New Hampshire's June 12 candidate filing deadline closed, the fields for the September 8 primary are set across all major races — including an open U.S. Senate seat, governor, both U.S. House seats, the Executive Council, and the state legislature.

NV.title: Who voted in Nevada's 2026 primary? Turnout up slightly, still about 20%
NV.summary: Following Nevada's June 9 primary, overall voter turnout came in around 20% — slightly above 2024 — with mail ballots accounting for about 60% of votes cast and roughly 46,000 more Nevadans voting than in the prior primary cycle.

NY.title: Early Voting Underway in New York for June Primaries
NY.summary: Early voting began June 13 for New York's June 23 primary election, with over 16,000 ballots cast in New York City alone on the first day; competitive races include NY-10 (Goldman vs. Lander) and a contested state comptroller primary.

OH.title: Ohio voters to decide voter ID amendment in November, one of five voter ID ballot measures in 2026
OH.summary: Ohio lawmakers advanced a constitutional amendment requiring photo ID for both in-person and absentee voting to the November 2026 ballot, while also passing a separate bill requiring absentee voters to submit a copy of their photo ID starting in 2027.

OK.title: State Election Board Offers Tips and Reminders Ahead of June 16 Primary
OK.summary: Oklahoma's State Election Board reminded voters of requirements for the June 16 primary: closed party primaries, mandatory photo ID, and early voting open June 11-13; over 635 positions are on the ballot including governor, U.S. Senate, and State Question 832 on raising the minimum wage.

OK.title: Oklahoma Voice launches voter guide ahead of June 16 primary election
OK.summary: Oklahoma Voice released a comprehensive voter guide for the June 16 primary covering all statewide and federal candidates, including 9 Republican gubernatorial candidates, the open U.S. Senate race, and State Question 832 on raising the minimum wage to $15 per hour.

PA.title: Democratic registration drops in key midterm districts
PA.summary: Democrats lost more than 275,000 registered voters across 28 competitive congressional districts from November 2024 to May 2026, including Pennsylvania swing districts, a trend with potential implications for Democratic competitiveness in the November 2026 elections.

RI.title: TGIF: Ian Donnis' Rhode Island politics roundup for June 12, 2026
RI.summary: The weekly Rhode Island politics roundup covers the close of the legislative session with the Rhode Island Voting Rights Act failing to advance to a floor vote, and previews the September 9 Democratic gubernatorial primary between incumbent Dan McKee and challenger Helena Foulkes.

SC.title: Democratic Party runoff in 1st Congressional District may go without debate before June 23
SC.summary: Mac Deford accepted a debate invitation from two Lowcountry TV stations while fellow Democratic runoff candidate Nancy Lacore declined, potentially leaving South Carolina's 1st Congressional District June 23 runoff without a head-to-head forum before voters decide.

SD.title: Early voting begins in South Dakota governor runoff
SD.summary: Early in-person voting opened for South Dakota's historic first gubernatorial runoff between Republican Gov. Larry Rhoden and businessman Toby Doeden, after neither cleared the 35% threshold in the June 2 primary; the runoff is scheduled for July 28.

TX.title: Election results: June 13 North Texas runoff
TX.summary: Voters across North Texas returned to the polls on June 13 for local municipal runoffs resulting from the May 2 Uniform Election Date, including races for mayoral and city council positions across the region.

TX.title: Terry Lynne leads Jaime Rivas by 25 votes in razor-thin Farmers Branch mayoral runoff, unofficial returns show
TX.summary: Incumbent Mayor Terry Lynne narrowly edged Jaime Rivas by just 25 votes (50.32% to 49.7%) in the June 13 Farmers Branch mayoral runoff, one of the tightest local races in Texas's June 13 runoff elections.

UT.title: 2026 primary elections in Northern Utah: candidate profiles for Weber, Davis counties
UT.summary: Candidate profiles for competitive Weber and Davis county races ahead of Utah's June 23 primary election, where mail-in ballots were mailed June 2 and must be received by 8 p.m. on Election Day under a new state law tightening mail ballot deadlines.

WI.title: Democrats make their pitch for governor at annual state convention
WI.summary: All seven Democratic candidates for Wisconsin governor spoke at the WisDems Convention in Madison, making their cases to succeed term-limited Gov. Tony Evers ahead of the August 11 primary.

WI.title: Wisconsin Democrats make their case in crowded governor primary
WI.summary: Seven Democratic governor candidates pitched voters on affordability and beating the Republican nominee at Wisconsin's Democratic Party annual state convention, with the August 11 primary approaching.
